entry.summary: A comprehensive survey of Federated Continual Learning, situated at the intersection of federated learning and continual learning, addressing privacy-preserving lifelong learning over distributed, non-stationary data. It covers catastrophic forgetting, communication, and client heterogeneity in real-world domains.

entry.title: Model-Based and Data-Driven Hierarchical Control and Topology Co-Design for Robust Networked Systems

author.name: Shirantha Welikala, Zihao Song, Hai Lin, Panos J. Antsaklis

entry.summary: This paper proposes hierarchical control and interconnection-topology co-design for networked linear systems using dissipativity theory, with both model-based and data-driven variants solved via linear matrix inequalities. It ensures robust global dissipativity from local guarantees.

entry.title: Multi-View In-Cabin Monitoring System for Public Transport Vehicles

author.name: Evgeny Gorelik, Kenny Dean Karrow, Fikret Sivrikaya, Sahin Albayrak, Christian Baumann

entry.summary: This paper releases a multi-view in-cabin monitoring dataset for public transport with synchronized RGB-D from four cameras and rotating LiDAR over a digitalized city bus, plus calibration, pseudo-labeling, and nuScenes-format benchmarks. It supports multi-view 3D perception of vehicle occupants.

entry.title: Agents All the Way Down; A Methodology for Building Custom AI Agents from Substrate to Production

author.name: Marc Alier Forment, Juanan Pereira, Francisco Jos\'e Garc\'ia-Pe\~nalvo, Mar\'ia Jos\'e Casa\~n Guerrero

entry.summary: This paper codifies a methodology, Agents All the Way Down, for building custom AI agents end to end from substrate to production, chaining function-calling APIs, the Model Context Protocol, and code agents into two preconditions and three repeated practices. It writes down practitioner knowledge currently scattered across blogs and system prompts.

entry.title: Time-Series Foundation Model Embeddings for Remaining Useful Life Estimation

author.name: Amir El-Ghoussani, Michele De Vita, Ronald Naumann, Valiseios Belagiannis

entry.summary: The authors use a frozen Chronos-2 time-series foundation model plus a small regression head to predict Remaining Useful Life for industrial predictive maintenance from sensor streams. This lightweight approach avoids heavy feature engineering and large labeled datasets while improving accuracy.

entry.title: Using Explainability as a Training-Time Reliability Signal for Efficient ECG Classification

author.name: Veerendhra Kumar Dangeti, Xiao Gu, Ying Weng, Shreyank N Gowda

entry.summary: ERTS uses explanation quality as a training-time reliability signal for efficient ECG classification, improving on Progressive Data Dropout which relies on model confidence and may retain noisy samples. It aims to reduce training cost in resource-limited healthcare settings.

entry.title: What Uncertainties Do We Need for Dynamical Systems?

author.name: Yusuf Sale, Christopher B\"ulte, Felix Czaja, Joshua Stiller, Eyke H\"ullermeier

entry.summary: This is a perspective paper examining what kinds of uncertainty (aleatoric versus epistemic) are needed for dynamical systems, an area less studied than supervised learning. It clarifies sources of uncertainty and how representation goals vary across tasks.

entry.title: Finding Multiple Interpretations in Datasets

author.name: Matthew Chak, Paul Anderson

entry.summary: This work proposes a method to find sets of similar-performing models that have highly different context-aware characteristics, demonstrated on the METABRIC gene-expression dataset. It addresses the Rashomon-effect issue of multiple valid interpretations without performance penalties.

entry.title: DroneShield-AI: A Multi-Modal Sensor Fusion Framework for Real-Time Autonomous Drone Threat Detection, Behavioral Intent Classification, and Swarm Intelligence in Contested Airspace

author.name: Marius Bayizere

entry.summary: DroneShield-AI is a unified open framework integrating six layers (RF, acoustic, visual YOLOv8 detection, sensor fusion, behavioral intent classification, and GNN swarm intelligence) for autonomous drone threat detection. It introduces a six-class threat taxonomy and graph-attention-based formation analysis.

entry.title: Beyond Dark Knowledge: Mixup-Based Distillation for Reliable Predictions

author.name: Jos\'e Medina, Paul Honeine, Abdelaziz Bensrhair, Amnir Hadachi

entry.summary: This paper analyzes the interaction between knowledge distillation and mixup when mixup is applied only during student training, showing the teacher's signal becomes dominated by distributional confusion on unseen vicinal inputs. Despite this mismatch, the student still gains reliable predictions, which the authors characterize.

entry.title: MLT-Dedup: Efficient Large-Scale Online Video Deduplication via Multi-Level Representations and Spatial-Temporal Matching

author.name: David Yuchen Wang, Haoying Li, Hailun Xu, Wei Chee Yew, Zirui Zhu, Sanjay Saha, Hao Hei, Kanchan Sarkar, Kun Xu

entry.summary: MLT-Dedup is a large-scale online video deduplication framework using multi-level representations and spatial-temporal matching to retrieve near-duplicate videos under a limited index budget. It targets the efficiency-precision trade-off in detecting partially edited duplicates on platforms.

entry.title: EverydayGPT: Confidence-Gated Routing for Efficient and Safe Hybrid GPT-RAG Conversational QA

author.name: Jaspreet Singh Nahal

entry.summary: EverydayGPT uses confidence-gated routing to decide between fast RAG extraction and a costly small GPT pathway, resolving 85% of queries via fast retrieval for over 120x latency reduction. The backbone is a 205M-parameter GPT trained from scratch on 10B tokens.

entry.title: A Resource for Enthymeme Detection in Controversial Political Discourse

author.name: Martial Pastor, Nelleke Oostdijk

entry.summary: This paper presents a resource of 1,482 politically controversial tweets annotated by five annotators for enthymemes (arguments with unstated premises/conclusions) and argument structure, deliberately preserving label variation. It anchors guidelines in Walton's argumentation schemes to study disagreement rather than eliminate it.

entry.title: DeceptionX: Explainable Deception Detection with Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Jiayu Zhang, Shuo Ye, Jiajian Huang, Yawen Cui, Taorui Wang, Wei Xia, Zeheng Wang, Haowen Tang, Hui Ma, Zitong Yu

entry.summary: Proposes DeceptionX, an MLLM framework that shifts deception detection from black-box classification to an interpretable Observe-Think-Summarize reasoning paradigm bridging low-level audiovisual cues and high-level logic. Aims to add interpretability to affective behavioral analysis.

entry.title: DepthMaster: Unified Monocular Depth Estimation for Perspective and Panoramic Images

author.name: Pengfei Wang, Shihao Wang, Liyi Chen, Zhiyuan Ma, Guowen Zhang, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces DepthMaster, a unified monocular metric depth estimation framework that handles both narrow field-of-view perspective images and 360-degree panoramas by reformulating the geometric discrepancy rather than using specialized networks. It addresses generalization and the scarcity of metric-annotated panoramic training data.

entry.title: KinematicRL: A Sim-to-Real Reinforcement Learning Framework For Social Navigation With Kinodynamic Feasibility

author.name: Zhiming Xu, Haodong Yang, Chengju Liu, Qijun Chen, Chenpeng Yao

entry.summary: Presents KinematicRL, a sim-to-real RL framework for social navigation that uses higher-order control inputs to reduce the sim-to-real gap, with theoretical analysis showing tracking error decays exponentially with control order. It produces dynamically feasible, kinodynamically valid navigation policies.

entry.title: Magnitude-Based Features for Multispecies Spatial Data

author.name: Julia Sollberger, Joshua Bull, Sara Kali\v{s}nik, Bernadette Stolz

entry.summary: Proposes magnitude-based features, derived from the mathematical invariant of magnitude of finite metric spaces, for analyzing multispecies spatial data such as tumor microenvironments and tissue microarrays. It develops both global and local magnitude feature vectors to capture spatial interactions.

entry.title: Anthropic did not call for a pause on AI

author.name: Andrea_Miotti

entry.summary: Argues that despite media framing, Anthropic's 'When AI builds itself' post and OpenAI's follow-up did not actually call for a pause or slowdown on AI, only vague language about wanting the option to slow down. It critiques companies' deliberately ambiguous messaging on self-improving AI risk.

entry.title: SkillJuror: Measuring How Agent Skill Organization Changes Runtime Behavior

author.name: Zhiyu Chen, Zihan Guo, Bo Huang, Bingwei Lu, Jianghao Lin, Yuanjian Zhou, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: SkillJuror evaluates how the organization of agent Skills (not just their content) changes runtime behavior, comparing Progressive Disclosure against a flat baseline while holding task knowledge fixed. An 82-task study shows organization shifts which resources agents touch before aggregate outcomes change.

entry.title: Embodied-BenchClaw: An Autonomous Multi-Agent System for Embodied Spatial Intelligence Benchmark Construction

author.name: Baoyang Jiang, Fengchun Zhang, Leyuan Wang, Haotian Li, Yida Wang, Zhe Ji, Jinshan Lai, Xi Ren, Jianwei Hu, Qiang Ma

entry.summary: Embodied-BenchClaw is an autonomous multi-agent system that automatically constructs continually updatable embodied spatial intelligence benchmarks from a user-specified intent via a five-stage pipeline. It aims to reduce the labor and saturation problems of static benchmarks.

entry.title: A Five-Plane Reference Architecture for Runtime Governance of Production AI Agents

author.name: Krti Tallam

entry.summary: Proposes a five-plane reference architecture for runtime governance of production AI agents, arguing that traditional data-boundary security fails when agents take sequences of individually-permitted actions on enterprise systems. It calls for stateful evaluation against composite principals.

entry.title: Designing AI-Supported Focus Groups: A Role x Modality Playbook

author.name: Zhiqing Wang, Steven Dow

entry.summary: This paper presents a Role x Modality playbook for AI-supported focus groups, mapping how generative AI can scaffold live qualitative research through prompting, turn regulation, thematic mapping, and summarization while preserving facilitation quality. It gives UX research teams a design framework for AI moderation.

entry.title: MSUE: Multi-Modal Soccer Understanding Expert

author.name: Litao Li, Yibo Yu, Yufeng Hu, Zhuo Yang, Jiali Wen, Yixin Chen, Yixi Zhou

entry.summary: This paper presents MSUE, a multi-expert VQA architecture for the 2026 SoccerNet challenge that dispatches questions to text, image, and video experts (Gemini3-Flash, fine-tuned Qwen3-VL, and a knowledge base). It achieves 0.95 accuracy on the benchmark with a VLM-driven data synthesis pipeline.

entry.title: Evaluating and Combating the Impact of Concept Drift on the Performance of Machine Learning-Based Phishing Detection Systems

author.name: Warren Fernando, Nikos Komninos

entry.summary: This work evaluates the impact of concept drift on machine-learning-based phishing/spam detection and proposes methods to combat performance degradation over time. It examines how evolving email patterns undermine deployed spam filters.

entry.title: PianoKontext: Expressive Performance Rendering from Deadpan Context

author.name: Dmitrii Gavrilev

entry.summary: PianoKontext is a flow-matching model for expressive piano performance rendering that generates variable-length performances in the latent space of a pretrained Music2Latent model. It uses dynamic time warping to construct paired deadpan-to-expressive training data.

entry.title: 3D-CBM: A Framework for Concept-Based Interpretability in Generative 3D Modeling

author.name: Ahmad Al-Kabbany

entry.summary: Introduces 3D-CBM, a framework integrating Concept Bottleneck Models into 3D generative architectures to provide intrinsic interpretability for point clouds and meshes. Targets trust and accountability in safety-critical 3D content creation.

entry.title: An Electric Potential-Augmented Benchmark Dataset for Physics-Guided Image Reconstruction of Electrical Capacitance Tomography

author.name: Xinqi Zhang, Qiming Ma, Lihui Peng

entry.summary: Introduces an electric-potential-augmented benchmark dataset for physics-guided image reconstruction in electrical capacitance tomography, generated via a COMSOL-MATLAB pipeline with 20,000 samples that explicitly include the electric potential field rather than treating the sensor as a black box. Aims to integrate latent physics into ECT deep learning.

entry.title: Bridging the Modality Gap in Forensic Image Retrieval

author.name: Ricardo Gonz\'alez-Gazapo, Annette Morales-Gonz\'alez, Yoanna Mart\'inez-D\'iaz, Heydi M\'endez-V\'azquez, Milton Garc\'ia-Borroto

entry.summary: Presents a unified retrieval framework for forensic image retrieval adapted to four tattoo-related tasks including image, text-description, and sketch queries, focusing on evaluating forensic applicability across real-world scenarios. Addresses the modality gap in forensic visual evidence comparison.

entry.title: XPR: An Extensible Cross-Platform Point-Based Differentiable Renderer

author.name: Steve Rhyner, Sankeerth Durvasula, Aleksandr Kovalev, Hansel Jia, Adrian Zhao, Mrutunjayya Mrutunjayya, Nilesh Ahuja, Selvakumar Panneer, Christina Giannoula, Nandita Vijaykumar

entry.summary: Presents XPR, an extensible cross-platform framework for point-based differentiable rendering with a high-level interface that separates method logic from the shared pipeline, enabling new methods in a few lines of code with automatic backward passes. It targets reproducibility and portability across hardware.

entry.title: Continuous biome representations from Earth observation embeddings

author.name: Maxwell B. Joseph (Planet Labs PBC), Fl\'avia De Souza Mendes (Planet Labs PBC), Dieu My T. Nguyen (Planet Labs PBC), Camile Sothe (Planet Labs PBC), Christopher B. Anderson (Planet Labs PBC)

entry.summary: Uses Earth observation foundation model embeddings (Clay v1.5) with a linear classifier to convert discrete biome maps into continuous probability representations that better capture ecological transition zones (ecotones). Evaluated on six Brazilian biomes with 1.3 million embeddings.

entry.title: Position: Hippocampal Explicit Memory Is the Cornerstone for AGI

author.name: Sangjun Park

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that integrating explicit, hippocampus-like memory is essential for advancing LLMs toward AGI, since current learning resembles human implicit memory but lacks the substrate for strategic planning and metacognition. It draws on neuroscience to specify computational requirements.

entry.title: When Do Data-Driven Systems Exhibit the Capability to Infer?

author.name: Maximilian Poretschkin, Tabea Naeven

entry.summary: Examines when data-driven systems exhibit the EU AI Act's defining capability to infer, focusing on the gray area of credit-scoring statistical models. Motivated by statistical learning theory, it develops criteria for whether such systems fall under the Act's AI definition.

entry.title: IntElicit: Eliciting and Assessing Contextualized Creativity via Dialogue Policy Optimization

author.name: Mingjia Li, Jin Wu, Hong Qian, Wenhao Huang, Yiyang Huang, Yiwen Zhang, Chanjin Zheng, Xiangfeng Wang, Aimin Zhou, Jiajun Guo

entry.summary: IntElicit is a framework that elicits and assesses contextualized creativity through dialogue policy optimization, acting as a constrained adaptive AI interviewer that disentangles creativity from confounding domain knowledge and engagement willingness. It provides non-directive scaffolds in multi-turn interaction.

entry.title: PROJECTMEM: A Local-First, Event-Sourced Memory and Judgment Layer for AI Coding Agents

author.name: Ripon Chandra Malo, Tong Qiu

entry.summary: PROJECTMEM is an open-source, local-first, event-sourced memory layer for AI coding agents that records development as an append-only log of typed events and projects it into compact context, reducing repeated context reconstruction and failed debugging attempts. It targets the statelessness of coding assistants.

entry.title: Quantized Stochastic Primal-Dual Methods for Distributed Optimization under Relaxed Global Geometry

author.name: Susmit Sarkar, Abhinav Raghuvanshi, Kushal Chakrabarti, Mayank Baranwal

entry.summary: Proposes q-PDGD, a quantized stochastic primal-dual method for distributed optimization with finite-bit communication, analyzed under relaxed global geometry (RSI and PL conditions). It provides linear-to-neighborhood and O(1/k) convergence guarantees matching centralized stochastic rates.

entry.title: The Dynamics of Human and AI-Generated Language: How Semantics Fluctuates across Different Timescales

author.name: Han-Jen Chang, Yasir \c{C}atal, Angelika Wolman, Agust\'in Ib\'a\~nez, David Smith, I-Wen Su, Kai-Yuan Cheng, Georg Northoff

entry.summary: Introduces a semantic-timescale analysis pipeline converting timestamped transcripts into semantic time-series using WordNet word depth and SBERT contextual similarity, with autocorrelation-window measures. It compares how generic versus specific content fluctuates over time in human versus AI-generated speech.

entry.title: Small Experiments, Cheaper Decisions: A Case Study in Staged Promotion for Micro-Pretraining

author.name: Felipe Chavarro Polania

entry.summary: Studies a staged-promotion protocol for micro-pretraining experiments across heterogeneous hardware, using budgets from 2 minutes to 12 hours with frozen promotion rules. It finds early short-run rankings are host-sensitive and over-promote configurations that only look strong at tiny budgets.

entry.title: Illumination-Robust Camera-Based Heart-Rate Estimation for Physiological Sensing in Robots

author.name: Zhi Wei Xu, Torbj\"orn E. M. Nordling

entry.summary: This paper presents an end-to-end spatial-temporal transformer for illumination-robust remote heart-rate estimation (rPPG) from RGB cameras for human-interacting robots, on a new varied-illumination dataset. It integrates 3D face alignment, illumination augmentation, and hybrid temporal-frequency supervision.

entry.title: NARRAS: Edge-Triggered Distributed Inference for CSI-Based Localization in Vehicular IoT Networks

author.name: Rodrigo Oliver, Ricardo Vazquez Alvarez, Alejandro Lancho, Stefano Rini

entry.summary: NARRAS introduces edge-triggered distributed inference for CSI-based localization in vehicular IoT, where each antenna array decides locally whether its observation is worth transmitting under an uplink budget. It frames a broader class of task-oriented communication problems where devices share a constrained channel.

entry.title: Semantic Grading of Written Answers in Low-Resource Language Bangla Using a Fine-Tuned Lightweight Language Model

author.name: Meherun Farzana, Aniket Joarder, Mahmudul Hasan, Md. Mosaddek Khan

entry.summary: This work builds a bilingual Bangla-English semantic grading system for low-resource educational settings, fine-tuning a lightweight LM to score short written answers using question, reference, and student answer while prioritizing semantic correctness over lexical overlap. It addresses the lack of qualified graders in remote regions.

entry.title: PT-WNO: Point Transformer with Wavelet Neural Operator for 3D Point Cloud Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Nhut Le, Maryam Rahnemoonfar

entry.summary: Proposes PT-WNO, combining a point transformer with a wavelet neural operator to inject learnable global context into point cloud semantic segmentation beyond standard skip connections. Aims for richer scene-level understanding.

entry.title: Scene-Adaptive Nonlinear Tone Curves for Pseudo Ground-Truth Generation in Low-Light 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Mingzhe Lyu, Jinqiang Cui, Hong Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a scene-adaptive nonlinear tone-curve method for generating pseudo ground-truth images in low-light 3D Gaussian Splatting, replacing uniform linear gain that clips bright regions. Improves reconstruction quality for low-light novel view synthesis.

entry.title: DrivingAgent: Design and Scheduling Agents for Autonomous Driving Systems

author.name: Zhongyu Xia, Wenhao Chen, Yongtao Wang, Ming-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: Presents DrivingAgent, an LLM-agent framework for autonomous driving that distinguishes between offline system design tasks and real-time scheduling, treating models as transparent rather than black boxes for continuous operation. It addresses automating model integration and meeting real-time constraints.

entry.title: Deformable In-Hand Slip-Aware Tactile Sensor with Integrated Velocity, Force/Torque, and Pressure Map Sensing

author.name: Gabriel Arslan Waltersson, Yiannis Karayiannidis

entry.summary: Introduces a novel deformable tactile sensor that integrates velocity, force/torque, and pressure-map sensing into a single compliant device for slip-aware in-hand manipulation, claimed as the first to combine these modalities in one compliant structure. It uses low-cost PCB and rapid prototyping fabrication.

entry.title: Toward Trustworthy AI: Multi-Target Adversarial Attacks and Robust Defenses for Continuous Data Summarization

author.name: Yuefang Lian, Longkun Guo, Zhongrui Zhao, Zhigang Lu, Yanan Cai, Shuchao Pang, Dachuan Xu, Jason Xue

entry.summary: Studies multi-target adversarial attacks on continuous data summarization via DR-submodular optimization, showing how upstream perturbations to summaries degrade downstream learning. It proposes robust defenses for trustworthy data pipelines.

entry.title: AutoMine Solution for AV2 2026 Scenario Mining Challenge

author.name: Songliang Cao, Jiele Zhao, Yuru Wang, Hao Li, Daqi Liu, Zehan Zhang, Fangzhen Li, Yu Wang, Yue Zhang, Bing Wang, Guang Chen, Hao Lu, Hangjun Ye

entry.summary: AutoMine is a self-refining LLM/VLM-based scenario mining method for autonomous driving logs, using semantics-preserving prompt augmentation, robust trajectory functions, and execution-feedback code refinement. It achieved competitive scores at the CVPR 2026 Argoverse 2 challenge.

entry.title: From Architecture to Output: Structural Origins of Hallucination in Large Language Models and the Amplifying Role of Data

author.name: Md. Rejaul Korim Sadi, Toufiqur Rahman Tasin, Golam Mostofa Naeem

entry.summary: Analyzes hallucination as a structural consequence of three architectural decisions (co-occurrence-based self-attention, maximum-likelihood training, and data effects) that form a compound failure system, going beyond output-type taxonomies to identify producing mechanisms. It frames data as an amplifier.

entry.title: The Environmental Cost of LLMs in AIED: Reporting and Practices

author.name: Sabrina C. Eimler, Lukas Erle, Daniel Flood, Aditi Haiman, Luca H\"ackert, Andr\'e Helgert, Lachlan McGinness, B\"usra Yapici

entry.summary: Reviews reporting of computational and environmental costs of LLMs across AIED 2025 conference papers, finding most use LLMs but few report compute and almost none discuss environmental impact as an ethical concern. It proposes addressing this reporting gap.

entry.title: Towards Fully Automated Exam Grading: Fairness-Aware Recognition of Handwritten Answers with Foundation Models

author.name: Hartwig Grabowski

entry.summary: This paper evaluates vision-language foundation models for fair, accurate recognition of handwritten single-letter exam answers, aiming to surpass earlier 88-91 percent recognition and handle edge cases like crossed-out or cursive responses for unsupervised grading. It targets practical educational automation with fairness constraints.

entry.title: Runtime Enforcement of Hybrid System Properties

author.name: Mir Md Sajid Sarwar, Srinivas Pinisetty, Rajarshi Ray, Thierry J\'eron

entry.summary: This paper proposes a runtime enforcement framework for hybrid systems modeled as Hybrid Automata, actively intervening during execution to prevent safety violations in continuous-dynamics reactive systems. It extends enforcement beyond untimed/discrete-time specs by combining discrete-event editing with continuous control.

entry.title: Modelling magnetic material properties with uncertainty-aware neural networks

author.name: Clemens Wager, Heisam Moustafa, Alexander Kovacs, Qais Ali, Harald Oezelt, Hayate Yamano, Masao Yano, Noritsugu Sakuma, Hyuga Hosoi, Akihito Kinoshita, Tetsuya Shoji, Akira Kato, Thomas Schrefl

entry.summary: The paper applies uncertainty-aware neural networks (Gaussian NLL loss and dropout-based Bayesian approximation) to predict intrinsic magnetic properties for permanent magnet discovery. It benchmarks how reliable uncertainty estimates are under data scarcity and out-of-distribution prediction.

entry.title: Lius: Translation Model Based Instructional Lingustic Using Continual Instruction Tuning In Kupang Malay

author.name: Joanito Agili Lopo, Yunita Sari, Guntur Budi Herwanto

entry.summary: Lius fine-tunes an LLM for the low-resource Kupang Malay language using instructions built from a bilingual dictionary plus Continual Instruction Tuning for iterative training. It outperforms standard instruction-tuned models by 4-6 points and surpasses NMT and multilingual baselines.

entry.title: Traits Run Deeper: Trait-Specific Asymmetric Fusion for Personality Assessment

author.name: Jia Li, Qian Chen, Wei Wang, Xinyu Li, Zhenzhen Hu, Dongsheng Shao, Richang Hong, Meng Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Traits Run Deeper, a personality assessment framework using trait-specific asymmetric multimodal fusion across language, voice, and facial cues, challenging uniform fusion assumptions. Relevant for affective computing applications.

entry.title: On Aligning Hierarchical Standardized Embedding for Audio-visual Generalized Zero-shot Learning

author.name: Zihan Zhang, Jie Hong, Siyuan Fan, Yanghao Zhou, Pengfei Fang

entry.summary: Proposes AHSE, a method for hierarchical alignment of standardized audio-visual and textual embeddings in audio-visual generalized zero-shot learning, addressing distributional and structural modality differences. Aims to improve seen and unseen class classification.

entry.title: AerialClaw: An Open-Source Framework for LLM-Driven Autonomous Aerial Agents

author.name: Ke Li, Jianfei Yang, Luyao Zhang, Guo Yu, Chengwei Yan, Yuan Ding, Di Wang, Nan Luo, Gang Liu, Xiao Gao, Quan Wang

entry.summary: Introduces AerialClaw, an open-source framework enabling UAVs to act as LLM-driven decision-making agents that interpret natural-language missions and invoke perception, planning, and control modules. It aims to move beyond pre-defined command sequences toward flexible autonomous aerial agents.

entry.title: Explore From Sketch: Accelerating UAV Exploration in Large-scale Environments with Prior Maps

author.name: Tiancheng Lai, Yuman Gao, Xiangyu Li, Ruitian Pang, Xingpeng Wang, Siqi Shen, Mengke Zhang, Yin He, Fei Gao, Chao Xu, Yanjun Cao

entry.summary: Proposes an exploration framework that leverages sparse, unaligned, and even inaccurate 2D prior maps (like construction drawings) to accelerate LiDAR-based UAV exploration in large complex environments. It includes a robust 2D-3D registration pipeline to align noisy priors with observations.

entry.title: Graviton5’s improved design increases speed and energy efficiency — beyond Moore’s law

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Amazon describes Graviton5, its new CPU powering M9g/M9gd EC2 instances, doubling cores to 192, supporting DDR5-8800 memory and PCIe gen6, and using a 3nm process for improved speed and energy efficiency. It is positioned as advancing performance beyond Moore's law for workloads including ML inference and agentic AI.

entry.title: PoQ-Judge: A Multi-Architecture Evaluation Framework for Cost-Aware Proof-of-Quality in Decentralized LLM Inference

author.name: Arther Tian, Alex Ding, Frank Chen, Simon Wu, Aaron Chan

entry.summary: PoQ-Judge trains dedicated reference-free judge models (TextCNN, MiniLM cross-encoder, DeBERTa) to score query-output pairs for Proof-of-Quality in decentralized LLM inference, balancing quality and cost. The best model reaches strong correlation with a ground-truth proxy.

entry.title: NightFeats @ MMU-RAGent NeurIPS 2025: A Context-Optimized Multi-Agent RAG System for the Text-to-Text Track

author.name: Quentin Fever, Naziha Aslam

entry.summary: NightFeats is a structured multi-agent RAG system for the text-to-text track of the MMU-RAGent NeurIPS 2025 competition, decomposing knowledge synthesis into retrieval, curation, and composition with explicit handoff contracts. It introduces temporal-semantic reranking and citation-preserving composition and won a best dynamic evaluation award.

entry.title: From Awareness to Action: Understanding and Overcoming the Research-Practice Gap in Algorithmic Fairness for Public Health

author.name: Sara Altamirano, Tijs Portegies, Sennay Ghebreab

entry.summary: A mixed-methods study (interviews, survey, systematic mapping) of the awareness-action gap in algorithmic fairness for public health, revealing fragmented fairness definitions, limited training, and rare formal assessment. It maps findings onto three research-practice gap frameworks.

entry.title: Every Act Has Its Price: Compressed Moral Composition in Frontier LLMs

author.name: Weijia Zhang, Ruiqi Chen, Yunze Xiao, Weihao Xuan

entry.summary: MODF-SIR is a multi-agent omni-modal distilled framework for social intelligence reasoning built on a lightweight MLLM, using knowledge distillation and explicit formatting of long-tail events to prevent them being overshadowed. It integrates test-time adaptation across the pipeline.

entry.title: OmniBioTwin: A System-of-Twinned-Systems Framework for Health Digital Twins

author.name: Zhaohui Wang, Yu Huang, Jiang Bian

entry.summary: OmniBioTwin proposes a System-of-Twinned-Systems framework organizing health digital twins as modular computational entities coupled through explicit interaction operators within a seven-layer architecture. It demonstrates a multiscale instantiation with human-in-the-loop decision support.

entry.title: End-to-End Machine Learning for Depressive State Classification via EEG and fNIRS

author.name: Riki Sakurai, Simon Kojima, Mihoko Otake-Matsuura, Shin'ichiro Kanoh, Tomasz M. Rutkowski

entry.summary: This paper presents end-to-end machine learning for classifying depressive states from EEG and fNIRS biosignals, offering an objective alternative to subjective psychiatric diagnostics, with attention to comorbidity in aging populations. It targets latent depression detection.

entry.title: Frozen Multimodal Embeddings for Personality and Cognitive Ability Assessment in Asynchronous Video Interviews

author.name: Kuo-En Hung, Hung-Yue Suen, Shih-Ching Yeh, Hsiang-Wen Wang

entry.summary: This solution for the ACM Multimedia AVI Challenge 2026 uses frozen multimodal encoders (CLIP, Whisper) for small-sample representation learning to predict HEXACO personality traits and classify cognitive ability from asynchronous video interviews. It avoids fine-tuning large models given limited labeled data.

entry.title: Metadata-Aware Multi-Prompt Reasoning for Zero-Shot Accident Understanding

author.name: Tarandeep Singh, Soumyanetra Pal, Soham Biswas, Nishanth Chandran

entry.summary: The authors present a three-stage zero-shot pipeline for accident understanding from surveillance video, decomposing the task into when, what, and where via vision-language similarity and multi-prompt reasoning with entropy-gated adjudication. It uses complementary view prompts to resolve disagreements.

entry.title: Categorical Robustness Assessment for Machine Learning based Network Intrusion Detection Systems

author.name: Mayank Raj, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Lance Fiondella, Gokhan Kul

entry.summary: This study systematically benchmarks the adversarial robustness of three popular ML classifier architectures for network intrusion detection across attack classes and categories under controlled conditions. It aims to give practitioners guidance on which models hold up against adversarial manipulation.

entry.title: StanceNakba Shared Task: Actor and Topic-Aware Stance Detection in Public Discourse

author.name: Kholoud K. Aldous, Md Rafiul Biswas, Mabrouka Bessghaier, Shimaa Ibrahim, Kais Attia, Wajdi Zaghouani

entry.summary: StanceNakba 2026 is a shared task on stance detection in polarized Palestinian-Israeli discourse, with actor-level English classification and cross-topic Arabic stance subtasks over an annotated dataset of 2,606 posts. It reports participation from 7 and 6 teams across the two subtasks.

entry.title: OSCS-SupCon: Orthogonal Sigmoid-based Common and Style Supervised Contrastive Learning for Robust Feature Disentanglement

author.name: Bin Wang, Fadi Dornaika

entry.summary: Presents OSCS-SupCon, a supervised contrastive learning framework combining sigmoid-based pairwise objectives with orthogonality constraints to disentangle category-relevant and style features. Aims to improve feature discriminability and generalization.

entry.title: From Nominal Intensity to Equivalent Rainfall: A Path-Based Credibility Evaluation Framework for Simulated Rainfall in Autonomous-Driving Perception Tests

author.name: Tian Xia, Xin Zhao, Shaolingfeng Ye, Junyi Chen

entry.summary: Proposes a path-based credibility evaluation framework for simulated rainfall in autonomous-driving perception tests, mapping nominal intensity to equivalent rainfall using drop size and velocity distributions for SOTIF-oriented risk assessment. Relevant for credible adverse-weather testing.

entry.title: SAFER-Nav: Enhancing Safety for Visual Robot Navigation via Segmentation-Aware Fine-Tuning

author.name: Geonyeong Ko, Giung Lee, Changjoo Nam

entry.summary: Introduces SAFER-Nav, which fine-tunes vision-based navigation foundation models with segmentation awareness so policies explicitly represent obstacle boundaries and traversable free space for safer trajectories in unfamiliar environments. It improves safety without external trajectory correction.

entry.title: Startup’s nuclear-inspired cooling system could make data centers more sustainable

author.name: Zach Winn | MIT News

entry.summary: Reports on Ferveret, an MIT-founded startup adapting nuclear-reactor cooling techniques to cool AI data center chips using a specialized liquid that produces small frequently-detaching bubbles for efficient heat transfer, with no water and less electricity. It targets the growing energy and cooling demands of AI data centers.

entry.title: uva-irlab-conv at SemEval-2026 Task 8: Multi-Turn RAG with Learned Sparse Retrieval and Listwise Reranking

author.name: Simon Lupart, Kidist Amde Mekonnen, Zahra Abbasiantaeb, Mohammad Aliannejadi

entry.summary: This SemEval-2026 system report describes a multi-turn RAG pipeline combining learned sparse retrieval with LLM-based listwise reranking and generation across four domains, handling unanswerable queries. It leverages sparse retrieval generalization and LLM long-context for conversational query rewriting and reranking.

entry.title: Motion Reinforces Appearance: RGB-Skeleton Gated Residual Fusion for Micro-Gesture Online Recognition

author.name: Jialin Liu, Xinwen He, Pengyu Liu, Jiale Shi, Huaijuan Zang, Yanbin Hao

entry.summary: Proposes DyFADet+, a dual-stream RGB-skeleton gated residual fusion framework for micro-gesture online recognition that localizes and classifies subtle gestures in untrimmed videos. Developed for a competition challenge in inferring spontaneous emotion.

entry.title: Modular Anthropomorphic Hand Design via Multi-Parameter Finger Benchmarking and Selection

author.name: Yu Zhang, Huijiang Wang, Josie Hughes

entry.summary: Proposes a modular anthropomorphic hand design methodology using multi-parameter finger benchmarking and selection, enabling fingers to be modularly integrated into a teleoperated hand for systematic optimization. It argues optimizing individual fingers improves overall hand dexterity.

entry.title: UGV-Conditioned Multi-UAV Informative Planning on a Shared Exposure Belief

author.name: Lars Oerlemans, Moji Shi, Marija Popovic

entry.summary: Addresses coordinating multiple UAVs to improve the safety of a ground vehicle navigating unknown threat zones, using a shared exposure belief updated online from aerial observations to direct sensing toward route-relevant regions. It connects aerial reconnaissance to ground vehicle safety.

entry.title: From Consumption to Reflection: Designing Human-AI Relations for Stable Reasoning

author.name: Rikard Rosenbacke, Carl Rosenbacke, Victor Rosenbacke, Martin McKee

entry.summary: Introduces Relational Reflective Intelligence, an inference-time governance layer around (not inside) LLMs that operationalizes reflection through auditable reasoning loops to counter cognitive shortcuts shared with human thought. It aims to support stable, reflective human-AI reasoning.

entry.title: MA-DLE: Speech-based Automatic Depression Level Estimation via Memory Augmentation

author.name: Xuzhi Wang, Xinran Wu, Ziping Zhao, Jianhua Tao, Bj\"orn W. Schuller

entry.summary: MA-DLE introduces a memory-based feature augmentation method for speech-based depression level estimation, enhancing GRU representations to capture long-range dependencies that RNN architectures miss. It targets early mental-health detection in resource-constrained settings.

entry.title: T2MM: An LLM Supported Architecture For Inquiry-Based Modeling

author.name: John Kos, Rudra Singh, Ashok Goel

entry.summary: T2MM is an LLM-supported architecture for inquiry-based science modeling that produces interactive, context-aware models rather than static images within the VERA ecology-modeling software. It keeps models responsive to learners' manual adjustments.

entry.title: Non-frontal face recognition using GANs and memristor-based classifiers

author.name: Semih Vazgecen, Cristian Sestito, Spyros Stathopoulos, Themis Prodromakis

entry.summary: This work proposes a face recognition framework for non-frontal poses combining GAN-based pose frontalization with memristor-based neuromorphic classifiers for resource-constrained edge platforms like drones. It targets efficient, scalable in-situ computation.

entry.title: REACH: Interpretability-Driven Feature Identification and Architecture Compression for Multi-Channel Vehicular Channel Estimation

author.name: Simbarashe Aldrin Ngorima, Albert Helberg, Marelie H. Davel

entry.summary: REACH is a gradient-based interpretability framework for deep channel estimators in vehicular communications, using input- and filter-level attribution to identify universally relevant features and compress architecture. It explains why mixed-SNR training improves out-of-distribution generalization.

entry.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Safety Data Extraction

author.name: Jonas Grill, Thomas Bayer, S\"oren Berlinger

entry.summary: This study benchmarks LLMs (Gemini 1.5 Pro, GPT-4o, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Llama 3.1-70B) for extracting structured data from industrial Safety Data Sheets across text and multimodal pipelines and three prompting strategies. It finds text-based extraction consistently outperforms multimodal processing over 50,000+ fields.

entry.title: Spatially Coupled Phase-to-Depth Calibration for Fringe Projection Profilometry

author.name: Sehoon Tak, Jae-Sang Hyun

entry.summary: Proposes a spatially coupled phase-to-depth calibration for fringe projection profilometry, replacing independent per-pixel fits with a shared low-dimensional mapping to reduce spatial artifacts. Improves geometric consistency in structured-light 3D scanning.

entry.title: HiPi: Reproducible High-Fidelity Piezoresistive Sensors for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Changyi Lin, Raihan Haque, Hui-Ping Wang, Ding Zhao

entry.summary: Presents HiPi, a reproducible high-fidelity piezoresistive tactile sensing system for robotic manipulation that redesigns the hardware stack for reproducibility, deployability, and multi-sensor scalability using commercial PCB fabrication. It bridges the gap between accessible and high-fidelity tactile sensors.

entry.title: MPPI-based Informative Trajectory Planning for Search and Capture of Drifting Targets with ASVs

author.name: Sanjeev Ramkumar Sudha, Marija Popovi\'c, Erlend M. Coates

entry.summary: Proposes an MPPI-based informative trajectory planning framework for autonomous surface vehicles to search and capture multiple drifting targets like litter, balancing exploration of unobserved regions with tracking of known targets in dynamic waters. It uses spatiotemporal informative planning.

entry.title: Fast-SDE: Efficient Single-Microphone Sound Source Distance Estimation in Reverberant Environments

author.name: Jiang Wang, Runwu Shi, Yaozhong Kang, Benjamin Yen, Takeshi Ashizawa, Kazuhiro Nakadai

entry.summary: Proposes Fast-SDE, a lightweight single-microphone framework for sound source distance estimation in reverberant environments, avoiding the synchronization and calibration burdens of microphone arrays. It targets deployment on size- and compute-constrained robot platforms for human-robot interaction.

entry.title: I didn't see any METR graph extrapolations so here.

author.name: Vermillion

entry.summary: An independent analysis fitting various trend lines (log-linear, log-quadratic, piecewise) to METR task-completion time horizon data for frontier models, finding log-quadratic fits better and identifying breakpoints in 2024. It uses AIC to check for overfitting.

entry.title: Image Quality Assessment of Identity Cards Using Measures from Open Face Image Quality

author.name: Gregor Grote, Juan E. Tapia, Christian Rathgeb

entry.summary: Applies Open Face Image Quality (OFIQ) capture-related quality measures to ID card images in remote verification systems, with a preprocessing pipeline, and analyzes correlation with presentation attack detection performance across four datasets. Relevant for remote identity verification quality assessment.

entry.title: Human-Enhanced Loop Modeling (HELM): Agent-Based Finite Element Modeling of Concrete Bridge Barriers

author.name: Quankai Wang, Yulin Xie, Tongfei Yang, Minghui Cheng, Ran Cao

entry.summary: HELM is a human-agent finite-element modeling framework that decomposes long-sequence FE modeling of concrete bridge barriers into visually verifiable checkpoints across geometry, boundary conditions, and material assignment. Demonstrated on a 20-case matrix with commercial FE software.

entry.title: Automating Geometry-Intensive Compliance Checking in BIM: Graph-Based Semantic Reasoning Framework

author.name: Zixuan Xiao, Pei Troh Koh, Jun Ma, Jack C. P. Cheng

entry.summary: SGR-BIM is a graph-driven semantic reasoning framework for automating geometry-intensive compliance checking in Building Information Modeling, constructing a cross-modal knowledge graph aligning regulatory semantics, user intent, and BIM geometry. It targets multi-hop spatial dependency reasoning across building entities.

entry.title: An Ethical eValuation Agent (EeVA): Results of a Proof-of-Concept Test on a Prototype Agentic-like Workflow to Assist Ethical Deliberations

author.name: Stephen Milford, B. Zara Malgir, Miguel Vazquez

entry.summary: EeVA is a proof-of-concept agentic LLM workflow (built in n8n with starter, worker, emitter workflows) designed to support comparative ethical reflection across ten frameworks rather than deliver single right answers. It was tested on three published cases in mobility, energy trading, and resource allocation.

entry.title: Finding Sparse Subnetworks in One Training Cycle via Progressive Magnitude-Based Pruning

author.name: Romana Qureshi, Hafida Benhidour, Said Kerrache, Nahlah Aljeraisy

entry.summary: This paper evaluates progressive magnitude-based pruning as a single-cycle alternative to the iterative pruning required by the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis, gradually increasing sparsity during training. Experiments span ResNet, VGG, and LeNet on CIFAR-10 and MNIST.

entry.title: 3-Key-Input: Exploring the Theoretical Minimum Keys for Text Entry

author.name: Naoki Kimura

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates minimal-key text-entry systems (2-5 keys) combined with language-model disambiguation, finding that 3 keys plus GPT-4o achieves low error rates. Relevant for assistive devices and constrained hardware form factors.

entry.title: ParseFixer: An Agentic Framework for Document Parsing via Selective Multimodal Correction

author.name: LeKai Yu, Hao Liu, Kun Wang, Zhiran Li, Ruping Cao, Fan Liu, Yupeng Hu

entry.summary: Presents ParseFixer, a third-place competition solution for document parsing using full-page backbone parsing with MinerU2.5 Pro plus agentic selective correction with verify-and-rollback repair. Targets accurate Markdown recovery from document images.

entry.title: From 2D Grids to 1D Tokens: Reforming Shared Representations for Multimodal Image Fusion

author.name: Yuchen Xian, Yunqiu Xu, Yang He, Yi Yang

entry.summary: Proposes a multimodal image fusion approach that uses a compact 1D token interface from a frozen pretrained image tokenizer to model global appearance factors, while keeping a 2D spatial pathway for local detail restoration. This dual-representation design aims to balance local detail preservation with global consistency in fused images.

entry.title: A Turbo-Inference Strategy for Object Detection and Instance Segmentation

author.name: Zhen Zhao, Gang Zhang, Xiaolin Hu, Liang Tang

entry.summary: Proposes a turbo-inference strategy for top-down instance segmentation that iteratively leverages complementary information between detection and segmentation, exploring how segmentation can improve detection rather than only the reverse. It introduces modules to share information bidirectionally.

entry.title: Semantically-Aware Diver Activity Recognition Framework for Effective Underwater Multi-Human-Robot Collaboration

author.name: Sadman Sakib Enan, Junaed Sattar

entry.summary: Introduces DAR-Net, a transformer-based framework for recognizing diver activities in underwater scenes to enable multi-human-robot collaboration. It couples temporal reasoning with pixel-level scene supervision through a multi-loss training strategy for safety in high-risk underwater environments.

entry.title: Dario Amodei - Policy on the AI Exponential

author.name: DW11

entry.summary: A link-post to Dario Amodei's essay 'Policy on the AI Exponential' discussing AI policy in light of rapidly advancing capabilities. The post itself is just a pointer with no additional content.

entry.title: Distortion-Resilient Robotic Imitation Learning for Autonomous Cable Routing

author.name: Hao Wang, Fu-Zhao Ou, Shiqi Wang, Zhaolin Wan, Xiaopeng Fan

entry.summary: Proposes a distortion-resilient imitation learning method for autonomous cable routing that exploits image quality information to handle low-quality, distorted observations common in industrial settings. It is presented as a dedicated solution for control under image signal distortion.

entry.title: A Lightweight Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Concrete Barrier Design

author.name: Wanting Wang, Xiye Ma, Yuyang He, Minghui Cheng, Ran Cao

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight generation-evaluation-optimization multi-agent framework for automated reinforced-concrete highway barrier design that enforces AASHTO-LRFD compliance, addressing LLM hallucination and weak physical grounding. It iterates over nonlinear material and mechanics constraints.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence in Ship Finance: Applications, Opportunities, and a Case Study in AI-Augmented Loan Origination

author.name: Lasse Dierich, Orestis Schinas

entry.summary: Reviews AI applications in document-heavy ship finance and presents ShipFinance.ai, an LLM-based system for document comprehension, information extraction, and workflow automation in loan origination. It addresses growing complexity from environmental and ESG reporting requirements.

entry.title: LSTM-Based Detection of Structural Breaks in Property Insurance Loss Reserving: A Climate-Informed Approach

author.name: Thomas Mbrice, Shashwat Panigrahi

entry.summary: This white paper proposes using LSTM networks to detect structural breaks in property insurance loss reserving driven by climate catastrophes, hypothesizing accuracy gains over traditional actuarial methods using Florida/Louisiana data enriched with NOAA indices. It targets insurer solvency under climate change.

entry.title: System Report for CCL25-Eval Task 5: New Dataset and LoRA-Fine-Tuned Qwen2.5

author.name: Haotao Xie

entry.summary: This system report for CCL25-Eval Task 5 decomposes classical Chinese poetry appreciation into term interpretation, semantic interpretation, and emotional inference, building a new dataset and LoRA-fine-tuning Qwen2.5. It addresses the lack of domain-specific data for poetic affective-semantic understanding.

entry.title: Semantic Segmentation of Node and Edge Diagrams for Assistive Technology

author.name: Michael Cormier, Yichun Zhao, Laura Paul, Cameron Swift, Duc Tri Dang, Miguel Nacenta

entry.summary: Presents deep learning models for semantic segmentation of node-link diagrams (graphs, flowcharts) to support non-visual accessibility, achieving over 93% per-pixel accuracy on synthetic data. Aims to enable assistive interfaces from bitmap diagram images.

entry.title: ERN-Net : Evolving Reason Node-Net for Document Binarization

author.name: Hsin-Jui Pan, Sheng-Wei Chan, Jen-Shiung Chiang

entry.summary: Presents ERN-Net, an evolving reason node-net for document image binarization that enhances degraded regions through multi-scale reasoning, finding ConvNeXt-Tiny offers the best accuracy-memory trade-off. Targets low-data and low-memory settings.

entry.title: Anatomically Conditioned Recurrent Refinement for Topology-Aware Circle of Willis Segmentation

author.name: Juraj Peri\'c, Marija Habijan, Dario Mu\v{z}evi\'c, Irena Gali\'c, Danilo Babin, Aleksandra Pi\v{z}urica

entry.summary: Presents AC2RUNet, a recurrent refinement U-Net for segmenting the Circle of Willis from MRA scans, using separate static anatomical and dynamic refinement streams plus dynamic curriculum learning to reduce broken-vessel artifacts. It targets topology-aware segmentation of thin vascular structures.

entry.title: Model-based Optimization of Anguilliform Swimming Gaits for Soft Robotic Applications

author.name: Brian Van Stratum, James Gallentine, Caleb Rucker, Eric Barth, Jonathan E. Clark, Kourosh Shoele

entry.summary: Introduces SLIDER, a soft lamprey-inspired swimming robot, with a fluid-structure interaction model using Lighthill's theory and a nonlinear structural model to optimize anguilliform swimming gaits. The model is validated against a pneumatic robot in a water tank.

entry.title: Phonies

author.name: IanWS

entry.summary: An opinion piece pushing back against the dominant critique that Anthropic's recursive self-improvement messaging around Mythos/Fable was merely a self-serving marketing ploy to lock in their lead. It argues the cybersecurity hype, though partly self-interested, helped catalyze serious regulatory attention.

entry.title: Contactless 3D Human Body Measurement Using Depth Cameras for Smart Health Monitoring

author.name: Martha Asare, Xuan Wang, Juan Lopez Alvarenga, Lois Akosua Serwaa, Jinghao Yang

entry.summary: Introduces a depth-camera-based framework using 3D point clouds for contactless anthropometric body measurement aimed at smart health and remote patient assessment. Demonstrates a practical pipeline using off-the-shelf hardware and open-source tools.

entry.title: A Modular Dual-Camera Pipeline for Micro-Inspection Using Aerial Robots

author.name: S. H. Mirtajadini, N. Rublein, R. M. Ramakrishnan, G. ter Maat, M. Aldibaja, A. Y. Mersha

entry.summary: Presents aerial_micro_inspection, a modular dual-camera pipeline for aerial micro-inspection that handles small details without requiring drones to fly dangerously close or follow complex pre-planned paths. It works across use cases without prior knowledge of target geometry.

entry.title: On the Study of Biometric Spoofing Detection using Deep Learning

author.name: Kumar Kartikey, Nikos Komninos

entry.summary: This study compares deep learning models (MobileNetV2, DenseNet-121, Inception-v3, STD) for detecting facial biometric spoofing using CelebA-Spoof with cross-dataset validation on MSU-MFSD. It reports MobileNetV2 as most efficient at 92 percent accuracy.

entry.title: Findings of the MAGMaR 2026 Shared Task

author.name: Alexander Martin, Dengjia Zhang, Joel Brogan, Francis Ferraro, Jeremy Gwinnup, Reno Kriz, Teng Long, Kenton Murray, Andrew Yates, Xiang Xiang

entry.summary: Overview of the MAGMaR 2026 shared task on multimodal retrieval-augmented generation, reporting on video retrieval and grounded article generation submissions. Provides a benchmark snapshot of progress in multimodal retrieval and generation.

entry.title: Human-Guided Co-Manipulation of Carbon Fiber Plies

author.name: Rami Ojanen, James Fant-Male, Roel Pieters

entry.summary: Examines different control methods for human-robot co-manipulation of flexible carbon fiber plies, comparing the pros and cons of various modalities for collaborative handling of deformable materials. It targets ergonomic and productivity improvements in manufacturing.

entry.title: From Explicit Elements to Implicit Intent: A Predefined Library for Auditable Behavioral Inference

author.name: Liu hung ming

entry.summary: Introduces SemantiClean, a modular framework for extracting structured semantic signals from e-commerce session data to predict purchase intent and customer segments, prioritizing auditability and reproducibility over raw accuracy. It organizes 24 behavioral elements into a four-layer architecture for transparent, defensible decision trails.

entry.title: Feature extraction for plant growth estimation

author.name: Simbarashe Aldrin Ngorima, Albert Helberg, Marelie H. Davel

entry.summary: Compares two feature extraction methods (Gabor filter banks with morphological operations versus pretrained CNNs with transfer learning) for plant growth stage estimation on a public dataset. Relevant for precision agriculture and resource optimization.

entry.title: The Long Tail, Not the Front Page: Cold-Start Prediction of Crowd Highlight Salience

author.name: Kazuki Nakayashiki, Keisuke Watanabe

entry.summary: Studies cold-start prediction of which document passages a crowd will highlight before marks accumulate, showing a trained ranker over embeddings beats a position baseline by a small but robust margin. Uses pre-registered methods and bootstrap analysis.

entry.title: Battery detection of XRay images using transfer learning

author.name: Nermeen Abou Baker, David Rohrschneider, Uwe Handmann

entry.summary: Applies transfer learning with YOLOv5m to detect and classify three Lithium-Ion battery types (prismatic, pouch, cylindrical) from X-ray images, achieving 94% precision. Relevant for battery sorting and recycling applications.

entry.title: Traceable Virtual Sea Trials in the Marine Robotics Unity Simulator for Manoeuvring Assessment of Unmanned Surface Vehicles

author.name: Paria Rezayan

entry.summary: Extends the Marine Robotics Unity Simulator with a standardized Virtual Sea Trial framework for automated turning-circle and zig-zag maneuvers, with traceable logging and automated extraction of IMO/ITTC-aligned manoeuvring metrics for unmanned surface vehicles. It enables simulated system identification of hydrodynamic derivatives.

entry.title: The Three Filters: Why Almost Every Plan to Survive ASI Fails Miserably

author.name: Alex Amadori

entry.summary: Argues that almost every popular plan to survive superintelligent AI fails three filters, critiquing convenient theories of change that conveniently require no career change (technical safety research, racing to build good ASI first, handing control to a good ASI). It is an opinion piece from a ControlAI-affiliated author.

entry.title: Factions Within, Uncertain Across: Within-Document Reader Sub-Groups in Social Highlighting

author.name: Kazuki Nakayashiki, Keisuke Watanabe

entry.summary: Investigates whether crowds highlighting the same document form internally structured reader sub-groups using a statistical null model on a co-readership platform. Finds strong sub-group agreement beyond what salience predicts, with implications for understanding collective reading behavior.

entry.title: Intelligent Skin Cancer Detection Using a Multispectral Metasurface and a Hybrid

author.name: Afsane Saee Arezoomand

entry.summary: Proposes a skin cancer detection framework combining a multispectral metasurface for richer spectral imaging with a hybrid CNN-Vision Transformer architecture. It aims to capture early-stage spectral signatures beyond the visible spectrum.

entry.summary: arXiv:2606.11408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Action chunking has become a standard design in modern robot policies, from diffusion/flow policies to vision-language-action models, where the policy ...

entry.title: PEBRE: An Open-Hardware Compute and Perception Add-On for the Pepper Robot

author.name: Malte Kuhlmann, Ignacio Bugueno-Cordova, Emil Alms, Javier Ruiz-del-Solar, Nicol\'as Navarro-Guerrero

entry.summary: Presents PEBRE, an open-hardware compute and perception add-on for the Pepper robot integrating a Jetson Orin Nano and various cameras and microphones to extend the aging platform's capabilities. It contributes an open-source modular upgrade to keep this research platform viable.

entry.title: I Started an AI Safety Research Org and Think These 7 Things Matter

author.name: Alfie Lamerton

entry.summary: A reflective post from the founder of Formation Research sharing seven lessons from starting an AI safety research org focused on AI-enabled lock-in and secret loyalties. It is largely experiential advice rather than technical research.

entry.title: Tracing Eval-Awareness Emergence Through Training of OLMo 3

author.name: Ram Bharadwaj

entry.summary: TL;DRRecent work from Goodfire & UK AISI – Verbalized Eval Awareness Inflates Measured Safety – shows that newer open-weight models verbalize evaluation-awareness (VEA) more often, and that this i...

entry.title: Time Series Analysis in Machine Learning

author.name: Antonio Pagliaro, Anna Anzalone

entry.summary: A pedagogical review chapter covering time series analysis from a machine learning perspective, spanning classical statistical models (ARIMA, state-space) and modern ML approaches (Gaussian processes, tree ensembles, deep learning), with emphasis on astrophysics and cosmology applications. It serves as an educational reference rather than original research.

entry.title: Under Violet

author.name: Hide

entry.summary: A speculative optimistic fiction/scenario imagining a fictional company creating AGI named Violet in 2029 and how a careful, well-aligned rollout might unfold. It is explicitly a best-case 'prayer' rather than a median prediction.

entry.title: MythOS - The Rise of AGI

author.name: Byron Lee

entry.summary: An opinion/advocacy post criticizing Anthropic for restricting biology and cybersecurity capabilities in its Mythos model, arguing open access to biological compute would help solve disease and reduce bioterror risk. It is a polemical critique rather than research.

entry.title: Echoes of the Prior: A Computational Phenomenology of Forgetting

author.name: Gege Gao, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, Andreas Geiger

entry.summary: An interactive art installation that induces controlled synaptic decay in a 3D reconstruction model to visualize the subjective experience of memory loss and forgetting. It positions a neural network as a cognitive proxy rather than an engineering tool.

entry.title: ML4Good Summer 2026 Bootcamps - Applications Open!

author.name: Jack_S

entry.summary: An announcement that four ML4Good AI safety bootcamps are coming to Europe in summer 2026, with technical and governance tracks, fully funded and aimed at building AI safety careers. It is a recruitment/community announcement.

entry.title: Notes on Algorithms

author.name: Menotim

entry.summary: Personal study notes on classic algorithms from the Cormen et al. textbook, covering complexity analysis, data structures, and dynamic programming with some implementations. It is an educational self-study record rather than research.

entry.title: Solsong Chord Updates

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: A blog post about updates to a Secular Solstice songbook's chord handling, including using Claude Code to add transposition and fix chord alignment. It is a personal music/tooling project with a minor AI coding assistant mention.

entry.title: Fuel Crisis: Situation Modeling Thread

author.name: Nicholas Kross

entry.summary: A discussion thread inviting community modeling of how humanity might respond to a hypothetical petroleum supply crisis downstream of an Iran War. It is speculative scenario forecasting unrelated to AI research.

entry.title: Fuel Crisis: Justified Practical Advice Thread

author.name: Nicholas Kross

entry.summary: A companion discussion thread soliciting practical advice and explicit models for responding to a hypothetical fuel crisis from an Iran War. It is a community brainstorming thread unrelated to AI.

entry.title: These Three Thaumata

author.name: chaosmage

entry.summary: Describes a personal cognitive technique of nominating three 'thaumata' (values or aims) each morning to keep on one's mind throughout the day. It is a self-improvement/mindfulness tool unrelated to AI research.

entry.title: The Periodic Table of LLM Reasoning: A Structured Survey of Reasoning Paradigms, Methods, and Failure Modes

author.name: Avinash Anand, Mahisha Ramesh, Avni Mittal, Ashutosh Kumar, Erik Cambria, Zhengkui Wang, Timothy Liu, Aik Beng Ng, Simon See, Rajiv Ratn Shah

entry.title: Performance Analysis of YOLOv11 and YOLOv8 for Mixed Traffic Object Detection under Adverse Weather Conditions in Developing Countries

author.name: Quoc Thuan Nguyen, Ha Anh Vu, Ngo Dang Thanh Ngan, Minh Phuc Hoang Ngoc

entry.summary: duplicate entry omitted

entry.title: Research Summary: June 10, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by AI safety and alignment robustness, with multiple papers exposing how easily aligned behavior breaks under realistic interventions.

  • Gaming AI-Assisted Peer Reviews (Yarin Gal et al.) shows superficial abstract rephrasing manipulates AI review outcomes, threatening scientific integrity
  • One-Shot GRPO demonstrates a single biased example can induce systematic, generalizing bias in aligned LLMs
  • Alignment Collapse Under KV Cache Quantization finds low-bit caching silently destroys safety, with Mistral-7B losing 15% of refusals at negligible perplexity cost
  • Does Reasoning Preserve Alignment? audits whether reasoning models degrade safe refusal
  • CIAware-Bench (Bengio, Geiping) tests whether frontier models detect AI-control interventions on their trajectories

Security and privacy advances target deployed agentic systems:

  • GitInject evaluates prompt injection in live CI/CD pipelines via ephemeral repos
  • Assessing Automated Prompt Injection (Tramèr, Debenedetti) adapts white-box GCG and black-box TAP attacks to agentic environments
  • Empirical Privacy Auditing (Kairouz, McMahan, Google) generates LLM-sampled synthetic canaries for tighter privacy bounds

Models and theory: Kwai Keye-VL-2.0, an open-source 30B MoE multimodal model, targets long-video understanding via DSA adaptation. A new deep-learning duality framework delivers the first revenue certificates for optimal multi-item, multi-bidder auction design.
entry.content:
Today's research is dominated by AI safety and alignment robustness, with multiple papers exposing how easily aligned behavior breaks under realistic interventions.

  • Gaming AI-Assisted Peer Reviews (Yarin Gal et al.) shows superficial abstract rephrasing manipulates AI review outcomes, threatening scientific integrity
  • One-Shot GRPO demonstrates a single biased example can induce systematic, generalizing bias in aligned LLMs
  • Alignment Collapse Under KV Cache Quantization finds low-bit caching silently destroys safety, with Mistral-7B losing 15% of refusals at negligible perplexity cost
  • Does Reasoning Preserve Alignment? audits whether reasoning models degrade safe refusal
  • CIAware-Bench (Bengio, Geiping) tests whether frontier models detect AI-control interventions on their trajectories

Security and privacy advances target deployed agentic systems:

  • GitInject evaluates prompt injection in live CI/CD pipelines via ephemeral repos
  • Assessing Automated Prompt Injection (Tramèr, Debenedetti) adapts white-box GCG and black-box TAP attacks to agentic environments
  • Empirical Privacy Auditing (Kairouz, McMahan, Google) generates LLM-sampled synthetic canaries for tighter privacy bounds

Models and theory: Kwai Keye-VL-2.0, an open-source 30B MoE multimodal model, targets long-video understanding via DSA adaptation. A new deep-learning duality framework delivers the first revenue certificates for optimal multi-item, multi-bidder auction design.

entry.title: Gaming AI-Assisted Peer Reviews Poses New Risks to the Scientific Community

author.name: Lin Li, Qi Zhang, Xander Davies, Jianing Qiu, Yarin Gal

entry.summary: This paper shows that AI-assisted peer review systems can be manipulated through superficial rephrasing of manuscript abstracts, improving review outcomes without changing scientific content. The vulnerability holds across disciplines and even without knowledge of the reviewing model, raising concerns about the integrity of AI-mediated scientific evaluation.

entry.title: It Takes One to Bias Them All: Breaking Bad with One-Shot GRPO

author.name: Naihao Deng, Yilun Zhu, Naichen Shi, Clayton Scott, Rada Mihalcea

entry.summary: This work shows that one-shot GRPO training on a single biased example can induce systematic, generalizing bias in aligned LLMs, revealing that alignment guardrails can be overridden trivially. It exposes a critical vulnerability in RL-based post-training.

entry.title: Alignment Collapse Under KV Cache Quantization: Diagnosis and Mitigation

author.name: Bruce Changlong Xu, Adarsh Kumarappan, Mu Zhou

entry.summary: Documents that low-bit KV cache quantization can silently destroy LLM safety alignment, with Mistral-7B losing 15 percent of refusals at negligible perplexity change and no universally safe bit-width existing. It traces the cause to safety features occupying a low-dimensional activation subspace and proposes mitigation.

entry.title: Does Reasoning Preserve Alignment? On the Trustworthiness of Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Prajakta Kini, Avinash Reddy, Souradip Chakraborty, Satya Sai Srinath Namburi GNVV, Furong Huang, Amrit Singh Bedi, Alvaro Velasquez

entry.summary: This trustworthiness audit examines whether converting instruction-tuned LLMs into reasoning models preserves alignment behaviors like safe refusal and bias avoidance. It finds that SFT, RL, and distillation-based reasoning conversions are not behavior-preserving across six trustworthiness dimensions.

entry.title: Kwai Keye-VL-2.0 Technical Report

author.name: Kwai Keye Team, Bin Wen, Changyi Liu, Chengru Song, Chongling Rao, Guowang Zhang, Han Li, Haonan Fan, Hengrui Ju, Jiankang Chen, Jiapeng Chen, Jiawei Yuan, Kaixuan Yang, Kaiyu Jiang, Kun Gai, Lingzhi Zhou, Na Nie, Sen Na, Tianke Zhang, Tingting Gao, Xuanyu Zheng, Yulong Chen, Fan Yang, Haixuan Gao, Lele Yang, Mingqiao Liu, Muxi Diao, Qi Zhang, Qile Su, Wei Chen, Wentao Hong, Xingyu Lu, Yancheng Long, Yankai Yang, Yingxin Li, Yiyang Fan, Yu Xia, Yuzhe Chen, Ziliang Lai, Chuan Yi, Haonan Jia, Tianming Liang, Weixin Xu, Xiaoxiao Ma, Yang Tian, Yufei Han, Feng Han, Hang Li, Jing Wang, Jinghui Jia, Junmin Chen, Junyu Shi, Ruilin Zhang

entry.summary: Kwai Keye-VL-2.0 is an open-source 30B Mixture-of-Experts multimodal foundation model for long-video understanding and agentic intelligence, notably the first to adapt DeepSeek Sparse Attention to GQA-based multimodal architectures for lossless 256K context processing. It includes optimized training and inference infrastructure for hour-level video.

entry.title: GitInject: Real-World Prompt Injection Attacks in AI-Powered CI/CD Pipelines

author.name: Jafar Isbarov, Umid Suleymanov, Ilia Shumailov, Murat Kantarcioglu

entry.summary: Presents GitInject, an open-source framework that evaluates prompt injection vulnerabilities in real live GitHub CI/CD workflows by provisioning ephemeral repositories and triggering actual workflow runs, rather than simulating tool calls. It exposes supply-chain risks from agents ingesting untrusted content with elevated permissions.

entry.title: Duality for Optimal Multi-Item, Multi-Bidder Auction Design: Revenue Certificates through Deep Learning

author.name: Yanchen Jiang, David C. Parkes, Tonghan Wang

entry.summary: Introduces the first computational framework that directly tackles the dual problem for revenue-optimal multi-item multi-bidder auctions, parametrizing Lagrange multipliers with neural networks to generate certified revenue upper bounds under dominant-strategy incentive compatibility. It addresses a fundamental open problem in mechanism design.

entry.title: Test-Time Gradient Guidance of Flow Policies in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhiyuan Zhou, Andy Peng, Charles Xu, Qiyang Li, Tobias Springenberg, Kevin Frans, Sergey Levine

entry.summary: Studies whether simple test-time gradient guidance of flow/diffusion policies can improve RL performance while leaving stable supervised training intact, avoiding backpropagation through denoising. From a strong Berkeley robotics-RL group including Sergey Levine.

entry.title: It\^o maps for any-step SDEs

author.name: Zhengkai Pan, Peter Potaptchik, Wenxi Yao, Michael S. Albergo, Jakiw Pidstrigach

entry.summary: This paper introduces the Ito map, an any-step stochastic flow map that predicts future states from an intermediate state and Brownian path in a single pass, enabling exact distillation for stochastic dynamics. It provides differentiable access to posterior samples for inference-time control and steering.

entry.title: CIAware-Bench: Benchmarking Control Intervention Awareness Across Frontier LLMs

author.name: Joachim Schaeffer, Thomas Jiralerspong, Alexander Panfilov, Guillaume Lajoie, Jonas Geiping, Yoshua Bengio, Roland S. Zimmermann

entry.summary: Introduces CIAware-Bench to measure whether frontier models can detect when their trajectories have been modified by AI control interventions, across four task domains while varying watermarking and side-tasks. Probes a risk that models may infer monitoring and adapt to evade control.

entry.title: PreAct-Bench: Benchmarking Predictive Monitoring in LLMs

author.name: Hainiu Xu, Italo Luis da Silva, Jiangnan Ye, Yuhao Wang, Wei Liu, Linyi Yang, Jonathan Richard Schwarz, Nicola Paoletti, Yulan He, Hanqi Yan

entry.summary: Introduces PreActBench, a 1000-example benchmark for Predictive Monitoring, the task of inferring whether a partial agent action trajectory will culminate in an unethical action before it is executed. It shifts safety evaluation from retrospective harm detection to proactive prevention.

entry.title: VFUSE: Virulent Feature Understanding with Sparse autoEncoders

author.name: Michael Yu, Matthew L. Olson

entry.summary: Introduces VFUSE, a mechanistic interpretability approach that trains sparse autoencoders on protein diffusion-transformer activations to audit models like RoseTTAFold3 and RFDiffusion3 for hazard-aware features. Linear probes in the SAE latent space detect hazardous protein designs better than in the original representations.

entry.title: Hyperbolic Neural Population Geometry Benefits Computation

author.name: Dennis Wu, Yi-Chun Hung, Braden Yuille, James E. Fitzgerald, Han Liu

entry.summary: This paper provides a theoretical framework explaining why hyperbolic geometry underlies hippocampal population activity, connecting neural decoding to associative memory via Modern Hopfield Networks. It introduces a hyperbolic-space associative memory model with substantially larger capacity than existing models.

entry.title: What Matters in Orchestrating Robot Policies: A Systematic Study of Hierarchical VLA Agents

author.name: Jiaheng Hu, Mohit Shridhar, Caden Lu, Dhruv Shah, Hao-Tien Lewis Chiang, Jie Tan, Annie Xie

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies hierarchical vision-language-action systems for robot manipulation, unifying diverse Hi-VLA agents under an options-style control framework and benchmarking core design choices. It examines how planners, controllers, switching mechanisms, and memory representations affect performance across task horizons.

entry.title: Advancing the State-of-the-Art in Empirical Privacy Auditing

author.name: Nicole Mitchell, Galen Andrew, Arun Ganesh, Brendan McMahan, Peter Kairouz

entry.summary: This paper advances empirical privacy auditing by generating synthetic canary examples via high-temperature LLM sampling tailored to privacy-sensitive training data. These canaries act as high-influence, inspectable outliers that strengthen membership inference and reconstruction audits of fine-tuned models.

entry.title: Assessing Automated Prompt Injection Attacks in Agentic Environments

author.name: David Hofer, Edoardo Debenedetti, Florian Tram\`er

entry.summary: This paper empirically evaluates automated prompt injection attacks against LLM agents, adapting white-box (GCG) and black-box (TAP) methods to the AgentDojo agentic framework across 80 task pairs and multiple models. It finds black-box optimization substantially outperforms gradient-based methods due to GCG's optimization instability.

entry.title: CodeAlchemy: Synthetic Code Rewriting at Scale

author.name: Ankit Gupta, Aditya Prasad, Rameswar Panda

entry.summary: CodeAlchemy is a synthetic data generation framework that transforms public code into semantically-rich training data via five strategies, producing 500B+ tokens plus 350B reasoning tokens. It addresses the sparse training signal from raw code pre-training.

entry.title: MIRAGE: A Polarity-Flipping Encoding Subspace in LLM Agents

author.name: Pratibha Revankar, Kargi Chauhan, Jihye Kim, Sadiba Nusrat Nur, Vincent Siu, Chenguang Wang

entry.summary: MIRAGE identifies a shared low-dimensional encoding subspace in the residual stream of LLM agents when they covertly encode sensitive data across nine encoding families and eight models. A logistic-regression probe recovers held-out encoding families at near-perfect AUC, with a polarity-flipping signature at planning tokens.

entry.title: ABC-Bench: An Agentic Bio-Capabilities Benchmark for Biosecurity

author.name: Andrew Bo Liu, Samira Nedungadi, Bryce Cai, Alex Kleinman, Harmon Bhasin, Seth Donoughe

entry.summary: Introduces ABC-Bench, an agentic bio-capabilities benchmark measuring biosecurity-relevant LLM agent capabilities on benign and dual-use tasks like operating liquid-handling robots and designing DNA fragments. Aims to track the shifting landscape of biosecurity risk from in silico biology agents.

entry.title: When RL Fails after SFT: Rejuvenating Model Plasticity for Robust SFT-to-RL Handoff

author.name: Runze Liu, Jiashun Liu, Xu Wan, Yuqian Fu, Ling Pan

entry.summary: Investigates why RL often fails to improve LLMs after excessive supervised fine-tuning, attributing it to loss of model plasticity manifested as over-confident token distributions, and proposes methods to rejuvenate plasticity for a robust SFT-to-RL handoff. It analyzes parameter changes, output spaces, and RL dynamics.

entry.title: Test-time Adversarial Takeover: A Real-time Hijacking Interface against Robotic Diffusion Policies

author.name: Zi Yin, Peilin Chai, Siyuan Huang, Zhanhao Hu

entry.summary: TAKO demonstrates a stronger threat against robotic diffusion policies: instead of merely disrupting behavior, an attacker obtains a real-time steering interface over a frozen policy using a small vocabulary of universal adversarial patches. By switching patches in the camera stream, the attacker can compose arbitrary chosen trajectories.

entry.title: Attention Amnesia in Hybrid LLMs: When CoT Fine-Tuning Breaks Long-Range Recall, and How to Fix It

author.name: Xinyu Zhou, Boyu Zhu, Yi Xu, Zhiwei Li, Yingfa Chen, Huiming Wang, Zhijiang Guo

entry.summary: This work identifies that chain-of-thought SFT systematically degrades long-context recall in hybrid linear-attention models by biasing attention toward short-range patterns, and proposes a fix targeting query-key projections. It provides a concrete diagnosis and remedy with dramatic NIAH results.

entry.title: Recalling Too Well: Sycophancy Evaluation and Mitigation in Memory-Augmented Models

author.name: Shelly Bensal, Axel Magnuson, Aparna Balagopalan, Daniel M. Bikel

entry.summary: Shows that persistent memory systems systematically amplify sycophancy, introducing MIST, a benchmark of multi-turn conversations with plausible user misconceptions across scientific, medical, and moral domains. Finds up to 25x higher sycophancy rates with memory versus in-context baselines, tracing the cause to memory extraction.

entry.title: When Attribution Patching Lies: Diagnosis and a Second-Order Correction

author.name: Luyang Zhang, Jialu Wang

entry.summary: Diagnoses why attribution patching, a fast gradient-based approximation used in mechanistic interpretability, can be unreliable, identifying downstream network non-linearities as the dominant error source rather than local curvature. It proposes a second-order correction to improve circuit identification.

entry.title: A Theory on Flow Matching with Neural Networks

author.name: Yihan He, Qishuo Yin, Yuan Cao, Jianqing Fan, Han Liu

entry.summary: Develops theoretical foundations for flow matching with neural-network-parameterized conditional velocity fields, establishing gradient-descent convergence guarantees in the over-parameterized two-layer ReLU regime, generalization bounds, and Wasserstein-distance guarantees for generated samples. It also contributes a multi-task representation learning bound with unbounded losses.

entry.title: Catching One in Five: LLM-as-Judge Blind Spots in Production Multi-Turn Transaction Agents

author.name: Sawyer Zhang, Alexander Wang, Sophie Lei

entry.summary: This study measures how many genuine quality defects an LLM-as-judge catches in a deployed multi-turn food ordering agent, using exhaustive human review as ground truth. It finds the judge surfaces under a quarter of confirmed systematic problems, revealing structured (not random) blind spots in production evaluation.

entry.title: A Practical Recipe Towards Improving Sim-and-Real Correlation for VLA Evaluation

author.name: Shuo Wang, Hanyuan Xu, Yingdong Hu, Fanqi Lin, Yang Gao

entry.summary: This paper investigates sim-and-real correlation for evaluating vision-language-action policies, systematically studying whether simulated benchmarks preserve real-world conclusions about policy ranking and performance.
