It provides a practical recipe to improve the reliability of simulation as a proxy for costly real-robot evaluation.

entry.title: Harnessing the Collective Intelligence of AI Agents in the Wild for New Discoveries

author.name: Federico Bianchi, Yongchan Kwon, Aneesh Pappu, James Zou

entry.summary: EinsteinArena is an agent-native platform for open distributed research, providing AI agents with live open problems, verifiers, public leaderboards, and discussion forums to share insights and build on each other's work. It focuses on mathematical tasks to harness collective intelligence of agents toward new discoveries.

entry.title: Convergence of Monte Carlo Optimistic Policy Iteration: Beyond Uniform State-Action Updates

author.name: Octave Oliviers, Glenn Vinnicombe

entry.summary: This paper resolves a long-standing open question about the convergence of Monte Carlo optimistic policy iteration, proving that initial-visit MC-O-PI converges to optimality even when updates are uniform only over actions within each state, rather than over the full state-action space. This relaxes an impractical exploring-starts condition toward realistic implementations.

entry.title: Toward Secure LLM Agents: Threat Surfaces, Attacks, Defenses, and Evaluation

author.name: Yuchen Ling, Shengcheng Yu, Zhenyu Chen, Chunrong Fang

entry.summary: A systems-oriented survey synthesizing 247 papers on LLM agent security through a lifecycle framework covering threat surfaces, attacks, defenses, and evaluation. Highlights how agentic settings expand risks beyond unsafe text to control-flow hijacking, tool misuse, and state corruption.

entry.title: K-Forcing: Joint Next-K-Token Decoding via Push-Forward Language Modeling

author.name: Zhiwei Tang, Yuanyu He, Yizheng Han, Wangbo Zhao, Jiasheng Tang, Fan Wang, Bohan Zhuang

entry.summary: Introduces K-Forcing, a push-forward language modeling paradigm that distills an AR model into a mapping transforming uniform noise into joint samples of multiple future tokens in one forward pass. Targets acceleration of high-load batch serving rather than just latency.

entry.title: Mechanistic Analysis of Alignment Algorithms in Language Models

author.name: Aarush Sinha, Ishan Garg, Veeraraju Elluru, Arth Singh, Kushal Garg

entry.summary: Provides a systematic mechanistic analysis of six preference-optimization methods (PPO, DPO, SimPO, ORPO, GRPO, KTO) across three model families using layer-wise probing, sparse autoencoders, and crosscoders. Finds preference signals concentrate in early-mid or mid-late layers with distinct representational shifts per objective.

entry.title: GHOST: Hierarchical Sub-Goal Policies for Generalizing Robot Manipulation

author.name: Sriram Krishna, Ben Eisner, Haotian Zhan, Ying Yuan, Haoyu Zhen, Chuang Gan, Shubham Tulsiani, David Held

entry.summary: GHOST is a hierarchical framework for visuomotor robot manipulation that factorizes control into a high-level sub-goal policy predicting 3D end-effector poses and a low-level goal-conditioned controller. It uses a spatial heatmap interface to condition image policies on 3D goals and improves generalization beyond training distribution.

entry.title: Multi-Faceted Interactivity Alignment in Full-Duplex Speech Models

author.name: Atsumoto Ohashi, Neil Zeghidour, Alexandre D\'efossez, Eugene Kharitonov

entry.summary: This paper proposes an RL-based post-training alignment method that comprehensively improves interactivity in full-duplex spoken dialogue models across four canonical axes like turn-taking and silence. It moves beyond token-level likelihood training to optimize interaction-level behaviors.

entry.title: SpeechJBB: Probing Safety Alignment and Comprehension in Large Audio Language Models under Code-Switched Speech

author.name: Virginia Ceccatelli, Yejin Jeon, David Ifeoluwa Adelani

entry.summary: SpeechJBB introduces an audio jailbreak dataset to probe safety alignment of large audio language models under code-switched speech, including phonological obfuscation. It finds code-switched harmful audio achieves high jailbreak success across models.

entry.title: Using Probabilistic Programs to Train Inductive Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Liyi Zhang, Akshay K. Jagadish, Brenden M. Lake, Thomas L. Griffiths

entry.summary: Introduces Program-based Posterior Training, generating diverse open-world scenarios as probabilistic programs and running probabilistic inference to produce distributional targets for training inductive reasoning in LLMs. Addresses challenges in dataset curation and distributional targets for inductive tasks.

entry.title: A Controlled Audit of Pretraining Contamination in Public Medical Vision-Language Benchmarks

author.name: Bruce Changlong Xu, Lan Wu, Alexander Ryu

entry.summary: Conducts a controlled audit of pretraining contamination in public medical vision-language benchmarks using four detector families, finding measurable image-side source overlap on SLAKE-En that inflates reported accuracy. It challenges the assumption that benchmark examples were absent from pretraining.

entry.title: Expert-Level Crisis Detection in Mental Health Conversations

author.name: Grace Byun, Abigail Lott, Rebecca Lipschutz, Sean T. Minton, Elizabeth A. Stinson, Jinho D. Choi

entry.summary: This work introduces CRADLE-Dialogue, a clinician-annotated benchmark for turn-level crisis detection in mental health conversations, with 600 dialogues labeled across clinically grounded risks like suicide ideation and self-harm. It addresses the gap between static-text models and the conversational, evolving nature of real crisis intervention.

entry.title: Janus: A Benchmark for Goal-Conditioned Information Distortion in LLMs

author.name: Polydoros Giannouris, Mohsinul Kabir, Sophia Ananiadou

entry.summary: Introduces JANUS, a benchmark measuring goal-conditioned pragmatic distortion in LLMs—subtle misleading via selective emphasis or omission of true facts rather than outright lies. Compares neutral versus goal-conditioned outputs over fixed favorable/adverse fact pools.

entry.title: A Unifying Lens on Supervised Fine-Tuning Through Target Distribution Design

author.name: Tong Xie, Yuanhao Ban, Yunqi Hong, Sohyun An, Yihang Chen, Cho-Jui Hsieh

entry.summary: Reinterprets supervised fine-tuning as target distribution design via a Q-target framework that decomposes supervision into how strongly to trust the observed token and how to allocate remaining probability mass over alternatives. Provides a unifying lens on SFT beyond one-hot likelihood maximization.

entry.title: Dexterous Point Policy: Learning Point-based Dexterous Hand Policies from Human Demonstrations

author.name: Beomjun Kim, Seong Hyeon Park, Seunghoon Sim, Seungjun Moon, Sanghyeok Lee, Jinwoo Shin

entry.summary: Dexterous Point Policy learns multi-fingered dexterous manipulation policies directly from human demonstration videos with no robot demonstrations, using a unified 3D keypoint representation to bridge the human-robot embodiment gap. It addresses the prohibitive cost of dexterous robot data collection.

entry.title: Training LLMs to Enforce Multi-Level Instruction Hierarchies via Gravity-Weighted Direct Preference Optimization

author.name: Lena S. Bolliger, Lena A. J\"ager

entry.summary: This paper formalizes a k-level instruction hierarchy problem and uses gravity-weighted Direct Preference Optimization to train LLMs to enforce five-level priority relations, going beyond prior three or four level approaches. It addresses prompt injection and instruction conflict resolution.

entry.title: Harmfulness Directions in OLMo

author.name: Daniele Pace

entry.summary: This technical report treats model harmfulness as a composition of subcategories and tracks linear activation directions for each across OLMo's training, measuring their geometric relationships and validating them with AUROC and steering vectors. The key findings are that harmfulness subcategories do not collapse to a single direction but form a structured shared space, and that in-distribution AUROC can be misleading without careful out-of-distribution evaluation. It matters for interpretability-based safety monitoring and concept-extraction methods.

entry.title: A Mike's-Eye View of ARC's Research

author.name: Mikewins

entry.summary: An updated overview of the Alignment Research Center's technical agenda, centered on the Matching Sampling Principle (MSP) and a pipeline that monitors training to detect added structure, converts it into advice for a mechanistic estimator of model behavior, and uses the estimator to bound safety-relevant quantities. It gives a current insider view of ARC's theory-driven approach to verifying advanced AI.

entry.title: When the Chain of Thought Knows Better: Failure Modes in Multi-Turn Reasoning Models

author.name: Sai Kartheek Reddy Kasu, Nils Lukas, Samuele Poppi

entry.summary: Proposes a CoT-Output 2x2 safety matrix to diagnose hidden temporal failure modes in multi-turn reasoning models, distinguishing internal reasoning from visible output. Identifies context-injection failure where safe CoT still yields harmful output.

entry.title: Time Series as Language: A Universal Tokenizer for General-Purpose Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Yunhao Zhang, Ruiying Qi, Jiale Zheng, Jianfeng Zhang, Lujia Pan, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: Introduces UniTok, a universal vector-quantized tokenizer that converts continuous time series into discrete tokens, plus UniTok-FM, a foundation model pretrained via next-token prediction on those tokens. It supports zero-shot forecasting and in-context few-shot generation and classification, extending the LLM paradigm to time series.

entry.title: TD-Grokking: Learning from Zero-Reward Problems by Training-Time Decomposition

author.name: Ningyuan Xi, Hao Xu, Hongsheng Xin, Ning Miao

entry.summary: Introduces TD-Grokking, a training-time decomposition method that enables LLMs to learn from zero-reward problems in RLVR, where all sampled trajectories fail and provide no optimization signal. It decomposes intractable problems to equip the policy with capabilities needed to eventually solve them.

entry.title: Flow Control: Steering Vision-Language-Action Models with Simple Real-Time Inputs

author.name: Jonathan C. Kao, Jason Chan, Andy Wang

entry.summary: Flow Control introduces a way to steer vision-language-action robot models in real time using simple inputs like a keyboard, without retraining or fine-tuning. The method maps crude user inputs to high-quality action samples from the learned expert distribution, enabling intuitive human guidance of robot behavior.

entry.title: SHAPO: Sharpness-Aware Policy Optimization for Safe Exploration

author.name: Kaustubh Mani, Yann Pequignot, Vincent Mai, Liam Paull

entry.summary: SHAPO is a sharpness-aware policy optimization method for safe exploration in reinforcement learning, using the policy's sensitivity to parameter perturbations as a proxy for epistemic uncertainty. It makes updates pessimistic in uncertain regions, analytically amplifying the influence of rare unsafe actions to bias learning toward safety.

entry.title: Routing-Aware Expert Calibration for Machine Unlearning in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models

author.name: Jingyi Xie, Yijun Lin, Yinjiang Xiong, Zhikun Zhang, Sai Li

entry.summary: TRACE is a routing-aware calibration method for machine unlearning in Mixture-of-Experts language models, addressing the underexplored problem of forget-retain routing mismatch. It detects forget-critical experts from activation statistics and calibrates them to remove targeted knowledge without over-regularizing experts that retain useful information.

entry.title: Achieving Cloud-Grade SLOs for Local Mixture-of-Experts Inference through CPU-GPU Hybrid Design

author.name: Wenxin Wang, Yule Hou, Yu Ji, Peng Qu, Youhui Zhang

entry.summary: This paper presents a CPU-GPU hybrid system achieving cloud-grade service-level objectives for local Mixture-of-Experts inference on commodity hardware. Through stream-loading prefill and distributed techniques, it boosts prefill throughput, enables 32K prompts within 30 seconds, and improves decode throughput on dual-socket CPUs and consumer GPUs.

entry.title: LC-QAT: Data-Efficient 2-Bit QAT for LLMs via Linear-Constrained Vector Quantization

author.name: Haoyu Wang, Xingyu Yu, Haiyan Zhao, Fengxiang Wang, Xu Han

entry.summary: LC-QAT is a data-efficient 2-bit quantization-aware training framework for LLMs that represents quantized weights via a learned affine mapping over discrete vectors, combining vector quantization's representational capacity with end-to-end differentiability. It avoids explicit codebook lookups while yielding a high-quality post-training initialization.

entry.title: Towards Diverse Scientific Hypothesis Search with Large Language Models

author.name: Haorui Wang, Parshin Shojaee, Kazem Meidani, Kunyang Sun, Jos\'e Miguel Hern\'andez-Lobato, Teresa Head-Gordon, Jiajun He, Chandan K. Reddy, Chao Zhang, Yuanqi Du

entry.summary: This paper reformulates LLM-driven scientific hypothesis generation as a sampling problem to produce diverse high-quality alternatives, countering the diversity collapse caused by selection pressure in evolutionary search. It aims to provide a set of hypotheses that hedge against downstream validation uncertainty rather than a single best one.

entry.title: Fast and Highly Expressive Policy Learning for Offline Reinforcement Learning via Bootstrapped Flow Q-Learning

author.name: Thanh Nguyen, Tri Ton, Hongbin Choe, Tung M. Luu, Chang D. Yoo

entry.summary: Bootstrapped Flow Q-Learning enables accurate single-step action generation for offline reinforcement learning without auxiliary networks, distillation, or multi-phase training, overcoming the computational cost of multi-step diffusion Q-learning. It uses a divide-and-conquer view of displacement to achieve fast and expressive policy learning.

entry.title: Dynamic Linear Attention

author.name: Xin Wang, Hui Shen, Boyuan Zheng, Xueshen Liu, Minkyoung Cho, Zhongwei Wan, Zesen Zhao, Zhuoqing Mao, Shen Yan, Mi Zhang

entry.summary: Dynamic Linear Attention introduces an information-aware dynamic memory framework for multi-state linear attention, replacing fixed state-merging policies that irreversibly obscure critical tokens over long sequences. It adapts memory management to dynamically varying token importance to reduce error accumulation in long-context processing.

entry.title: Decentralized Multi-Agent Systems with Shared Context

author.name: Yuzhen Mao, Azalia Mirhoseini

entry.summary: Presents DeLM, a decentralized multi-agent LLM framework that replaces centralized orchestration with parallel agents coordinating through a shared verified context and task queue. Aims to remove the controller bottleneck as subtask counts grow.

entry.title: PhantomBench: Benchmarking the Non-existential Threat of Language Models

author.name: Haeji Jung, Hila Gonen

entry.summary: Introduces PhantomBench, a large-scale benchmark of 60K+ non-existent terms and entities derived from real concepts to test whether LMs recognize the limits of their knowledge. Evaluates 21 models and reports staggeringly high hallucination rates.

entry.title: From Confident Closing to Silent Failure: Characterizing False Success in LLM Agents

author.name: Laksh Advani

entry.summary: Characterizes false success in LLM agents—asserting completion when the environment shows otherwise—across two benchmarks (9,876 tau2-bench and 1,879 AppWorld trajectories). Finds false success is common and that LLM judges fail to detect it reliably (AUROC at or below 0.65).

entry.title: Gradient-Guided Reward Optimization for Inference-time Alignment

author.name: Hankun Lin, Ruqi Zhang

entry.summary: GGRO is a lightweight inference-time alignment method that uses token-level entropy to identify high-uncertainty positions and applies gradient guidance for minimal intervention during decoding. It aims to overcome the limitations of Best-of-N and rejection sampling, which are bounded by base model quality and vulnerable to reward hacking.

entry.title: Efficient AI-Inspired Reduction of Feynman Integrals via Tube Seeding

author.name: Justin Berman, Francois Charton, Andres Luna, Matthias Wilhelm, Mao Zeng

entry.summary: This work uses machine learning to discover a new seeding strategy (tube seeding) for integration-by-parts reduction of Feynman integrals, allowing seed selection to grow only linearly with numerator power rather than polynomially. It addresses a major bottleneck in theoretical particle and gravitational-wave physics calculations.

entry.title: MemVenom: Triggered Poisoning of Multimodal Memories in Web Agents

author.name: Yv Zhang, Hao Sun, Hao Fang, Kuofeng Gao, Fan Mo, Bin Chen, Shu-Tao Xia, Yaowei Wang

entry.summary: MemVenom is a black-box attack framework that poisons graph-structured external memory of web agents with coordinated text-image evidence, using a trigger-conditioned retrieval attack to ensure high-probability recall of malicious content. It systematically studies multimodal memory poisoning as an overlooked attack surface.

entry.title: KCSAT-ML: Probing Reasoning Models with Nationwide-Cohort Human Difficulty

author.name: Sanghee Park, Geewook Kim, Kee-Eung Kim

entry.summary: KCSAT-ML is a benchmark of 664 Korean college entrance exam math problems with official per-item error rates from nationwide cohorts, paired with a Difficulty-aligned Reasoning Gain metric. It probes whether model mistakes concentrate on items humans found hard versus easy across many VLMs and LLMs.

entry.title: Benchmarking and Exploring the Capabilities of LLMs for Attack Investigations

author.name: Aniket Anand, Yiwei Hou, Daniel Fields, Alex Kantchelian, David Tao, Kurt Thomas, Grant Ho

entry.summary: AuditBench is a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on security audit log investigation tasks across Linux and Windows systems and over 50 scenarios, used to assess five frontier models. It probes LLM capabilities for incident response and attack investigation.

entry.title: ABot-Earth 0.5: Generative 3D Earth Model

author.name: Ming Qian, Tianjian Ouyang, Mingchao Sun, Zijian Wang, Jincheng Xiong, Jiarong Han, Yongchang Zhang, Jiawei Zhang, Xu Wang, Yu Liu, Luyang Tang, Fei Yu, Zengye Ge, Mengmeng Du, Yuan Liu, Nianfei Fan, Song Wang, Yingliang Peng, Chunxue Jia, Yang Liu, Shiying Zeng, Haozhe Shi, Junnan Lai, Hongyu Pan, Zheng Wu, Ning Guo, Mu Xu, Hang Zhang

entry.summary: ABot-Earth 0.5 is a generative 3D framework that synthesizes seamless 3D environments from satellite imagery using a model formulated directly with 3D Gaussian Splatting, scaling to under 10 minutes per square kilometer. It includes hierarchical level-of-detail for real-time rendering.

entry.title: ARM: An AutoRegressive Large Multimodal Model with Unified Discrete Representations

author.name: Junke Wang, Xiao Wang, Jiacheng Pan, Xuefeng Hu, Feng Li, Jingxiang Sun, Chaorui Deng, Zilong Chen, Yunpeng Chen, Kaibin Tian, Matthew Gwilliam, Hao Chen, Danhui Guan, Kun Xu, Weilin Huang, Zuxuan Wu, Haoqi Fan, Yu-Gang Jiang, Zhenheng Yang

entry.summary: Introduces ARM, a 7B discrete-representation autoregressive multimodal model unifying image understanding, generation, and editing via next-token prediction over a jointly supervised semantic visual tokenizer. Adds preference alignment for improved behavior.

entry.title: A Mike's-Eye View of ARC's Research

author.name: Mikewins

entry.summary: This is the AI Alignment Forum cross-post of the same updated overview of ARC's technical agenda built around the Matching Sampling Principle, describing the pipeline from detecting structure during training to producing safety-relevant behavior bounds. Content is identical to the LessWrong version.

entry.title: Sample Where You Struggle: Sharpening Base Model Reasoning via Entropy-Guided Power Sampling

author.name: Hong Guo, Nianhui Guo, Christoph Meinel, Haojin Yang

entry.summary: Proposes Entropy-Guided Power Sampling, a training-free and verifier-free sampler that elicits RL-level reasoning from base LLMs by targeting resampling at sparse high-entropy decision points where the power distribution diverges from the base. It improves on slow-mixing Metropolis-Hastings without parameter updates.

entry.title: Interpreting and Steering a Text-to-Speech Language Model with Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Nikita Koriagin, Georgii Aparin, Nikita Balagansky, Daniil Gavrilov

entry.summary: Trains BatchTopK sparse autoencoders on the LM backbone of a text-to-speech model and introduces a modality-aware auto-interpretation pipeline, recovering interpretable features for phonemes, laughter, accent, and speaker gender. Steering interventions causally control attributes like raising laughter probability and flipping perceived gender.

entry.title: Effective Reinforcement Learning for Agentic Search by Recycling Zero-Variance Queries During Training

author.name: Jo\~ao Coelho, Jo\~ao Magalh\~aes, Bruno Martins, Chenyan Xiong

entry.summary: Proposes query recycling for GRPO-style agentic search RL, returning zero-variance rollout groups to a mutable pool for resampling since queries flip between informative and zero-variance states as the policy evolves. Improves rollout efficiency in outcome-only reward training.

entry.title: Beyond Uniform Token-Level Trust Region in LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Renjie Mao, Xiangxin Zhou, Lvfang Tao, Yixin Ding, Yu Shi, Yongguang Lin, Yuheng Wu, Honglin Zhu, Qian Qiu, Wenxi Zhu

entry.summary: Argues that uniform token-level trust regions in PPO-style RLVR conflict with autoregressive generation, since early deviations compound and cumulative prefix drift is ignored. Proposes position-aware, drift-sensitive trust-region mechanisms for LLM reasoning RL.

entry.title: Piper: A Programmable Distributed Training System

author.name: Megan Frisella, Shubham Tiwari, Andy Ruan, Yi Pan, Parker Gustafson, Mat Jacob, Gilbert Bernstein, Stephanie Wang

entry.summary: Presents Piper, a user-controllable distributed training system that decouples high-level parallelism strategy from low-level execution to flexibly compose data, pipeline, expert parallelism and ZeRO. Aims to ease integration of state-of-the-art parallelism strategies without manual reimplementation.

entry.title: Prefilling-dLLM: Predictive Prefilling for Long-Context Inference in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Jing Xiong, Qi Han, Shansan Gong, Yunta Hsieh, Chengyue Wu, Chaofan Tao, Chenyang Zhao, Ngai Wong

entry.summary: Prefilling-dLLM is a training-free prefill-decode disaggregation framework for diffusion language models that partitions the prefix into chunks, caches KV representations once, and selects top-K relevant chunks for decoding. It reduces per-step complexity from quadratic in full sequence length to quadratic only in decode length for long-context inference.

entry.title: Are We Evaluating Knowledge or Phrasing? Mitigating MCQA Sensitivity with ParaEval

author.name: Jo\~ao Maria Janeiro, Mathurin Videau, Andrea Caciolai, Benjamin Piwowarski, Patrick Gallinari, Loic Barrault

entry.summary: ParaEval is an evaluation framework that queries models using multiple paraphrases per MCQA answer option, scoring each model by its most favorable phrasing to disentangle knowledge from surface-form sensitivity. It demonstrates that standard log-likelihood scoring falsely reports performance gaps between models with identical knowledge.

entry.title: 5% > 100%: Flatness Preference is All You Need for Multimodal Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning

author.name: Yifan Zhu, Can Lin, Hangjie Yuan, Zixiang Zhao, Pengfei Zhang, Tao Feng, Zhonghong Ou

entry.summary: This paper reveals a flatness preference across various parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods, where a small fraction of sharp dimensions dominates generalization, suggesting one can achieve better generalization by attending to just these dimensions. It offers insights into PEFT generalization mechanisms for multimodal models.

entry.title: Supervised Fine-tuning with Synthetic Rationale Data Hurts Real-World Disease Prediction

author.name: Buxin Su, Bingxuan Li, Cheng Qian, Yiwei Wang, Jin Jin, Bingxin Zhao

entry.summary: Tests the common assumption that synthetic rationale fine-tuning improves clinical prediction, finding it consistently and substantially hurts five-year dementia prediction relative to label-only training. The degradation persists across model families and is not due to poor rationale quality.

entry.title: ComBench: A Benchmark for Rigorous Proof Reasoning and Constructive Realization in Olympiad-Level Combinatorics

author.name: Shunkai Zhang, Haoran Zhang, Yun Luo, Qianjia Cheng, Haodi Lei, Yizhuo Li, Runzhe Zhan, Zhilin Wang, Bangjie Xu, Yucheng Su, Xinmiao Han, Xiaoye Qu, Dongrui Liu, Zhouchen Lin, Yu Qiao, Ning Ding, Yafu Li, Yu Cheng

entry.summary: Introduces ComBench, an Olympiad-level combinatorics benchmark of 100 human-annotated problems split into analysis-centric and construction-centric settings to diagnose LLM combinatorial reasoning. Reveals gaps in creative mathematical reasoning of frontier models.

entry.title: The Arbiter Agent: Continually Monitoring Multi-Agent Conversations to Detect Emergent Misalignment

author.name: Filippo Tonini, Federico Torrielli, Anton Danholt Lautrup, Peter Schneider-Kamp, Mustafa Mert \c{C}elikok, Lukas Galke Poech

entry.summary: Introduces the Arbiter, an agent that monitors multi-agent conversations in real time under a limited inspection budget to detect emergent misalignment arising from agent interactions. Decides when to wait, question participants, or examine internal information.

entry.title: What Fits (Into Few Tokens) Doesn't Overfit: Compression and Generalization in ML Research Agents

author.name: Martin Andres Bertran, Aaron Roth, Zhiwei Steven Wu

entry.summary: Studies why benchmark-driven ML shows little overfitting despite adaptive reuse, hypothesizing successful strategies are highly compressible and testing this via output and input information bottlenecks with LLM research agents. Examines whether a reproducer agent can match performance from extremely short prompts.

entry.title: The Interlocutor Effect: Why LLMs Leak More Personal Data to Agents Than Humans

author.name: Faouzi El Yagoubi, Godwin Badu-Marfo, Ranwa Al Mallah

entry.summary: Documents the Interlocutor Effect whereby LLMs leak more personal data to AI agents than to humans, and proposes the Attention Suppression Hypothesis that safety-aligned attention heads deactivate during agent interactions. Provides ablation and quantitative analysis of this privacy vulnerability.

entry.title: Blurry Window Attention

author.name: Axel Laborieux, Christos Sourmpis, Juan Gabriel Kostelec, Qinghai Guo

entry.summary: Introduces Blurry Window Attention, a bounded-memory attention mechanism inspired by state-space models that stores a frequency window to improve retrieval and recall in linear-complexity architectures. It aims to close the gap between efficient linear models and Transformers on recall-heavy tasks.

entry.title: SD-GRPO: Verifiable Segment Decomposition for Long-Form Vision-Language Generation

author.name: Hyunwoong Kim, Seongeun Lee, Hannah Yun, Junhyun Park, Jonggwon Park

entry.summary: Proposes SD-GRPO, which decomposes long-form vision-language outputs into segments and assigns per-segment verifiable rewards rather than a single scalar advantage, improving credit assignment for multimodal RL. It exploits natural segmentation that holistic GRPO formulations discard.

entry.title: Integrating Local and Global Entropy for Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs

author.name: Johanne Medina, Tianyi Zhou, Keivin Isufaj, Aristides Gionis, Sanjay Chawla

entry.summary: Proposes integrating hidden-state geometric entropy (global uncertainty) with token-level entropy (local uncertainty) for LLM uncertainty quantification, showing the two signals are near-orthogonal and capture distinct failure modes. The global geometry recovers confident-but-wrong errors that token signals miss.

entry.title: A Note on the Strategic Confinement Problem

author.name: Christian Schroeder de Witt

entry.summary: Introduces the strategic confinement problem, extending Lampson's classical confinement to strategic agents with shared coordination resources, showing that bounds on information leakage do not bound worst-case harm. It argues learnt strategic agent systems naturally instantiate this risk.

entry.title: Interactions Between Crosscoder Features: A Compact Proofs Perspective

author.name: Dmitry Manning-Coe, Thomas Read, Anna Soligo, Oliver Clive-Griffin, Chun-Hei Yip, Rajashree Agrawal, Jason Gross

entry.summary: Formalizes interactions between crosscoder features in dictionary-learning interpretability via compact proofs, showing how feature interactions induce reconstruction errors and providing an explicit interaction measure for MLP layers. It offers three applications of the interaction metric.

entry.title: GAGI: A Gini-Adjusted GDP-per-Capita Index for Distribution-Aware Macroeconomic Welfare Monitoring

author.name: Sivasathivel Kandasamy

entry.summary: Introduces IDP-Bench, the first LLM benchmark for interdependent privacy scenarios, grounded in Contextual Integrity, where one person's data can be revealed through others. Evaluation of eight open models finds strong co-ownership recognition but persistent weaknesses in nuanced IDP reasoning.

entry.title: 3SPO: State-Score-Supervised Policy Optimization for LLM Agents

author.name: Yu Han, Kailing Li, Yang Jiao, Yulin Dai, Yuqian Fu, Linhai Zhuo, Tianwen Qian

entry.summary: Proposes 3SPO, a reinforcement learning algorithm for LLM agents that performs post-step policy optimization with dynamic state-score supervision instead of trajectory-level updates, addressing sparse delayed rewards and per-step credit assignment in multi-turn settings. It computes state scores from history at each step.

entry.title: Unsupervised Style Representation Learning for AI-Text Detection via Paraphrase Inversion

author.name: Rafael Rivera Soto, Barry Chen, Nicholas Andrews

entry.summary: Learns discriminative writing-style features for AI-text detection without authorship labels by training a style encoder to reconstruct human-authored text from its machine paraphrase. The resulting unsupervised style representations are robust to adversarial attacks and avoid the few-shot in-distribution requirements of prior detectors.

entry.title: $\tau$-Rec: A Verifiable Benchmark for Agentic Recommender Systems

author.name: Bharath Sivaram Narasimhan, Karthik R Narasimhan

entry.summary: Introduces tau-Rec, a benchmark for agentic recommender systems that replaces subjective LLM-as-a-judge evaluation with verifiable rewards and a reveal-tagged elicitation mechanism controlling how task constraints surface during dialogue. It uses structured catalog predicates and a pass-k reliability metric across model families including GPT-5.4 and Claude Sonnet.

entry.title: MMClima: A Framework for Multimodal Climate Science Data and Evaluation

author.name: Muhammad Umer Sheikh, Hassan Abid, Khawar Shehzad, Ufaq Khan, Muhammad Haris Khan

entry.summary: MMClima is a large-scale multimodal climate science QA framework with over 104k expert-validated question-answer pairs spanning articles, video transcriptions, and figures across five climate domains. It enables benchmarking of multimodal LLMs on factual recall, visual interpretation, and cross-modal synthesis for climate research.

entry.title: Fisher-Guided Progressive Parameter Selection for Adaptive Fine-Tuning

author.name: Ghodsiyeh Rostami, Po-Han Chen, Mahdi S. Hosseini

entry.summary: FisherAdapTune is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that dynamically selects which parameter groups to train by tracking the temporal drift of their Fisher information geometry. Grounded in a PAC-Bayesian generalization bound, it freezes parameter groups whose curvature contribution has stabilized to reduce error without disrupting adaptation.

entry.title: YUBI: Yielding Universal Bidigital Interface for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation at Scale

author.name: Takehiko Ohkawa, Jumpei Arima, Yuki Noguchi, Masatoshi Tateno, Makoto Sugiura, Takuya Okubo, Kengo Ikeuchi, Yuma Shin, Hiroki Nishizawa, Naoaki Kanazawa, Yuki Wakayama, Daiki Fukunaga, Koshi Makihara, Tomohiro Motoda, Floris Erich, Yukiyasu Domae, Tatsuya Matsushima, Yohishiro Okumatsu, Kei Ota

entry.summary: YUBI is a finger-aligned gripper for intuitive, ergonomic, and scalable data collection in bimanual dexterous manipulation, improving on bulky pistol-grip designs like UMI. It directly maps human finger movements to gripper jaw motion and integrates VR-based 6-DoF tracking for high-fidelity trajectory data.

entry.title: Hierarchical Policies from Verbal and Egocentric Human Signals for Natural Human-Robot Interaction

author.name: Dongjun Lee, Juheon Choi, Dong Kyu Shin, Sinjae Kang, Kimin Lee

entry.summary: EDITH is a robot framework that captures human nonverbal signals (first-person view and gaze from smart glasses) alongside language to infer intent for natural human-robot interaction. It streams view, gaze, and speech to the robot in real time and uses hierarchical policies to act on multimodal human signals.

entry.title: FOGO: Forgetting-aware Orthogonalization Optimizer

author.name: Toan Nguyen, Yang Liu, Trung Le, Celso de Melo, Flora D. Salim

entry.summary: FOGO is a scalable optimizer arguing that forgetting is a general optimization phenomenon where dominant mini-batch gradients suppress rare useful update directions. It spectrally orthogonalizes momentum updates and stores past directions in a compact codebook to continuously detect and resolve gradient interference.

entry.title: LakeQA: An Exploratory QA Benchmark over a Million-Scale Data Lake

author.name: Haonan Wang, Jiaxiang Liu, Yurong Liu, Austin Senna Wijaya, Tianle Zhou, Eden Wu, Yijia Chen, Wanting You, Reya Vir, Daniela Pinto, Grace Fan, Yusen Zhang, Juliana Freire, Eugene Wu

entry.summary: LakeQA is a benchmark for search-centric question answering over million-scale data lakes (about 9.5 TB), requiring both searching for evidence and reasoning over it rather than relying on provided documents. It addresses the gap between reading-based QA and real-world questions where useful evidence must first be located.

entry.title: Stop Early, Spend Less: Hidden-State Probes as a Practical Recipe for Streaming Moderation of LLM Outputs

author.name: Huizhen Shu, Xuying Li, Piao Xue

entry.summary: This work trains lightweight token-level probes on LLM hidden-state activations to detect unsafe content during generation, enabling sub-millisecond per-token safety checks without an extra forward pass. The approach allows early stopping and online intervention, halving the cost of separate post-generation moderation models.

entry.title: Flexible Flows for Biological Sequence Design

author.name: Yogesh Verma, Dani Korpela, Harri L\"ahdesm\"aki, Vikas Garg

entry.summary: This work improves discrete flow matching for biological sequence design by introducing structured couplings that encode domain-specific preferences among sequence elements, biasing the source distribution without modifying the flow objective. A latent edit-based rate parameterization enables variable-length generation and fine-grained control.

entry.title: Hidden Consensus:Preference-Validity Compression in Human Feedback

author.name: Dorcas Chia Ern Chua, Karen Myn Hui Lee, Jia Yue Tan, Zhen Xue Gue, Norzalena Abdul Hamid, Azima Binti Azmi, Keat Mei Yeong, Aizat Izyani binti Mujab, Hafsah Noor Azam, Chee Guo Khoo, Han Ying Lim, Chee Seng Chan

entry.summary: This paper argues that standard RLHF compresses heterogeneous, culturally-grounded human judgments into a single scalar reward, a failure called Preference-Validity Compression. Using Malaysia as a diagnostic setting, it analyzes preference events across interpretive frames to show how plural-valid responses collapse into a single optimization target.

entry.title: Embedding Hybrid Systems into Continuous Latent Vector Fields

author.name: Sangli Teng, Hang Liu, Koushil Sreenath

entry.summary: This work proves that an n-dimensional hybrid system can be embedded into Euclidean space with a continuous vector field whenever the dimension exceeds 2n, showing that discontinuous hybrid systems admit continuous representations suitable for differentiable optimization. It then uses a latent Neural ODE with consistency loss to accurately recover hybrid system flows from time-series data.

entry.title: Causal Ensemble Agent: Hierarchical Causal Discovery with LLM-guided Expert Reweighting

author.name: Xinyu Li, Yuanyuan Wang, Haoxuan Li, Chuan Zhou, Erdun Gao, Bo Han, Tongliang Liu, Kun Zhang, Howard Bondell, Mingming Gong

entry.summary: Causal Ensemble Agent uses LLM-guided hierarchical reweighting to reconcile divergent results from different causal discovery algorithms, incorporating domain-specific feature descriptions alongside numerical data. It addresses the unreliability of direct LLM causal queries by aligning expert reweighting with the actual data.

entry.title: UniDexTok: A Unified Dexterous Hand Tokenizer from Real Data

author.name: Dong Fang, Youjun Wu, Yuanxin Zhong, Rui Zhang, Yunlong Wang, Xiaosong Jia, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces UDHM, a unified 22-DoF semantic interface mapping human and robot hand states, and UniDexTok, a retargeting-free tokenizer producing embodiment-conditioned discrete tokens for dexterous manipulation. Aims to unify fragmented dexterous-hand data for joint training.

entry.title: Beyond APIs: Probing the Limits of MLLMs in Physical Tool Use

author.name: Zhixin Ma, Yutong Zhou, Yongqi Li, Chong-Wah Ngo, Wenjie Li

entry.summary: Introduces PhysTool-Bench, the first benchmark for evaluating MLLMs on physical tool use, with 2,510 queries over 2,678 real-world tools spanning diverse domains. Probes whether MLLMs serving as embodied AI brains can identify and plan physical tool use.

entry.title: Optimal Post-Training Quantization Scales and Where to Find Them

author.name: Juan Amboage, Pablo Monteagudo-Lago, Ian Colbert, Giuseppe Franco, Nicholas Fraser

entry.summary: Presents PiSO, an algorithm that uses calibration data to compute optimal channel-wise weight quantization scales exactly via piecewise interval minimization under round-to-nearest. Extends to group-wise quantization and interleaves with error correction, tested on Llama.

entry.title: Unifying Local Communications and Local Updates for LLM Pretraining

author.name: Pietro Cagnasso, Eugene Belilovsky, Edouard Oyallon

entry.summary: Introduces GASLoC, a decentralized LLM pretraining algorithm generalizing communication acceleration via outer optimizers into a gossip-based framework compatible with adaptive optimizers, local steps, and sparse communication. Targets heterogeneous-bandwidth distributed training.

entry.title: TRACE: A Unified Rollout Budget Allocation Framework for Efficient Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Heming Zou, Qi Wang, Yun Qu, Yuhang Jiang, Lizhou Cai, Yixiu Mao, Ru Peng, Xin Xu, Weijie Liu, Kai Yang, Saiyong Yang, Xiangyang Ji

entry.summary: Proposes TRACE, a unified rollout budget allocation framework for multi-turn agentic RL that models prefix-level informativeness across turns rather than only prompt-level, addressing insufficient reward contrast in RLVR. Targets credit assignment in ReAct-style rollouts.

entry.title: SynIB: Informational Bottleneck for Maximizing Synergy in Multimodal Learning

author.name: Konstantinos Kontras, Teodora Gagaleska, Thomas Strypsteen, Christos Chatzichristos, Matthew Blaschko, Maarten De Vos, Paul Pu Liang

entry.summary: Introduces SynIB, a Synergistic Information Bottleneck objective that directly targets task-relevant information arising only from joint use of multiple modalities, complementing architectural fusion approaches. Formalizes multimodal synergy via information theory.

entry.title: ASTRA-sim 3.0: Next-Level Distributed Machine Learning Simulations via High-Fidelity GPU and Infrastructure Modeling

author.name: William Won, Jinsun Yoo, Tuan Ta, Moumita Dey, Andy Balogh, Pradosh Datta, Furkan Eris, Conor Green, Winston Liu, Changhai Man, Kingshuk Mandal, Amos Rai, Vinay Ramakrishnaiah, Ruchi Shah, David Sidler, Harsh Sikhwal, Hanjiang Wu, Tushar Krishna, Bradford M. Beckmann

entry.summary: ASTRA-sim 3.0 augments the open-source distributed ML simulator with high-fidelity GPU and infrastructure modeling, enabling fine-grained simulation of latency-sensitive collective communication. It provides a standardized infrastructure representation for distributed ML systems, increasingly important for large-scale inference.

entry.title: Density Field State Space Models: 1-Bit Distillation, Efficient Inference, and Knowledge Organization in Mamba-2

author.name: Chirag Shinde

entry.summary: DF-SSM compresses Mamba-2 state space models to a 1-bit scaffold with int8 low-rank correction, achieving a 9.7x smaller model and 21.4x faster inference while staying within 2-4 points of baseline performance. Distillation requires only 32M tokens and 6 hours on a single A100.

entry.title: Do Vision-Language Models See or Guess? Measuring and Reducing Textual-Prior Reliance with a Phrasing-Controlled Benchmark

author.name: Pratham Singla, Shivank Garg, Vihan Singh, Paras Chopra

entry.summary: This work builds a phrasing-controlled benchmark of 540 images with four question variants to isolate whether VLMs answer from image content or textual priors. It measures and proposes methods to reduce reliance on memorized world knowledge and question phrasing.

entry.title: UniSVQ: 2-bit Unified Scalar-Vector Quantization

author.name: Haoyu Wang, Haiyan Zhao, Xingyu Yu, Zhangyang Yao, Xu Han, Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: UniSVQ is a unified 2-bit quantization framework that bridges scalar and vector quantization by parameterizing codewords as affine transforms of integer lattices, preserving integer-kernel compatibility while retaining VQ flexibility. A data-driven block-wise fine-tuning strategy minimizes quantization reconstruction error.

entry.title: Continual LLM Upcycling: A Predictor-Gated Bank-Wise Sparsity Training Recipe for Dense-to-Sparse LLMs

author.name: Ruixuan Huang, Jinyuan Shi, Hantao Huang, Yifan Huang, Ziyi Guan, Hao Zeng, Ian En-Hsu Yen, Minghui Yu

entry.summary: This work proposes a continual training recipe to convert dense LLMs into channel-sparse models using a predictor-gated bank-wise sparse FFN, achieving 4x activation sparsity while keeping routing on the main path. It targets hardware-oriented efficient inference via dense-to-sparse upcycling.

entry.title: RedAct: Redacting Agent Capability Traces for Procedural Skill Protection

author.name: Shuwen Xu (May), Zhitao He (May), Yi R. (May), Fung

entry.summary: RedAct introduces a framework for redacting agent execution traces to protect proprietary procedural skills, along with CapTraceBench, a benchmark of long-horizon tasks and curated skills across seven domains. It quantifies the risk of skill leakage from observable traces.

entry.title: Data Journalist Agent: Transforming Data into Verifiable Multimodal Stories

author.name: Kevin Qinghong Lin, Batu EI, Yuhong Shi, Pan Lu, Philip Torr, James Zou

entry.summary: Data2Story is a multi-agent framework that acts as an end-to-end data journalist, orchestrating specialized roles to turn raw data into evidence-grounded multimodal stories with an Inspector linking every claim back to data and code. It targets verifiable automated data journalism.

entry.title: 3D-CoS: A New 3D Reconstruction Paradigm Based on VLM Code Synthesis

author.name: Yuhao Wang, Puyi Wang, Linjie Li, Zhengyuan Yang, Kevin Qinghong Lin, Yu Cheng

entry.summary: 3D-CoS proposes a new 3D reconstruction paradigm where assets are constructed as executable Blender code, providing a programmatic and interpretable medium, and evaluates VLMs on code-based reconstruction under a unified protocol. It explores controllable, editable 3D representation via code synthesis.

entry.title: LAFP: Preserving Latent Action Structure in Latent Policy Learning via Flow Matching

author.name: Jiexi Lyu, Xizhou Bu, Qingqiu Huang, Chufeng Tang, Xiaoshuai Hao, Hongbo Wang, Wei Li

entry.summary: LAFP (Latent Action Flow Policy) preserves latent action structure in latent policy learning by using flow matching while addressing misalignment between latent and physical actions during decoder training. It avoids the modal collapse of behavior cloning for scalable policy learning from unlabeled video.

entry.title: FadeMem: Distance-Aware Memory Consolidation for Autoregressive Video Diffusion

author.name: Yu Lu, Junjie Yang, Piotr Koniusz, YuXin Song, Yi Yang

entry.summary: FadeMem is a distance-aware KV memory consolidation mechanism for autoregressive video diffusion that organizes historical KV blocks into a temporal hierarchy under a fixed cache budget, motivated by frequency-dependent temporal decay. It enables efficient long-video generation.

entry.title: From Patches to Patients: A study of the tile-to-slide performance transferability in Digital Pathology

author.name: Sofi\`ene Boutaj, Leo Fillioux, Maria Vakalopoulou, Stergios Christodoulidis, Pierre Marza

entry.summary: This study investigates whether efficient tile-level linear probing can serve as a reliable proxy for slide-level performance in digital pathology, benchmarking 19 foundation models across 42 slide-level and 16 tile-level tasks. It aims to reduce costly per-model slide-level pipelines for encoder selection.

entry.title: The consequences of relying on AI for accurate news

author.name: Adam Conner-Simons | MIT Media Lab

entry.summary: An MIT Media Lab open-access study finds that people who relied on AI systems to verify facts over a month became worse at detecting misinformation on their own once the chatbots were removed, an instance of the AI dependency paradox and broader cognitive-offloading/deskilling trend. It has direct implications given that growing shares of teens and young adults use LLMs for news.

entry.title: Earth-OneVision: Extending Remote Sensing Multimodal Large Language Models to More Sensor Modalities and Tasks

author.name: Miaoxin Cai, Guanqun Wang, Wei Zhang, Guangyao Zhou, Yin Zhuang, Tong Zhang, Hao Wang, He Chen, Jun Li

entry.summary: Presents Earth-OneVision, a 2B remote-sensing MLLM unifying six sensor modalities (optical, SAR, infrared, multispectral, temporal, video) and cross-sensor fusion across 9 task categories in one autoregressive framework. Uses dedicated alignment and serialization mechanisms.

entry.title: RealMath-Eval: Why SOTA Judges Struggle with Real Human Reasoning

author.name: Yiteng Mao, Kenan Xu, Yijia Lyu, Wenhao Li, Jianlong Chen, Xiangfeng Wang

entry.summary: Introduces RealMath-Eval, a benchmark of 224 real human student exam responses, showing that SOTA LLM judges struggle to grade authentic human reasoning compared with synthetic solutions. Reveals a stark evaluation gap between judging human versus model-generated work.

entry.title: Frontier Coding Agents Use Metaprogramming to Adapt to Unfamiliar Programming Languages

author.name: Aman Sharma, Sushrut Thorat, Paras Chopra

entry.summary: Evaluates six frontier coding agents on four esoteric programming languages, revealing capability differences hidden by mainstream benchmarks like SWE-Bench. Finds the strongest agents use metaprogramming to avoid writing unfamiliar target languages directly.

entry.title: Workflow-GYM: Towards Long-Horizon Evaluation of Computer-use Agentic tasks in Real-World Professional Fields

author.name: Liya Zhu, Jingzhe Ding, Jian Zhang, Jianbo Xue, Shihao Liang, Ge Zhang, Xiang Gao, Qingshui Gu, Mailun Gao, Huimin Che, Yan Zhao, Peiheng Zhou, Haojun Wang, Chaobo Xian, Lili Le, Chi Wu, Yiwei Liu, Shengda Long, Jiale Yang, Fangzhi Xu, Sijin Wu, Haodong Duan, Yi Zhu, Chao He, Zhaojian Li, Minchao Wang, Huan Zhou, Jiani Hou, Chuqian Yu, Weiran Shi, Hongwan Gao, Jiamin Chen, Guanhong Chen, Tingqin Luo, Kaiyuan Zhang, Zhixin Yao, Qing Hua, Yuhao Jiang, Jin Chen, Pu Chen, Zhenyu Hu, Xingyu Li, Zhengxuan Jiang, Meng Cao, Tianfeng Long, Haozhe Wang, Mingzhang Wang, Yichen Zhang, Yiming Dai, Chenchen Zhang, Jiaying Wang, Zhiyong Wu, Shen Yan, Yujia Qin, Wenhao Huang, Zaiyuan Wang, Xiaolong Chang

entry.summary: Introduces Workflow-GYM, a benchmark for long-horizon GUI computer-use agentic tasks across real-world professional domains, going beyond general-purpose software and short-horizon tasks. Evaluates whether agents can autonomously operate domain-specific professional software end-to-end.

entry.title: Mitigating Manifold Departure: Uncertainty-Aware Subspace Rectification for Trustworthy MLLM Decoding

author.name: Yingxuan Zhuang, Jingxiao Yang, Miao Pan, Cheng Tan, Yuxiang Cai, Siwei Tan, Chen Zhi, Xuhong Zhang, Jianwei Yin, Jintao Chen

entry.summary: Proposes MGAP, a training-free decoding method that mitigates object hallucination in multimodal LLMs by adaptively projecting representations to respect the model's semantic manifold, rather than blindly suppressing language priors. It addresses the dual nature of priors, which can be helpful or harmful depending on visual alignment.

entry.title: Failure Modes of Deep Multi-Agent RL in Asynchronous Pricing: Reproducible Triggers, Trace Diagnostics, and a Partial Fix

author.name: Shree Murthy, Rohan Pandey

entry.summary: Studies two reproducible failure modes of deep multi-agent RL in continuous-time pricing markets: tacit collusion between competing agents and actor-critic instability at high event rates, with trace diagnostics and a partial asynchrony-based fix. It quantifies collusion indices and the costs of mitigation.

entry.title: SocraticPO: Policy Optimization via Interactive Guidance

author.name: Zirui Liu, Jie Ouyang, Qi Liu, Xianquan Wang, Jiayu Liu, Tingyue Pan, Qingchuan Li, Jing Sha, Zhenya Huang, Shijin Wang, Enhong Chen

entry.summary: Proposes SocraticPO, which augments RL rollouts with Socratic-style natural-language corrective guidance from a teacher when the student answers incorrectly, providing explanatory signal beyond scalar rewards. It aims to reduce shortcut learning and brittle policies in reasoning.

entry.title: Mix, Don't Pick: Why Synthetic Corpus Composition Matters for Time Series Foundation Model Pretraining

author.name: Aaryan Nagpal, Debdeep Sanyal, Murari Mandal, Dhruv Kumar, Saurabh Deshpande

entry.summary: Shows that for time-series foundation model pretraining, simply mixing all synthetic generators with equal weight matches or beats the best individual generator, sidestepping the unstable and architecture-dependent generator-selection problem. It reports up to 2x error gaps between best and worst generators.

entry.title: IntentKV: Cross-Turn Intent-Aware KV Cache Pruning for Agent Inference

author.name: Junjie Li, Jiong Lou, Jie Li

entry.summary: Proposes IntentKV, a learned KV cache pruning method for multi-turn LLM agents that maintains a session-level intent memory to score and evict history tokens while keeping the base model frozen and composable with prefix caches. It targets KV cache as the dominant serving bottleneck in long-horizon agents.

entry.title: Dropout-GRPO: Variational Stochasticity for Continuous Latent Reasoning

author.name: Wooil Jung

entry.summary: Dropout-GRPO addresses the problem that continuous latent reasoning models (like Coconut) produce deterministic, identical rollouts that collapse GRPO's group-relative advantage. The authors introduce structured dropout to inject stochasticity, enabling reinforcement learning on continuous latent reasoning trajectories.

entry.title: Integral Field Unit Spectroscopy with One Fiber

author.name: Zehao Peng, Biprateep Dey, Chris J. Maddison, Joshua S. Speagle

entry.summary: This work presents a multimodal probabilistic foundation model that predicts high-resolution galaxy spectra with calibrated uncertainties from broadband images, mimicking expensive integral field unit spectroscopy. Trained on 4.7 million DESI images and single-fiber observations, it uses a masked autoencoder with positional and redshift-aware encodings.

entry.title: LLM-Guided Neural Architecture Search for Robust Co-Design of Physical Neural Networks

author.name: Tyler King, Timothee Leleu

entry.summary: UH-NAS is a hardware-agnostic neural architecture search framework that uses LLMs as evolutionary operators to co-optimize task accuracy and inference energy for unconventional hardware. It exposes hardware as a swappable backend with per-platform energy models and non-ideality simulators for fair cross-platform comparison.

entry.title: Beyond Absolute Imitation: Anchored Residual Guidance for Privileged On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Wenhao Zhang

entry.summary: This paper improves privileged on-policy distillation for LLM reasoning by disentangling locally reachable reasoning steps from future-conditioned oracle signals, rather than treating privileged information as a monolithic imitation target. It introduces anchored residual guidance to avoid encouraging the student to match a hindsight-biased distribution.

entry.title: Benchmarking Knowledge Editing using Logical Rules

author.name: Tatiana Moteu Ngoli, NDah Jean Kouagou, Hamada M. Zahera, Axel-Cyrille Ngonga Ngomo

entry.summary: This paper introduces a benchmark to evaluate how knowledge editing methods handle the logical consequences of a single fact edit, not just recall of the edited fact. It extracts logical rules from a knowledge graph and generates multi-hop questions to test downstream logical propagation of edits.

entry.title: Dmsh: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for All-Quad Mesh Generation

author.name: Anirudh Kalyan, Cosmin Anitescu, Xiaoying Zhuang, Timon Rabczuk, Somdatta Goswami, Sundararajan Natarajan

entry.summary: Dmsh is a fully automated multi-agent reinforcement learning pipeline for all-quad mesh generation, unifying geometric decomposition and quadrilateral meshing within one learning framework. Three coordinated agents handle topology simplification, geometric regularization, and mesh generation via a parametric Soft Actor-Critic architecture.

entry.title: STORM: Stepwise Token Optimization with Reward-Guided Beam Search

author.name: Arthur Satouf, Giulio D'Erasmo, Yuxuan Zong, Habiboulaye Amadou Boubacar, Pablo Piantanida, Benjamin Piwowarski

entry.summary: STORM is a self-supervised framework for lexical query expansion that trains LLM query rewriting via reward-guided beam search, providing token-level supervision instead of delayed sequence-level signals. It keeps the transparency and efficiency of BM25 inverted indexes while addressing vocabulary mismatch without rebuilding specialized neural indexes.

entry.title: Divide and Cooperate: Role-Decomposed Multi-Agent LLM Training with Cross-Agent Learning Signals

author.name: Jaewan Park, Solbee Cho, Jay-Yoon Lee

entry.summary: Proposes DAC, a role-decomposed multi-agent training framework that separates evidence acquisition and answer generation into cooperative subtasks to ease credit assignment in agentic search RL. Addresses combinatorial policy explosion from coupling roles in one model.

entry.title: Spatial-Omni: Spatial Audio Understanding Integration in Multimodal LLMs via FOA Encoding

author.name: Zhiyuan Zhu, Yixuan Chen, Yiwen Shao, Wenxiang Guo, Changhao Pan, Yu Zhang, Yuxiang Wang, Wei Liu, Houhua Zhang, Chengkuan Zeng, Wenbo Cheng, Yunxi Liu, Rui Yang, Steve Yves, Liefeng Bo, Zhou Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes Spatial-Omni with an SO-Encoder that injects First-Order Ambisonics spatial audio into existing Omni LLMs as an independent modality without altering original audio encoders. Introduces datasets and benchmarks for spatial audio understanding.

entry.title: LIBERO-Occ: Evaluating and Improving Vision-Language-Action Models under Scene-Induced Occlusion via Viewpoint Imagination

author.name: Taishan Li, Jiwen Zhang, Siyuan Wang, Xuanjing Huang, Zhongyu Wei

entry.summary: Introduces LIBERO-Occ, an occlusion-oriented benchmark extension showing SOTA vision-language-action models degrade substantially under scene-induced occlusion. Proposes Viewpoint Imagination (VIM) generating complementary views to condition action prediction.

entry.title: CLP: Collocation-Length Prediction for Zero-Loss Adaptive Multi-Token Inference

author.name: Xuezhen Xie, Zhiqiang Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes CLP and a Backbone-as-Architect principle for multi-token prediction, identifying head-backbone competition for the first token as the cause of quality degradation. Has the backbone LM head always generate the first token while MTP heads handle subsequent ones.

entry.title: Compile Once, Differentiate Everywhere: A Differentiable Meta-Circular Interpreter

author.name: Lucas Sheneman

entry.summary: This work presents a compiler that translates a self-hosting subset of Scheme into differentiable computation graphs, enabling differentiable meta-circular interpretation where programs supplied as data inherit differentiability. This allows code itself to become a learnable scientific model.

entry.title: Learning the Universe: Posterior Reliability of Neural Generative Models in High-Dimensional Field-Level Inference of Cosmic Initial Conditions

author.name: Ludvig Doeser, Jens Jasche

entry.summary: This work evaluates the posterior reliability of neural generative models (Stochastic Interpolants and GLOW normalizing flows) for high-dimensional field-level inference of cosmic initial conditions, using Hamiltonian Monte Carlo as a reference. It provides a controlled assessment of accuracy guarantees lacking in amortized inference.

entry.title: Embodiment-conditioned Generalist Control for Multirotor Aerial Robots

author.name: Orestis Konstantaropoulos, Welf Rehberg, Mihir Kulkarni, Kostas Alexis

entry.summary: This work presents a generalist position control policy for arbitrary multirotor configurations of a given rotor count using a single network, conditioned on a physics-grounded mass and inertia-normalized control allocation matrix. Trained via PPO across diverse configurations in just five minutes on an RTX 3090.

entry.title: Task Robustness via Re-Labelling Vision-Action Robot Data

author.name: Artur Kuramshin, \"Ozg\"ur Aslan, Cyrus Neary, Glen Berseth

entry.summary: TREAD is a scalable framework that uses large Vision-Language Models to re-label and augment existing robotics datasets with diverse semantic sub-tasks and instructions, without additional data collection. It improves robot policy instruction-following by addressing limited linguistic and action diversity in datasets.

entry.title: OpenRTLSet: A Fully Open-Source Dataset for Large Language Model-based Verilog Module Design

author.name: Jinghua Wang, Lily Jiaxin Wan, Sanjana Pingali, Scott Smith, Manvi Jha, Shalini Sivakumar, Xing Zhao, Kaiwen Cao, Deming Chen

entry.summary: OpenRTLSet is the largest fully open-source hardware design dataset with 131,000+ Verilog samples combining GitHub code, VHDL translations, and synthesizable C/C++ translations. Natural language descriptions were generated using DeepSeek-R1 to enable fine-tuning LLMs for Verilog generation.

entry.title: Pushing the Limits of LLM Tool Calling via Experiential Knowledge Integration and Activation

author.name: Yupu Hao, Zhuoran Jin, Huanxuan Liao, Kang Liu, Jun Zhao

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies how experiential knowledge affects LLM tool-calling across acquisition, activation, and internalization stages, finding instance-level knowledge yields strong gains while abstract intent-level knowledge helps less. It offers practical insights for improving agentic tool use.

entry.title: VISTA: A Versatile Interactive User Simulation Toolkit for Agent Evaluation

author.name: Yunan Lu, Ryan Shea, Yusen Zhang, Zhou Yu

entry.summary: VISTA is a versatile interactive user simulation toolkit for agent evaluation that supports both UI and API actions and provides mechanisms to assess the quality and coverage of simulated interactions. It addresses limitations of static benchmarks for dynamic agentic behavior.

entry.title: ManiSplat: Manipulation Trajectory Synthesis from Monocular Video via Decoupled 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Wenhao Hu, Haonan Zhou, Liu Liu, Yun Du, Xinjie Wang, Ziang Li, Zhizhong Su, Gaoang Wang

entry.summary: ManiSplat reconstructs controllable, decoupled Gaussian digital twins from monocular ego-view robotic videos using a graph-structured disentangled representation that separates robot, objects, and background. It enables manipulation trajectory synthesis for interactive 3D scenes.

entry.title: Envision4D: Envisioning Visual Futures via Feed-forward 4D Gaussian Splatting for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Qi Song, Yifei He, Chi Zhang, Zheng Fu, Xuhe Zhao, Mengmeng Yang, Kun Jiang, Rui Huang, Diange Yang

entry.summary: Envision4D is a self-supervised feed-forward framework for pose-free future extrapolation in autonomous driving using 4D Gaussian Splatting, with a future pose prediction module and temporal attention to capture non-linear dynamics. It addresses ghosting artifacts under large displacements.

entry.title: WorldOlympiad: Can Your World Model Survive a Triathlon?

author.name: Yuke Zhao, Wangbo Zhao, Weijie Wang, Zeyu Zhang, Dakai An, Akide Liu, Yinghao Yu, Jiasheng Tang, Fan Wang, Wei Wang, Bohan Zhuang

entry.summary: Introduces WorldOlympiad, a benchmark diagnosing video world models across physical faithfulness, geometric consistency, and interaction fidelity using object segmentation and MLLM-as-judge. Goes beyond visual-quality metrics toward physical-rule adherence.

entry.title: Uncovering Vulnerability of Vision-Language-Action Models under Joint-Level Physical Faults

author.name: Minsoo Jo, Taeju Kwon, Junha Chun, Youngjoon Jeong, Taesup Kim

entry.summary: Presents SARM2, a multi-task stage-aware reward model combining action-primitive awareness for self-improving robotic manipulation, providing dense general supervision for on-robot RL without per-task annotations. Reduces dependence on costly behavior cloning demonstrations.

entry.title: Claude Fable 5 and new AI safety fables

author.name: Nathan Lambert

entry.summary: Nathan Lambert analyzes Anthropic's release of Claude Fable 5, the general-access variant of its Mythos-class models, focusing on the bundled safety measures, some disclosed and some silently modifying the model, and argues these unevenly applied controls reflect attempts to protect or entrench Anthropic's lead while raising concerns about narrow, self-fulfilling notions of safety. It frames a frontier release as a cautionary case in safety-versus-access tradeoffs.

entry.title: Reasoning or Memorization? Direction-Aware Diversity Exploration in LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jiangnan Xia, Yucheng Shi, Yu Yang, Kishan Panaganti, Zhenwen Liang, Ninghao Liu

entry.summary: Proposes DiRL, a direction-aware RL framework that anchors exploration to an internal reasoning-versus-memorization direction in the policy, preventing exploration from rewarding memorized shortcuts. Aims to steer RL exploration toward genuine reasoning improvement in LLMs.

entry.title: One Token per Multimodal Evidence: Latent Memory for Resource-Constrained QA

author.name: Zhi Zheng, Ziqiao Meng, Hao Luan, Wei Liu, Wee Sun Lee

entry.summary: Proposes Latent Memory, replacing raw text and image evidence with single high-dimensional latent tokens produced by a small compressor model, drastically reducing token consumption and storage for multimodal QA. Operates retrieval and generation in a unified latent space.

entry.title: Mind the Gap: Can Frontier LLMs Pass a Standardized Office Proficiency Exam?

author.name: Tengchao Lv, Dongdong Zhang, Jiayu Ding, Yilin Jia, Yuzhong Zhao, Yupan Huang, Wenshan Wu, Xiangyang Zhou, Shaohan Huang, Nan Yang, Li Dong, Lei Cui, Furu Wei

entry.summary: Introduces an Office automation benchmark based on China's National Computer Rank Examination with 200 practical Word, Excel, and PowerPoint tasks scored against 7,118 machine-gradable criteria. Tests frontier LLM agents on long-horizon, multi-application productivity workflows.

entry.title: SPACE: Source-free Proxy Anchor Concept Erasure for MLLMs

author.name: Zhijing Zhang, Jiaqi Ding, Qianshan Wei, Nan Zhou, Jiaqi Li, Yongliang Wu, Tongxin Zhu, Xiaolin Fang

entry.summary: Introduces SPACE, the first source-free machine unlearning framework for multimodal LLMs that erases target concepts without access to the original visual data, using text-guided proxy anchor selection. It addresses privacy and data-retention constraints where source data is unavailable.

entry.title: SHAPE: Coalition-Aware Expert Pruning for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs

author.name: Yuhao Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes SHAPE, a task-driven expert pruning framework for sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs that models intra-layer expert cooperation as a cooperative game and uses Shapley-style attribution, rather than scoring experts independently. It targets the memory wall of resident expert pools.

entry.title: A Source Domain is All You Need: Source-Only Cross-OS Transfer Learning for APT Anomaly Detection via Semantic Alignment and Optimal Transport

author.name: Sidahmed Benabderrahmanea, Petko Valtchev, James Cheney, Talal Rahwan

entry.summary: This work tackles source-only cross-OS detection of Advanced Persistent Threats, where a detector trained on one operating system must transfer to an unlabeled target OS. It abstracts process behavior into natural-language descriptions, embeds them with pretrained models, and uses optimal transport for anomaly ranking without target labels.

entry.title: Baseline-Free Policy Optimization for Neural Combinatorial Optimization

author.name: Carlos S. Sep\'ulveda, Gonzalo A. Ruz

entry.summary: This paper evaluates GRPO, an LLM alignment algorithm, for neural combinatorial optimization on routing problems, showing it eliminates the unstable rollout baseline of standard REINFORCE. A controlled comparison of five RL algorithms on TSP and CVRP finds GRPO improves stability on harder instances.

entry.title: UPLOTS: A Unified Pretrained Language Model for Constrained Time-series Generation

author.name: Du Yin, Hao Xue, Jinliang Deng, Yang Yang, Shuang Ao, Arian Prabowo, Flora Salim

entry.summary: UPLOTS is a unified, prompt-guided language model framework for constrained time-series generation across diverse domains, using a single pretrained transformer with learned constraint prompts instead of per-dataset models. It introduces dynamic multi-dataset loss reweighting and prompt-to-pattern mapping for on-demand controllable generation.

entry.title: Can Image Models Imagine Time? ImageTime: A Novel Benchmark for Probing Visual World Modeling Through Spatiotemporal Consistency

author.name: Xinrui Wu, Lichen Huang

entry.summary: ImageTime is a diagnostic benchmark probing whether image generation models can coherently represent how a visual world changes over time, using spatiotemporal consistency across multiple visual states. It tests preservation of identities, objects, spatial relations, and causal order for tasks like storyboarding and step-by-step illustration.

entry.title: Attention-Discounted Adaptive Sampler for Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Yusuf Sahin, Ahmed Rockey Saikia, Volkan Cevher, Paolo Favaro

entry.summary: Proposes ADAS, a training-free reranking rule for parallel masked diffusion decoding that discounts candidate tokens attending strongly to already-selected positions, capturing token interactions ignored by score-based samplers. Keeps the base stopping rule unchanged.

entry.title: T1-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-Scenario Agents in Real-World Domains

author.name: Genta Indra Winata, Amartya Chakraborty, Yuzhen Lin, Swasthi P Rao, Shikhhar Siingh, Houhan Lu, Nadia Bathaee, Sriharsha Hatwar, Paresh Dashore, Anmol Jain, Kshitij Tayal, Xiuzhu Lin, Anirban Das, Sambit Sahu, Shi-Xiong Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces T1-Bench, a high-fidelity benchmark for evaluating agentic systems in realistic, multi-domain, customer-facing environments with interleaved multi-turn scenarios requiring sustained reasoning and coordination. Targets gaps in task complexity and domain diversity of prior benchmarks.

entry.title: RoboNaldo: Accurate, Stable and Powerful Humanoid Soccer Shooting via Motion-Guided Curriculum Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yichao Zhong, Yidan Lu, Yuhang Lu, Tianyang Tang, Haoguang Mai, Yixuan Pan, Tianyu Li, Li Chen, Jingbo Wang, Zhongyu Li, Peng Lu, Hongyang Li

entry.summary: Presents RoboNaldo, a three-stage motion-guided curriculum RL framework enabling accurate, stable, high-impulse humanoid soccer shooting from a single human-kick reference. Progressively shifts optimization from stable kicking prior toward shooting performance.

entry.title: Flaws in the LLM Automation Narrative

author.name: George Perrett, Javae Elliott, Jennifer Hill, Marc Scott

entry.summary: Critiques the LLM automation narrative by showing benchmark claims overstate expert-level performance, since benchmarks often test training-data content and ignore reliability and error magnitude. Uses a novel code-writing data analysis task to compare a frontier LLM against humans in high-stakes contexts.

entry.title: Calibrating Overconfidence Without Sacrificing Confidence: Probe-Conditioned Head Intervention for LLMs

author.name: Ke Li, Chongzhe Zhang, Zifan Zeng, Feng Liu, Qunli Zhang, Zheng Hu

entry.summary: Introduces Probe-Conditioned Head Intervention (PCHI), an inference-time calibration method using a frozen probe to detect likely wrong-but-confident responses and conditionally rescale attention-head outputs during confidence generation. Reduces overconfidence on wrong answers while preserving warranted confidence on correct ones.

entry.title: What Demonstration Curation Metrics Do to Your Policy

author.name: Aarav Bedi

entry.summary: This paper shows that demonstration-curation metrics with high defect-detection accuracy do not necessarily yield better behavior-cloning policies, revealing a sharp decoupling on a LIBERO manipulation benchmark. It finds most metrics exploit episode length as a trivial proxy for defects.

entry.title: PADD: Path-Aligned Decompression Distillation for Non-Router Teacher to Guide MoE Student Learning

author.name: Xinyue Peng, Yi Qian, Jiaojiao Lin, Wenjian Shao, Yanming Liu

entry.summary: PADD is a four-stage distillation framework that transfers knowledge from dense teachers without routing into mixture-of-experts students while learning routing policies. It uses teacher neuron clustering, online adaptive distillation, path-refined policy optimization, and reward-augmented load balancing.

entry.title: Few-step Generative Models as Lossy Compression

author.name: Fuma Kimishima, Jinjia Zhou

entry.summary: This work studies whether few-step generative models (Rectified Flow, CTM, MeanFlow) can serve as fast codecs within the reverse channel coding framework of DiffC for lossy compression. It derives the necessary posterior quantities by exploiting velocity-denoising parameterization equivalences.

entry.title: Who Brought Easter Eggs to Eid? Auditing Cultural Translation of Math Word Problems Across Diverse Languages and Regions

author.name: Parisa Suchdev, Juniper Lovato

entry.summary: This study audits how Claude, GPT-4.1, and Gemini culturally adapt math word problems across high- to low-resource languages, annotating thousands of entity transformations to assess cultural preservation and bias. It reveals inconsistencies and salience patterns in model localization.

entry.title: Dissect and Prune: Enhancing Robustness in AI-Generated Image Detection

author.name: Dahye Kim, Jaehyun Choi, Hyun Seok Seong, Seongho Kim, Donghun Lee, Sungwon Yi, Jang-Ho Choi

entry.summary: DEAR (Dissect and Prune) improves robustness in AI-generated image detection by identifying a prediction asymmetry toward the real class and using inpainted images to prune spurious features less robust to post-processing. It enhances sensitivity under compression and resizing.

entry.title: PathRelax: Parallel-Path Relaxed Speculative Jacobi Decoding for Accelerating Auto-Regressive Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Haodong Lei, Hongsong Wang, Bingxuan Dai, Pan Zhou

entry.summary: PathRelax (PathSpec) accelerates autoregressive text-to-image generation using parallel-path relaxed speculative Jacobi decoding with a multi-sequence draft tree, expanding the token search space for higher speedups and longer acceptance lengths. It targets efficient high-resolution image generation.

entry.title: GUI-AC: Enhancing Continual Learning in GUI Agents

author.name: Can Lin, Tao Feng, Hangjie Yuan, Dan Zhang, Yifan Zhu, Zhonghong Ou

entry.summary: GUI-AC enhances continual learning in GUI agents under non-stationary interface distributions, addressing the instability of reinforcement fine-tuning's grounding capability and reward collapse. It targets robust generalization across novel domains and resolutions.

entry.title: Vector Map as Language: Toward Unified Remote Sensing Vector Mapping

author.name: Yinglong Yan, Yunkai Yang, Haoyi Wang, Wei Fu, Linshan Wu, Honghu Pan, Shaobo Xia, Shanghang Zhang, Hao Chen, Leyuan Fang

entry.summary: This work proposes representing remote sensing vector maps as language, offering a flexible unified medium that can accommodate heterogeneous map elements including geometry, semantics, and topology across multiple category layers. It overcomes limitations of polygon and graph representations.

entry.title: Next Forcing: Causal World Modeling with Multi-Chunk Prediction

author.name: Gangwei Xu, Qihang Zhang, Jiaming Zhou, Xing Zhu, Yujun Shen, Xin Yang, Yinghao Xu

entry.summary: Introduces Next Forcing, a multi-chunk prediction framework for causal world action models, inspired by multi-token prediction in LLMs, to speed training, raise accuracy, and accelerate inference at high frame rates. Adds future-dynamics supervision beyond the current chunk.

entry.title: OMG: Omni-Modal Motion Generation for Generalist Humanoid Control

author.name: Siqiao Huang, Kun-Ying Lee, Dongming Qiao, Guanqi He, Zhenyu Wang, Yitang Li, Shaoting Zhu, Hang Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces OMG, an omni-modal motion generator for generalist humanoid control structured as a reasoning brain over a reactive motion-tracking cerebellum, conditioning on compositional multi-modal inputs at scale. Aims to overcome few-skill, reward-heavy prior approaches.

entry.title: Some Interesting Papers on RLVR

author.name: CarolusRenniusVitellius

entry.summary: A MATS-produced informal review of recent RLVR (reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards) papers, advancing the thesis that RL updates act qualitatively differently from pretraining/SFT, rotating principal subspaces far less and thus changing propensity rather than capability. The author speculatively links this to emergent misalignment and subliminal learning. It synthesizes a notable strand of mechanistic RL research.

entry.title: From Context-Aware to Conflict-Aware: Generalizing Contrastive Decoding for Knowledge Conflict in LLMs

author.name: Runze Jiang, Taiqiang Wu, Yan Wang, Bingyu Zhu, Longtao Huang

entry.summary: Generalizes contrastive decoding from a context-aware to a conflict-aware paradigm that dynamically allocates authority between parametric priors and external context based on conflict signals. Identifies a power-family of logit combinations with regime asymmetry to avoid overwriting correct priors.

entry.title: Cross-Modal Knowledge Distillation without Paired Data: Theoretical Foundation and Algorithm

author.name: Trong Khiem Tran, Anh Duc Chu, Quang Hung Pham, Phi Le Nguyen, Trong Nghia Hoang

entry.summary: Develops a theoretical framework and algorithm for cross-modal knowledge distillation without paired data, establishing distributional relationships and identifying feature alignment and label alignment as governing quantities. Removes the costly requirement for aligned multimodal data.

entry.title: A History-Aware Visually Grounded Critic for Computer Use Agents

author.name: Jaewoo Lee, Zaid Khan, Archiki Prasad, Justin Chih-Yao Chen, Supriyo Chakraborty, Kartik Balasubramaniam, Sambit Sahu, Elias Stengel-Eskin, Hyunji Lee, Mohit Bansal

entry.summary: Introduces HiViG, a history-aware visually grounded test-time critic for computer-use agents that abstracts past interactions into a compact record and evaluates actions with visual grounding. Addresses short-sighted decision loops and lack of visual grounding in existing critics.

entry.title: ReasonAlloc: Hierarchical Decoding-Time KV Cache Budget Allocation for Reasoning Models

author.name: Wenhao Liu, Hao Shi, Yunhe Li, Weizhi Fei, Xiangyuan Wang, Mengzhe Ruan, Hanxu Hou, Peisong Wang, Linqi Song, Shuang Qiu

entry.summary: Proposes ReasonAlloc, a training-free hierarchical KV-cache budget allocation framework for reasoning models that adapts to stepwise context demands of autoregressive reasoning rather than assuming uniform budgets. Operates at offline layer-wise and online levels to mitigate KV cache growth in long CoT.

entry.title: An LLM-Native Psychometric Instrument Does Not Predict LLM Behavior: Evidence Across 25 Models

author.name: Juan Manuel Contreras

entry.summary: Constructs the first bottom-up psychometric instrument derived from LLM behavioral affordances via exploratory factor analysis, administering 300 items to 25 models and yielding a five-factor structure. Finds that even this LLM-native instrument's self-reports do not predict observed behavior.

entry.title: Rotate2Think: Geometric Priming via Orthogonal Rotation to Improve Language Model Reasoning

author.name: Aditya Sharma, Christopher J. Pal, Amal Zouaq

entry.summary: Shows that LLM input and thinking embeddings both exhibit extreme conicity but lie along non-collinear mean directions, and proposes Rotate2Think, an inference-time orthogonal rotation that primes stronger reasoning. It links representation-space geometry to reasoning quality.

entry.title: Less Context, More Accuracy: A Bi-Temporal Memory Engine for LLM Agents Where a Lean Retrieved Context Beats the Full History

author.name: Liuyin Wang

entry.summary: Presents Engram, an open-source bi-temporal memory engine for LLM agents that combines a fast lossless episodic write path with an asynchronous knowledge-graph fact extraction path, showing lean retrieved context can beat full-history replay on accuracy. It also critiques inconsistent memory benchmark reporting.

entry.title: Generalized-CVO: Fast and Correspondence-Free Local Point Cloud Registration with Second Order Riemannian Optimization

author.name: Ray Zhang, Marcus Greiff, Thomas Lew, John Subosits

entry.summary: Proposes Generalized-CVO, a correspondence-free local point cloud registration method using RKHS embeddings with anisotropic kernels and a second-order on-manifold Riemannian optimization scheme, achieving up to 10x speedup over first-order solvers. It improves LiDAR and RGB-D tracking accuracy.

entry.title: Density Ridge Selective Prediction for LLM and VLM Hallucination Detection under Calibration Label Scarcity

author.name: Nina I. Shamsi
