entry.summary: This paper introduces efficient minimal solvers for relative pose estimation in multi-camera autonomous driving systems using a novel translation parameterization and first-order rotation approximation. It reduces computation and feature-match requirements for time-sensitive scenarios.

entry.title: LAEI: Layered Autonomous Edge Intelligence Framework for Robust UAV Swarm Operations

author.name: Changmin Park, Wooyong Jung, Hwangnam Kim

entry.summary: LAEI is a layered autonomous edge intelligence framework for UAV swarms combining onboard learned policies with lightweight mission-level supervision for adaptive goal reassignment and fault-aware recovery. It balances centralized coordination consistency with decentralized robustness.

entry.title: Curation of a Cardiology Interface Terminology for Highlighting Electronic Health Records using Machine Learning

author.name: Mahshad Koohi Habibi Dehkordi, Shuxin Zhou, Yehoshua Perl, Fadi P. Deek, James Geller, Gai Elhanan, Andrew J. Einstein, Luke Lindemann, Vipina K. Keloth

entry.summary: This study designs a Cardiology Interface Terminology using a novel machine-learning technique to automatically highlight all clinically relevant details in dense cardiology EHR notes, reducing manual training-data preparation. It aims to help clinicians avoid missing crucial information.

entry.title: Bridging Expert Knowledge and Automated Feature Engineering via Self-Evolution

author.name: Varun Khurana, Vijval Ekbote, Vashu Chauhan, Yaman Kumar Singla, Rajiv Ratn Shah, Balaji Krishnamurthy

entry.summary: FEST proposes a self-evolving tree-based system for automated feature engineering that produces interpretable, expert-aligned features from unstructured content in high-stakes domains like clinical care and content moderation. It aims to operationalize qualitative expert criteria into precise discriminative features.

entry.title: FAME: Forecastability-Aware Mixture of Experts for Heterogeneous Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Qianyang Li, Xingjun Zhang, Shaoxun Wang, Tao Peng, Jia Wei

entry.summary: FAME is a sparse mixture-of-experts framework for heterogeneous time series forecasting that represents each series with a forecastability fingerprint and learns cost-aware expert routing from validation performance. It targets large-scale retail/industrial forecasting with diverse regimes.

entry.title: Graph2Idea:Retrieval-Augmented Scientific Idea Generation with Graph-Structured Contexts

author.name: Xu Li, Hanzhe Tu, Xun Han

entry.summary: Graph2Idea is a knowledge-graph-guided retrieval-augmented framework for scientific idea generation that transforms retrieved papers into structured graphs capturing cross-paper relations among problems, methods, and findings. It aims to overcome redundancy in flat-text retrieval contexts.

entry.title: Implicit Causal Graph Construction in Text via Chain Discovery

author.name: Liesbeth Allein, Marie-Francine Moens

entry.summary: Studies implicit causal graph construction from text by treating cause-effect pairs as endpoints of latent graphs and using LLMs to infer intermediate events via chain discovery. Includes wisdom-of-the-crowd extensions aggregating multiple LLMs.

entry.title: DiffoR: A Unified Continuous Generative Framework for Universal Ordinal Regression

author.name: Hongxu Ma, Lin Wang, Chenghou Jin, Han Zhou, Jie Zhang, Xiaoyu Yang, Chunjie Chen, Jihong Guan, Shuigeng Zhou

entry.summary: Reformulates ordinal regression as a continuous generative task with DiffOR, using diffusion/rectified-flow style modeling to overcome quantization artifacts and capture global ordinal topology. Targets non-stationary semantic transitions in ordinal data.

entry.title: No Free Lunch for Synthetic Images under Data Scarcity Conditions

author.name: Borja Arroyo Galende, Alejandro Almod\'ovar, Patricia A. Apell\'aniz, Juan Parras, Silvia Uribe, Santiago Zazo

entry.summary: Investigates fidelity-privacy-utility trade-offs in synthetic image generation under data scarcity, evaluating VAE, GAN, and DDPM with differential privacy on MNIST, OCTMNIST, and OrganAMNIST. Finds GAN and DDPM more robust to DP noise while VAE degrades faster.

entry.title: Liquid Neural Networks as a Drop-in Continuous-Time Deformation Field for Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Mingzhao Li, Arghya Pal, Guan Yuan Tan

entry.summary: This work replaces the MLP deformation field in dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting with closed-form continuous-time Liquid Neural Network cells, providing genuine temporal coupling instead of discrete per-frame offsets. It claims improved temporal smoothness as a drop-in modification.

entry.title: Pharmacogenomic Knowledge Graph Augmentation for Graph Neural Network-Based Drug-Drug Interaction Prediction

author.name: Juergen Dietrich

entry.summary: This study augments GNN-based drug-drug interaction prediction with pharmacogenomic prior knowledge (CYP enzyme substrate/inhibitor/inducer annotations) to surpass an information ceiling that purely structural models cannot exceed. The added metabolic pathway context is complementary to molecular structure.

entry.title: Jas: AI-Paired Engineering as a Revival of N-Version Programming

author.name: Jason Hickey

entry.summary: Jas presents a case study of AI-paired software engineering producing five working ports of a vector illustration app across Rust, Swift, OCaml, Python, and browser platforms in roughly 120 hours, framed as a revival of N-version programming. It uses an executable YAML specification and parallel implementations as differential testing safeguards.

entry.title: Decoupling Semantics and Logic: A Training-Free Coarse-to-Fine Pipeline for Video Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Jiaxin Dai, Zehang Wei, Jiamin Yan, Xiang Xiang

entry.summary: This system description presents a training-free two-stage cascaded video RAG pipeline that decouples semantic retrieval from logical reasoning through modality-aware division of labor for cross-lingual long-video comprehension. It isolates noisy modalities like OCR and ASR during high-recall pre-fetching.

entry.title: Human-Centered Benchmarking of Driver Monitoring Models

author.name: Ruben Dario Florez-Zela

entry.summary: This paper proposes a Human-Centered Benchmarking Framework for driver monitoring models, evaluating across accuracy, explainability, efficiency, and robustness rather than accuracy alone. Applied to four lightweight architectures on eye-state classification, it shows each model leads on a different dimension.

entry.title: Lost in the Flow with Code Talkers: Unveiling the Instruction-Tuning Tax of Large Language Models in Code Tasks

author.name: Shi Ying Chang, Chiok Yew Ho, Yichen Li, Yintong Huo

entry.summary: Investigates the instruction-tuning tax for LLMs in code tasks across Flow (infill/completion) and Command (instruction-following) cognitive modes. It examines whether instruction tuning degrades code-completion capabilities developers need in IDEs.

entry.title: Hybridizing Equilibrium Propagation with Ising Machines for Efficient Energy-Based Learning

author.name: Chen-Rui Fan, Bo Lu, Xing-Yu Wu, Tie-Jun Wang, Chuan Wang

entry.summary: Introduces an Ising-dynamics-inspired equilibrium-propagation framework replacing dissipative Hopfield relaxation with extended phase-space dynamics using conjugate variables to avoid local-minima convergence. Targets energy-efficient physical learning hardware.

entry.title: From USD Scenes to Knowledge Graphs: Zero-Shot Ontology Grounding with LLMs

author.name: Jiangtao Shuai, Zongxiong Chen, Manfred Hauswirth, Sonja Schimmler

entry.summary: Investigates zero-shot LLM grounding of USD 3D scene objects to formal ontology classes for robot knowledge graphs, achieving 90-96% accuracy with descriptive names versus brittle dictionaries. Offers a training-free alternative to manual grounding.

entry.title: SAILS: Surrogate-based Analysis of Interactions via Local Effect Smooths

author.name: Timo Hei{\ss}, Julia Herbinger, Bernd Bischl, Giuseppe Casalicchio

entry.summary: Introduces SAILS, a model-agnostic framework that analyzes pairwise feature interactions via interpretable GAM surrogates fitted to local effects, revealing functional forms rather than just detecting interactions. It enables interaction detection through significance tests on smooth terms.

entry.title: A Finetuned SpeechLLM for Joint Multi-Granular L2 Assessment and Natural-Language Rationales

author.name: Aditya Kamlesh Parikh, Cristian Tejedor-Garcia, Catia Cucchiarini, Helmer Strik

entry.summary: Presents a rubric-guided SpeechLLM fine-tuned for multi-aspect, multi-granular L2 speech assessment that jointly predicts ordinal proficiency labels and generates natural-language rationales. Uses supervised fine-tuning plus Bounded Direct Preference Optimization and analyzes rationale reliability.

entry.title: ArtiFact: A Large-Scale Multi-Modal Cultural Heritage Dataset

author.name: Luciano Duarte, Olga Ovcharenko, Sebastian Schelter

entry.summary: Releases ArtiFact, a large multimodal cultural heritage dataset of 651K museum records combining tables, text, and images from three major museums. Demonstrates utility through cross-modal error detection with a curated taxonomy of seven error categories.

entry.title: SPIN: Decentralized Swarm Control via Tensorized Policy Coordination

author.name: Zhaowen Fan

entry.summary: Introduces SPIN, a decentralized swarm control framework that models swarm topologies as compressed tensor networks, factorizing joint policy tensors into Matrix Product State chains to reduce complexity from exponential to linear. It targets resource-constrained edge platforms for multi-agent coordination.

entry.title: KITE: A Tri-Modal Transformer Integrating Text, Images, and Knowledge Graphs for Fake News Detection

author.name: Kevin Patel, Shashi Bhushan Jha

entry.summary: Introduces KITE, a tri-modal transformer fusing text, images, and Wikidata knowledge graphs via RoBERTa, CLIP, and a graph attention network for fake news detection. It jointly models semantic inconsistencies across modalities rather than treating knowledge as post-processing.

entry.title: Mesh Graph Neural Network Framework for Accelerating Finite Element Simulation for Arbitrary Geometries

author.name: Josiah D. Kunz, Kamal Choudhary

entry.summary: Presents a mesh graph network surrogate predicting von Mises stress fields for 2D components with arbitrary hole geometries, using node-type and relative-edge features instead of absolute coordinates for generalization. It accelerates finite element analysis across geometries.

entry.title: Backward Coherence and Hidden-State Stability in Recurrent Neural Networks: A Quasi-Reverse-Martingale Theory

author.name: Yuan-chin Ivan Chang

entry.summary: Develops a quasi-reverse-martingale theory for RNN hidden-state stability via backward coherence, where states can be reconstructed from future states. Provides convergence guarantees and a regularization scheme that improves stability empirically. Theoretical contribution to RNN understanding.

entry.title: Heterophily-Aware Adaptive Knowledge Distillation for Hypergraph Neural Networks

author.name: Joohee Cho, David Yoon Suk Kang, Yunyong Ko

entry.summary: Proposes HADES, a heterophily-aware adaptive knowledge distillation method for hypergraph neural networks that modulates teacher knowledge transfer based on node heterophily as a reliability estimate. Improves student model quality. Relevant to efficient hypergraph learning.

entry.title: Machine-Learning Emulation of Satellite Greenhouse Gas Retrievals: Stability over Time

author.name: Nugzar Gognadze, Motonobu Kanagawa, Yu Someya, Hisashi Yashiro

entry.summary: Studies temporal stability of ML emulators of satellite greenhouse gas retrievals using GOSAT data, showing prediction accuracy degrades when test periods move away from training periods. Highlights distribution-shift challenges in environmental emulation. Relevant to climate monitoring ML.

entry.title: Information-Geometric Optimization on Spheres

author.name: Vladimir Ja\' cimovi\'c

entry.summary: Designs two information-geometric optimization flows for black-box optimization on spheres using hyperbolic geometry of Poincare and Bergman balls, showing ensembles of generalized Kuramoto oscillators compute natural search gradients. Connects to quantum decision making. Theoretical optimization contribution with physics links.

entry.title: Hardware-aware Low-latency Quantum Compilation with Data-driven Lightweight Error Detection for Early Fault-Tolerant Systems

author.name: Sumit Chongder (Indian Institute of Technology Jodhpur)

entry.summary: Presents an integrated hardware-aware quantum compilation and lightweight error-detection framework that jointly optimizes qubit mapping, SWAP insertion, and syndrome scheduling under latency constraints. Targets the early fault-tolerant regime where full error correction is too costly.

entry.title: RACT: Retrieval Augmented Column-Table Learning and Prediction for Multi-Table Schema Matching

author.name: Leonard Traeger, Enas Khwaileh, Andreas Behrend, George Karabatis

entry.summary: Proposes RACT, a self-supervised retrieval-augmented framework for multi-table schema matching that uses referential context to probabilistically retrieve candidate tables, constraining relevant column matches. Outperforms similarity-based baselines on holistic schema matching.

entry.title: Structure-Aware Modeling of Multiple-Choice Questions Improves Automatic Difficulty Estimation

author.name: Gabriel Ortega, Abelino Jim\'enez, S\'everin Lions, Pablo Dartnell

entry.summary: Studies automatic difficulty estimation for multiple-choice questions, hypothesizing that explicitly modeling distractors as separate structural components improves prediction over treating them as appended text. Shows structure-aware modeling of distractors consistently improves difficulty estimation over baselines that omit them.

entry.title: Report the Floor: A Training-Free Conformal Interval Is a Mandatory Baseline for Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Valery Manokhin

entry.summary: Argues that a training-free split-conformal interval around a last-value forecast is a strong yet routinely omitted baseline for probabilistic time-series forecasting, beating many learned methods across 2,217 real series. A methodological critique calling for honest baselines.

entry.title: Arabic Sentence Segmentation Across Genres and Punctuation Conditions

author.name: Mohammed Elkholy, Khalid N. Elmadani, Nizar Habash, Bashar Alhafni

entry.summary: Introduces AraSEG, a genre-diverse Arabic sentence segmentation corpus spanning eight genres and varied punctuation conditions, finding lightweight encoders and dependency parsers outperform LLMs in hard settings. Addresses robustness gaps in realistic Arabic text.

entry.title: Cross Paraphrastic Invariance Learning for Hallucination Detection

author.name: Shanshan Lin, Dongsheng Hong, Sibo Ju, Chao Chen, Sihong Xie, Xiangwen Liao

entry.summary: Proposes CPIL, a two-stage Siamese framework for hallucination detection that enforces paraphrastic invariance via positive views and mines same-document opposite-label hard negatives. Maximizes utility of limited labeled data without costly LLM evaluators.

entry.title: Multilingual Sentiment Aware Text Summarization A Reinforcement Learning Approach for Consistency Maintenance

author.name: Mikhail Krasitskii, Alexander Gelbukh, Olga Kolesnikova, Grigori Sidorov

entry.summary: Studies sentiment drift in RLHF-based multilingual summarization, showing a systematic shift toward neutral sentiment that strengthens with KL regularization across eight languages. Proposes a reinforcement learning approach for sentiment consistency, revealing an alignment-vs-affective-fidelity tradeoff.

entry.title: Explicit Representation Alignment for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Baode Wang, Ziming Wang, Huacan Wang, Ronghao Chen, Biao Wu

entry.summary: This paper identifies representation misalignment between independently pretrained modality encoders as a key bottleneck in multimodal sentiment analysis, arguing that alignment before fusion matters more than fusion complexity. It proposes using vision-language models to convert visual content into structured text for explicit alignment.

entry.title: Introducing multiplex semantic networks as multifaceted representations of creative associative knowledge across multilingual samples

author.name: Edith Haim, Kurt Haim, Roger E. Beaty, Cynthia S. Q. Siew, Massimo Stella

entry.summary: Introduces multiplex semantic networks built from six cognitive tasks across 518 individuals in four countries as a multifaceted representation of creative associative knowledge, comparing with AI persona-based responses. It models creativity more comprehensively than single-task measures.

entry.title: Learning a Semantic Calibration Network for Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Yang Sun, Tao Wang, Anastasia Ioannou, Ge Xu

entry.summary: The Semantic Calibration Network refines mask classification for open-vocabulary semantic segmentation by explicitly modeling semantic correlations between classes rather than just feature aggregation or fine-tuning. It aims to enhance discriminative power for novel concepts.

entry.title: MAGIS: Evidence-Based Multi-Agent Reasoning for Interpretable Strabismus Clinical Decision-Making

author.name: Xikai Tang, Yifan Wang, Jiafan Zhuang, Li Luo, Jinming Guo, Xiaoling Xie, Jiacheng Liu, Peiwei Wei, Lihao Zhong, Xiaoli Kang, Jie Cen, Guangqiang Yin, Kunliang Qiu, Ce Zheng, Zhun Fan

entry.summary: MAGIS is a multi-agent reasoning framework for interpretable strabismus diagnosis that replaces black-box predictions with structured hypothesis generation and evidence-constrained reasoning to reduce hallucination. It targets a rule-driven medical imaging task requiring transparency.

entry.title: IB-HFN: Information Bottleneck-Driven SAR-Optical Fusion Network for High-Fidelity Cloud Removal

author.name: Haojun Guo, Fan Feng, Ziquan Wang

entry.summary: IB-HFN uses an information bottleneck to fuse SAR and optical imagery for cloud removal, employing a dual-stream backbone to preserve modality-specific features and avoid propagating SAR speckle noise. It targets high-fidelity surface reconstruction in remote sensing.

entry.title: Cranio-Diff: Diffusion-based Cross-domain Craniofacial Reconstruction with 2D X-ray Skull Guidance and Structural Identity Constraints

author.name: Ravi Shankar Prasad, Naresh Gurjar, Shashank Baghel, Chirag, Dinesh Singh

entry.summary: Cranio-Diff performs cross-domain craniofacial reconstruction from 2D X-ray skull images using a diffusion framework with ControlNet skull-conditioned structural guidance and biometric text conditioning. It addresses structural identity misalignment in skull-to-face translation.

entry.title: Assessing model calibration with boosting trees

author.name: Selim Gatti

entry.summary: This paper shows that boosting trees can test necessary conditions for model calibration and auto-calibration, where conditional mean estimates match true conditional means, important for applications like insurance pricing to avoid cross-subsidization. It connects gradient boosting to calibration assessment.

entry.title: How to build a cancer vaccine, and whether they will work this time

author.name: Abhishaike Mahajan

entry.summary: This essay explains the science of therapeutic cancer vaccines, distinguishing them from preventive vaccines against oncogenic viruses, and reviews why the field has largely failed over forty years and whether new approaches may finally succeed. It offers an accessible technical overview of cancer immunotherapy.

entry.title: Standpoint Logics with Defeasible Beliefs

author.name: Nicholas Leisegang, Thomas Meyer, Sebastian Rudolph

entry.summary: This paper integrates KLM defeasible logic with standpoint logic to formally represent multiple, possibly contradicting viewpoints that hold defeasible beliefs, providing a representation result and lifting entailment relations to the standpoint-enhanced setting. It advances formal knowledge representation for multi-perspective reasoning.

entry.title: ZIPP:Zero-shot Image Personalization from Personas

author.name: Harini SI, Somesh Singh, Yaman Kumar Singla, David Doermann, Rajiv Ratn Shah

entry.summary: ZIPP enables zero-shot personalization of text-to-image generation by conditioning on natural-language personas describing a user's aesthetic identity, avoiding per-user fine-tuning or dense interaction histories. It targets cold-start and pluralistic preference settings.

entry.title: MASS: Deep Research for Social Sciences with Memory-Augmented Social Simulation

author.name: Yongrui Liu, Deyi Xiong

entry.summary: MASS is a deep-research paradigm for social sciences that augments LLM idea generation with realistic, research-oriented social simulations to improve creativity and empirical grounding. It integrates goal-path planning under social norms with a multi-disciplinary simulation backbone.

entry.title: LLM-Orchestrated Conformance Checking in Stroke Care Without Computer-Interpretable Guidelines

author.name: Giorgio Leonardi, Stefania Montani, Manuel Striani, Alessandro Canessa, Delfina Ferrandi

entry.summary: This work introduces a modular LLM-orchestration framework for clinical conformance checking in stroke care that operates directly from unstructured clinical and guideline texts without requiring formal computer-interpretable guidelines. It extracts patient traces from discharge letters to assess guideline adherence.

entry.title: GraphLoRA: Structure-Aware Low-Rank Adaptation for Large Language Model Recommendation

author.name: Lin Mu, Guoji Wang, Li Ni, Lei Sang, Zhize Wu, Peiquan Jin, Yiwen Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces GraphLoRA, a structure-aware low-rank adaptation that embeds a trainable graph message-passing network within LoRA to capture high-order collaborative signals for LLM recommendation. Bridges textual semantics with structural collaborative information.

entry.title: Multimodal Large Language Models as Synthetic Participants in Video-Based Studies: An Evaluation

author.name: Prabal Shrestha, Bohan Jiang, Haoning Xue, Huan Liu, Xinyi Zhou

entry.summary: Evaluates whether multimodal LLMs can serve as synthetic participants approximating subjective human responses to short videos using the Perceived Message Sensation Value framework. Compares 673 profile-conditioned MLLM simulations against human ratings.

entry.title: SlideCheck: Guiding Self-Supervised Pretraining of Pathology Foundation Models via Dataset Distributions

author.name: Mingyi He, Xinyi Guo, Xitong Ling, Weiming Chen, Jiawen Li, Lianghui Zhu, Minxi Ouyang, Mingxi Fu, Yizhi Wang, Tian Guan

entry.summary: Proposes SlideCheck, a lightweight tool built on frozen pathology foundation-model features that provides abnormality and malignancy scores to organize, filter, and audit pretraining data for pathology foundation models. Addresses mismatch between patch-level data and slide-level supervision.

entry.title: Knowledge-Inclusive Adaptive Physics-Informed Neural Network for Microbial Interaction Modelling

author.name: Ravisha Rupasinghe, Rajith Vidanaarachchi, Asela Hevapathige, Sachith Seneviratne, Sen-Lin Tang, Saman Halgamuge

entry.summary: This work proposes a Physics-Informed Neural Network framework that augments equation-based parameter discovery with auxiliary knowledge from text and network structure, instantiated for generalized Lotka-Volterra microbial community modeling. Incorporating peer-reviewed knowledge improves parameter estimation.

entry.title: Model Multiplicity for Adversarial Detection in Small Language Model Training on Edge Devices

author.name: Stefan Behfar, Richard Mortier

entry.summary: This work proposes a model-multiplicity system-level defense for small language model training on edge devices, maintaining multiple models instead of one global model to detect coordinated or persistent poisoning. It targets stealthy adversarial updates in distributed edge finetuning.

entry.title: Impacts of Histories and Models on LLM Grading: A Study in Advanced Software Engineering Courses

author.name: Qilin Zhou, Zhuo Wang, Yue Li, W. K. Chan

entry.summary: This case study evaluates a human-aligned LLM-assisted grading workflow on 180 graduate software engineering submissions, comparing Grok and GPT for grading consistency and alignment with human scores. It finds distinct intra-model consistency and significant inter-model variation.

entry.title: Structuring agentic AI for HPC code modernization

author.name: Anthony Marinov, Igor Sfiligoi

entry.summary: Reports a successful two-phase AI-assisted modernization of a 60,000-line legacy Fortran scientific code into parallel C++ using structured agentic workflows. Finds raw LLM tools insufficient alone but effective when wrapped in structured agentic processes.

entry.title: PAI: Preserving Amplitude Information in Representation-Based Time-Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Kang Zhang, Wei Jian Lau, Shoushou Ren, Dong Lin, Joon Son Chung, Chuanhao Sun

entry.summary: PAI addresses amplitude-agnostic embeddings in representation-based time-series anomaly detection by adding a diagnostic module and score augmentation that restores amplitude sensitivity. Shows existing representation methods systematically lose amplitude information.

entry.title: Optimizing Energy-based Neural Network Training with Coherent Ising Machine

author.name: Chen-Rui Fan, Bo Lu, Zhi-Hong Zhang, Run-Qing Zhang, Jing-Wei Wen, Chuan Wang

entry.summary: Trains an energy-based neural network on a Coherent Ising Machine using Equilibrium Propagation, integrating the Adam optimizer to solve for Hopfield ground states and improve convergence. Demonstrates scalability of physical-hardware-based neural training.

entry.title: LargeMonitor: Monitoring Online Task-Free Continual Learning via Large Pretrained Models

author.name: Mingqi Yuan, Xiaoquan Sun, Shihao Luo, Jiayu Chen

entry.summary: Proposes LargeMonitor, a framework using large pretrained models to monitor distribution drift in online task-free continual learning, addressing the structure-agnostic nature of existing training-coupled solvers. It aims to adapt strategies to the structural origins of drift.

entry.title: Seeing the Hivemind: A Consensus-Aware Interaction Technique for Mitigating AI Homogenization

author.name: Muhammad Haris Khan, Joel wester

entry.summary: Introduces the Semantic Repulsion Technique to mitigate AI-driven homogenization of creative writing, increasing semantic diversity by 85-167% while reducing consensus phrases. A study with 16 participants found SRT outputs rated higher in usefulness and coherence.

entry.title: Visual Prompting Meets Feature Reconstruction-Based Anomaly Detection with Dual-Teacher Supervision

author.name: Mateo Diaz-Bone, Daniel Caraballo, Florian Scheidegger, Thomas Frick, Mattia Rigotti, Andrea Bartezzaghi, Roy Assaf, Niccolo Avogaro, Yagmur G. Cinar, Brown Ebouky, Filip M. Janicki, Piotr S. Kluska, Cezary Skura, Cristiano Malossi

entry.summary: Combines visual prompting with feature-reconstruction anomaly detection using foreground-background masking, dual-teacher supervision, and diffusion-generated augmentation to handle scale, viewpoint, and illumination variations. It targets real-world deployment scenarios where standard MVTec assumptions are violated.

entry.title: Data Synthesis and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Low-Resource NMT: A Case Study on Q'eqchi' Mayan

author.name: Alexander Chulzhanov, Soeren Eberhardt, Arjun Mukherjee

entry.summary: Introduces a data synthesis methodology for low-resource Indigenous NMT (Q'eqchi' Mayan) that transforms community dictionaries into a synthetic corpus, avoiding web-scraping for data sovereignty, using LoRA on mT5-base. Achieves high in-domain BLEU but reveals generalization gaps on organic glossaries.

entry.title: An Agency-Transferring Model-Free Policy Enhancement Technique

author.name: Anton Bolychev, Georgiy Malaniya, Sinan Ibrahim, Pavel Osinenko

entry.summary: Proposes an agency-transferring technique that embeds an existing suboptimal baseline policy into RL training, initially relying on the baseline and progressively transferring control to a learnable policy. It improves training efficiency over from-scratch methods while outperforming the baseline.

entry.title: QDSP: An Interpretable Structured Learning Framework for Predicting Death or Cerebral Palsy in Very Low Birth Weight Infants

author.name: Ling Wang, Xiaolong Li, Hui Zhou, Jing Shi, Fuhao Zhang, Dapeng Chen, Nan Mu

entry.summary: Proposes QDSP, an interpretable structured learning framework predicting death or cerebral palsy in very low birth weight infants, combining quota-guided subspace sampling with differentiable soft oblique decision structures. It targets reliable, traceable prognosis in high-dimensional data-limited clinical settings.

entry.title: CAAL: Contextual Bandits based Online Hand-Craft Active Learning Strategy Selection

author.name: Shao-An Yin, Jiacong Li, Tianpei Xie, Cecile Levasseur, Wojciech Kowalinski, Nicola Elia

entry.summary: Proposes CAAL, a contextual-bandit framework that dynamically selects among hand-crafted active learning strategies using external context for reward prediction. It outperforms a baseline adaptive strategy on several tasks.

entry.title: Neural Legendre-Fenchel transform with Hessian Preconditioning

author.name: Basile Plus-Gourdon, Frank Nielsen

entry.summary: Improves the neural Legendre-Fenchel transform method using Hessian-based preconditioning, leveraging the affine invariance of the projective-polarity reformulation to handle ill-conditioned functions. Enhances numerical computation of convex conjugates. Niche tool for convex analysis with neural networks.

entry.title: Efficient Traffic Prediction at Scale: A Systematic Study of STGCN Architectural Depth

author.name: Soban Nasir Lone, Mohamed Abouelela, Taeyoung Yu, Jiwon Kim, Constantinos Antoniou

entry.summary: Systematically studies whether STGCN traffic prediction architectures are over-parameterized, finding that a single-block variant achieves optimal performance across four datasets compared to standard deeper variants. Suggests efficiency gains for ITS deployment. Empirical architecture study.

entry.title: Transfer learning for causal forest

author.name: B\'er\'enice-Alexia Jocteur (ICJ, PSPM), V\'eronique Maume-Deschamps (ICJ, PSPM), Pierre Ribereau (PSPM, ICJ)

entry.summary: Adapts an offset-based transfer learning method to causal forests (HTERF) for estimating Conditional Average Treatment Effects under model shift between source and target domains. Provides a theoretical bound on the transfer error.

entry.title: Latent Structural Categorical Matrix Completion with Application to Quasispecies Analysis

author.name: Qian Zhang, Meixia Lin

entry.summary: Proposes LCMC, a double-loop optimization framework for categorical matrix completion via latent factorization on a binary tensor representation that preserves the discrete non-ordinal nature of categories. Adaptively estimates latent dimension and applies the method to quasispecies (viral variant) analysis.

entry.title: Towards End to End Motion Planning and Execution for Autonomous Underwater Vehicles Using Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Elisei Shafer, Oren Gal

entry.summary: Explores end-to-end deep RL for autonomous underwater vehicles, mapping raw camera, sonar, and proprioceptive sensor data directly to thruster commands via a hierarchical two-level policy. Reduces reliance on heavily engineered perception-planning-control pipelines.

entry.title: Weighted universal approximation of differentiable maps on infinite-dimensional manifolds

author.name: Philipp Schmocker, Josef Teichmann

entry.summary: Generalizes the universal approximation theorem for functional neural networks to differentiable maps on infinite-dimensional manifolds, including approximation of derivatives via a weighted Nachbin theorem. Extends theory beyond compact sets to non-anticipative functionals.

entry.title: ZAS-SQL: Distilling Rules from Failures for Zero-Shot Text-to-SQL

author.name: Hongzhou Zheng, Yixin Gou, Wenjia Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes ZAS-SQL, a fully zero-shot Text-to-SQL framework that distills recurring failure patterns into generation rules via a Map-Reduce pipeline. Aims to close the gap with few-shot methods without consuming context window for demonstrations.

entry.title: Language-Aware Token Boosting: LLM Language Confusion Reduction Without Tuning

author.name: Trapoom Ukarapol, Pakhapoom Sarapat, Nut Chukamphaeng

entry.summary: Proposes tuning-free Language-Aware Token Boosting and an adaptive variant that perturb tokens associated with the desired language to reduce LLM language confusion without fine-tuning. Improves multilingual alignment while preserving summarization quality.

entry.title: MAAM: Anchor-Preserving Compression and Contextual Calibration for Chinese Discriminatory Language Detection

author.name: Yuxin Fu, Shijing Si

entry.summary: Proposes MAAM, a lightweight model-agnostic framework retaining discrimination-relevant semantic anchors with contextual priors for Chinese discriminatory-language detection, and introduces ChLGBT, a first Chinese LGBT-focused dataset of 8,120 annotated samples. Improves detection of implicit, context-dependent bias.

entry.title: One Model, Multiple Goals: Adaptive Multi-Objective Learning for E-commerce Dialogue Systems

author.name: Mingzhe Li, Jing Xiang, Enguo Zhou, Lang Gao, Tai Li, Qishen Zhang, Xiangliang Zhang, Xiuying Chen

entry.summary: MORE is an adaptive multi-objective reinforcement learning framework for e-commerce dialogue that jointly optimizes reasoning accuracy and linguistic naturalness by treating reasoning as constraints rather than mixed rewards. This avoids unstable learning from conflicting reward dynamics.

entry.title: DECSELFMASK: Leveraging Unlabeled Text via Self-Relevance-Guided Masking for Decoder-Only Classification

author.name: Pietro Ferrazzi, Matteo Merler, Giovanni Bonetta, Alberto Lavelli, Bernardo Magnini

entry.summary: DecSelfMask enhances decoder-only model classification on low-annotation tasks by using relevance attribution to identify and mask task-relevant text portions, creating self-supervised training examples from unlabeled data. It targets domains like medicine with scarce annotations.

entry.title: Assessing the Energy and Carbon Emissions of Neural Speaker Verification Model in Training and Inference

author.name: Hugo Leguillier, Driss Matrouf, Guillaume Lechien, Mickael Rouvier

entry.summary: Assesses energy consumption and carbon footprint of neural speaker verification ResNet architectures across depth, width, and stage distribution, finding clear diminishing returns where mid-sized models offer favorable performance-environment trade-offs. It provides actionable guidelines for energy-efficient design.

entry.title: Paediatric-HGNN: A Hybrid Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network for Detecting Disfluency in Children's Speech via Multiscale Acoustic Fusion

author.name: Rashini Liyanarachchi, Rachael Mackay, Alison Short, Aditya Joshi, Erik Meijering

entry.summary: Paediatric-HGNN is a hybrid heterogeneous graph neural network for detecting disfluency in children's speech, building graphs that capture hierarchical relationships between word and acoustic frame nodes. It addresses high acoustic variability in developing voices.

entry.title: Interpretable Crisis Behavior Analysis Using Mobility and Social Media Data

author.name: Muhammad Hamza Arshad Majeed, Sidahmed Benabderrahmane, Talal Rahwan

entry.summary: Presents an interpretable pipeline integrating mobility and social media data to identify cross-domain behavioral patterns in crisis settings, evaluated on the 2025 LA wildfires and UAE COVID-19 behavior over 671 days. It jointly studies movement and emotional discourse usually studied in isolation.

entry.title: FADRW: A Feature-Aware Modulated and Dynamically Reweighted Loss for Few-Shot Linguistic Steganalysis

author.name: Shuo Liu, Xianghong Lin, Yukun Wei, Zhongliang Yang

entry.summary: FADRW is a feature-aware modulated and dynamically reweighted loss for few-shot linguistic steganalysis that addresses extreme class imbalance and feature marginalization of near-invisible steganographic signals. It operates at the optimization level rather than data resampling.

entry.title: Gray-Box Optimization and the Vertex Coloring Problem

author.name: Johanna Gasse, Antonia Heinen, Hendrik Higl, Timo K\"otzing

entry.summary: This theoretical work analyzes gray-box optimization for the vertex coloring problem, proving RLS can find a proper 2-coloring of bipartite graphs in expected O(n log n) time while the (1+1) EA cannot from an n-coloring start without guidance. It explores the continuum between black-box and tailored algorithms.

entry.title: Quality-Diversity Search in Sound Generation: Investigating Innovation Engines for Audio Exploration

author.name: Bj\"orn {\TH}\'or J\'onsson, \c{C}a\u{g}r{\i} Erdem, Stefano Fasciani, Kyrre Glette

entry.summary: This study applies Quality-Diversity algorithms with a supervised discriminative model, inspired by Innovation Engines, to automate exploration of sonic spaces for sound generation and synthesis. It argues diversity-promoting algorithms aid composers in discovering novel sounds.

entry.title: Safe, Fluent and Acceptable Motion Generation and Execution for Human--Robot Interaction in Manufacturing Environments

author.name: Thibaut Lopez, Olivier Aycard, Pierre-Brice Wieber, Mohamed Boua, Christine Jeoffrion

entry.summary: This work investigates motion generation strategies for human-robot interaction in manufacturing that combine safety guarantees with interaction quality such as smoothness, comfort, and social acceptability. It argues for integrating psycho-cognitive and social perspectives into robot behavior design.

entry.title: A Variability-Based Framework for Interpretable Naming in Formal and Relational Concept Analysis

author.name: Alain Gutierrez, Marianne Huchard, Pierre Martin, Andr\'e Miralles, Violaine Prince

entry.summary: This paper proposes a variability-based framework for assigning interpretable, meaningful names to concepts produced by Formal and Relational Concept Analysis, which are otherwise labeled with opaque technical identifiers. It improves human interpretation, navigation, and reuse of symbolic knowledge structures.

entry.title: Agent Economics: An Entropy-Controlled Pluralistic Alignment Framework for Preventing Artificial Hivemind in Autonomous Agents

author.name: Cheonsu Jeong

entry.summary: The Behavioral Protocol Framework is an entropy-controlled pluralistic alignment framework to prevent hivemind-like strategic convergence among autonomous agents, combining Theory-of-Mind social intelligence, pluralistic alignment, and a verifiable execution kernel. It targets transparency and diversity in agent economies.

entry.title: Collaborative Human-Agent Protocol (CHAP)

author.name: Arsalan Shahid, Gordon Suttie, Philip Black

entry.summary: CHAP is a proposed protocol for multi-human, multi-agent collaboration that captures human judgement moments—such as edits to agent drafts—as first-class signals rather than leaving them buried in application code or chat threads. It addresses the weakly specified technical surface of production human-agent collaboration.

entry.title: BEACON: Behavioral Entropy Aggregation for Cross-Model Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models

author.name: Naveen Bera, Pulijala Sai Nikhila, Kondaguduru Abhiram, Shaik Gayaz Ali, Shoaib Sadiq Salehmohamed, Shaik Mohammed Omar, Jinal Prashant Thakkar, Hansika Aredla, Shalmali Ayachit

entry.summary: Presents BEACON, a black-box hallucination detector using a 31-dimensional feature vector from multi-pass generation (semantic entropy, embedding geometry, CoT consistency, paraphrase stability) fed to a gradient-boosted classifier. Achieves around 0.81 AUC across seven benchmarks without internal access.

entry.title: SRT: Super-Resolution for Time Series via Disentangled Rectified Flow

author.name: Jufang Duan, Shenglong Xiao, Yuren Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes SRT, a time-series super-resolution framework reconstructing high-resolution signals from low-resolution inputs via disentangled rectified flow that separates trend and other components. Adapts super-resolution concepts from vision to temporal data.

entry.title: NeuroAlign: Hierarchical Multimodal Fusion of Dynamic and Structural Neuroimaging for MCI Analysis

author.name: Xiongri Shen, Zhenxi Song, Jiaqi wang, Yi Zhong, Leilei Zhao, Chenqi Xu, Linling Li, Yichen Wei, Lingyan Liang, Demao Deng, Luping Song, Ping Luan, Ahmed M. Anter, Shuqiang Wang, Baiying Lei, Zhiguo Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes NeuroAlign, a hierarchical multimodal fusion framework aligning dynamic functional MRI and structural DTI for mild cognitive impairment analysis via dual-modal hierarchical alignment and dual-domain interaction modules. Addresses heterogeneous feature spaces and misaligned representations.

entry.title: Memetic Capture: A Pluralistic Policy Framework for Governing AI-Driven Cultural Disempowerment

author.name: Subramanyam Sahoo

entry.summary: This conceptual paper introduces memetic capture as a framework for AI-driven cultural disempowerment and proposes a four-tier Cultural Pluralistic Governance Framework with cultural influence metrics, democratic value assemblies, and transnational cooperation. It argues cultural impact is a critical blind spot in AI governance.

entry.title: Voting Protocols as Coordination Mechanisms for Role-Constrained Multi-Agent Tutoring Systems

author.name: Eric S. Qiu, Joyce Gill

entry.summary: This work studies voting protocols as coordination mechanisms among four role-constrained pedagogical agents (scaffolding, misconception, motivation, metacognition) in multi-agent tutoring, comparing simple, ranked, cumulative, and approval voting. It analyzes how collective decision rules shape coordination under pedagogical conflict across SciQ and HumanEval.

entry.title: SafeRun: Enabling Determinism in LLM Planning for Running

author.name: Meilin Chen, Zepeng Zhai, Jiaxuan Zhao, Yuan Lu

entry.summary: SafeRun enables deterministic LLM-based planning for running training by decoupling soft LLM interpretation from hard constraint enforcement via a deterministic solver. It provides safety-constraint guarantees while preserving natural-language flexibility, with a dedicated benchmark.

entry.title: Physics-Guided Sequence-Based Generative Framework for Acoustic Metamaterial Inverse Design

author.name: Yijie Li, Jiahao Xu, Ching-Chih Tsao, Lili Qiu, Jingxian Wang

entry.summary: Presents MetaSeq, a physics-guided sequence-based generative framework for acoustic metamaterial inverse design that represents structures as token sequences to preserve geometric precision. It tackles broadband design challenges from acoustic dispersion that template- or image-based methods struggle with.

entry.title: ATN3D: Density-Aware LiDAR-Radar Early 3D Object Detection Under Extreme Sparsity

author.name: Debojyoti Biswas, Xianbiao Hu

entry.summary: Introduces ATN3D, a density-aware LiDAR-radar early-fusion 3D detection framework targeting long-range objects under extreme sparsity for autonomous vehicles. It addresses noise injection from early fusion and context-agnostic supervision that under-optimizes far and small objects.

entry.title: Optimality of Sequential Filtering Under Independent Cost and Selectivity Models

author.name: Hrishikesh Paranjape, Abhishek Mandal, Xian Sun

entry.summary: Formalizes sequential filtering pipelines under an expected-cost objective and proves that, under independence, ordering filters by increasing cost-to-rejection-probability ratio minimizes expected total cost. Monte Carlo simulations confirm the optimal ordering strictly dominates common heuristics.

entry.title: Overcoming the Limits of Finite Difference Method; Physics-Informed Neural Network for Noisy High-Dimensional Heat Diffusion

author.name: Shreesh Bhattarai, Harish Chandra Bhandari

entry.summary: Demonstrates that Physics-Informed Neural Networks substantially outperform finite difference methods for high-dimensional heat diffusion under noisy boundary conditions, sustaining ~91% accuracy at 20% noise in 3D versus FDM collapse. It maps operational regimes where PINNs are preferable.

entry.title: From inverse problems to neural operators: prediction, mechanism, and generalization of data-driven models

author.name: Conor Rowan

entry.summary: A survey/perspective connecting inverse problems to neural operators, comparing scientific ML modeling strategies like SINDy and Neural ODEs in terms of prediction, mechanism, and generalization. Provides organizing framework for data-driven physical modeling. Educational and synthesizing contribution.

entry.title: Community-Specific Slang and Entity Detection via Semantic Shift in Fine-Tuned Language Models

author.name: Julia Kruk, Sanchita Porwal, Amitrajit Bhattacharjee, Mansi Phute

entry.summary: Proposes an unsupervised method to detect community-specific slang and entities by measuring semantic shift, the drop in cosine similarity between base and community-fine-tuned model word representations, validated on three Reddit subreddits. Useful for sociolinguistic and community NLP. Lightweight interpretive method.

entry.title: Improving the sharpness in neural network-based parametric post-processing of ensemble forecasts

author.name: \'Agnes Baran, M\'at\'e Mihalina

entry.summary: Extends neural-network-based parametric post-processing of ensemble weather forecasts with a sharpness penalty term in the loss function to counteract the over-widening of prediction intervals that calibration usually causes. Demonstrates improved sharpness especially at short lead times.

entry.title: Evaluating RAG Reliability under Clean, Misleading, and Mixed Retrieval

author.name: Sevgi Yigit-Sert

entry.summary: Proposes an evaluation protocol to systematically test how RAG systems handle conflicts between parametric knowledge and retrieved evidence under clean, poisoned, and mixed conditions. Focuses on misinformation robustness for factoid questions the model already answers correctly.

entry.title: AlignFed: Alignment-Aware Asynchronous Federated Fine-Tuning for Large Language Models in Heterogeneous Edge Environments

author.name: Yan Wang, Ziyi Gao, Rui Wang

entry.summary: Proposes AlignFed, an alignment-aware asynchronous federated fine-tuning method for LLMs in heterogeneous edge environments addressing privacy, non-IID data, and straggler effects. Targets collaborative on-device LLM adaptation without raw data sharing.

entry.title: On Low-Bit Quantization Errors in Speaker Verification: Diagnostic and Mitigation

author.name: Hugo Leguillier, Driss Matrouf, Guillaume Lechien, Mickael Rouvier

entry.summary: Studies low-bit quantization errors in speaker verification through layer-wise and score-level analysis of ResNet models, identifying a knee point at 2 bits with harmful decision flips near the decision threshold. It proposes a calibration-based mitigation.

entry.title: Aqua Boundary-Saliency Attention Module for Lightweight Underwater Salient Instance Segmentation Detection Transformer

author.name: M. Fazri Nizar, Julian Supardi, Muhammad Naufal Rachmatullah

entry.summary: LUSIS-DETR is a lightweight detection-transformer for underwater salient instance segmentation built around an Aqua Boundary-Saliency Attention Module that embeds underwater-specific cues like attenuation, chroma, and dark-channel priors. It avoids reliance on large foundation models or prompts for efficient deployment.

entry.title: An Opticalmechanics Framework for Dynamic Estimation of Multibody Systems

author.name: Banglei Guan, Xuanyu Bai, Qingquan Chen, Zibin Liu, Dongcai Tan, Zhenbao Yu, Yang Shang, Qifeng Yu

entry.summary: This work proposes an optical-mechanics framework that integrates image-measured kinematics with a constrained multibody model to estimate joint torques without contact force sensors. Joint torque is identified via genetic-algorithm optimization minimizing kinematic discrepancy.

entry.title: Feasibility to detect rapid change and disappearance of seagrass: Lessons from nearly 80 years of vegetation change in the Ako, Seto Inland Sea, Japan

author.name: Takehisa Yamakita, Yoji Igarashi, Akira Eto, Ken Ishida, Masaaki Iiyama

entry.summary: This study reconstructs roughly 80 years of seagrass distribution at a Japanese tidal flat using historical aerial photos and satellite imagery with YOLO-based segmentation, documenting near-total disappearance of Zostera marina in 2025. It assesses the feasibility of detecting rapid vegetation change.

entry.title: From Validator Selection to Portfolio Collection Optimization in Proof-of-Stake Blockchains

author.name: Jonas Gehrlein, Grzegorz Miebs, Matteo Brunelli, Adam Mielniczuk, Mi{\l}osz Kadzi\'nski

entry.summary: This paper reformulates validator selection in proof-of-stake blockchains as a multi-criteria portfolio optimization problem, simultaneously maximizing expected validator utility and allocation entropy for risk diversification. It offers a decision-support framework for nominators operating across multiple accounts.

entry.title: Quantitative Promise Theory: Intentionality and Inference in Autonomous Agents

author.name: Mark Burgess

entry.summary: This paper develops quantitative representations of Promise Theory for autonomous-agent systems, incorporating Bayesian probability, information-theoretic optimization, and Active Inference while using promise semantics to avoid probability pitfalls like non-local coordination. It connects agent alignment to boundary-condition constraints on allowed states.

entry.title: The Token Not Taken: Sampling, State, and the Variability of AI Agent Outputs

author.name: Muhammad Zia Hydari, Raja Iqbal

entry.summary: This conceptual paper disentangles the layered sources of variability in agentic AI outputs—token sampling, orchestration state, tool calls—that are often conflated. It clarifies how nondeterminism arises across the agent stack.

entry.title: BRAIN: Bayesian Reasoning via Active Inference for Agentic and Embodied Intelligence in Mobile Networks

author.name: Osman Tugay Basaran, Martin Maier, Falko Dressler

entry.summary: BRAIN proposes a Bayesian reasoning via Active Inference agent for 6G mobile networks, using a deep generative environment model to provide explainable, adaptable decision-making that resists catastrophic forgetting under non-stationary conditions. It offers an alternative to brittle DRL-based networking agents.

entry.title: CAPruner: Conceptual-Adjacent Scene Graph Pruner for Enhancing 3D Spatial Reasoning of Large Language Models

author.name: Shengli Zhou, Xiangchen Wang, Guanhua Chen, Feng Zheng

entry.summary: Proposes CAPruner, a conceptual-adjacency scene graph pruner that preserves task-relevant spatial relations to improve 3D spatial reasoning of LLMs while reducing token cost. Addresses a key inefficiency in 3D vision-language tasks.

entry.title: A Topological Characterization of Graph Neural Networks via Stochastic Block Model Embeddings on the n-Sphere

author.name: Gopal Anantharaman

entry.summary: Proposes a topological framework comparing trained GNNs by mapping induced stochastic block models onto the n-sphere, grounded in graphon cut-distance compactness and weak regularity lemmas. Offers a theoretical characterization of message-passing networks.

entry.title: Eyes All Around: Design and Analysis of 360-Degree LiDAR Perception Using Equivariant Feature Learning in Unstructured Traffic

author.name: Pranav Darshan, Raghuveer Narayanan Rajesh, M Uttara Kumari

entry.summary: Studies a 360-degree LiDAR perception pipeline for autonomous driving in dense unstructured traffic, using panoramic sensing, azimuthal sector-wise processing, and transformation-equivariant feature extraction. Addresses occlusions and irregular motion absent from structured-road benchmarks.

entry.title: EvoCSFL: Surrogate-Assisted Evolutionary Client Selection for Efficient and Robust Federated Learning

author.name: Lin Qiang, Sun Xiaoyan, Hu Yao, Fang Wei

entry.summary: EvoCSFL is a surrogate-assisted evolutionary client selection framework for federated learning that formulates selection as combinatorial optimization over model performance, latency, and energy. A surrogate model approximates selection performance to improve convergence and robustness under heterogeneity.

entry.title: Post-AGI Economies: Superposition and the Second Fundamental Theorem of Welfare Economics

author.name: Elija Perrier

entry.summary: This conceptual paper extends the Second Welfare Theorem to post-AGI economies, proposing an autonomy-qualified version stating conditions under which an autonomy Pareto optimum remains decentralizable. It addresses how autonomy rights, self-modification, and superposed preferences may break classical welfare economics assumptions.

entry.title: Evaluating AI Investment Strategies

author.name: Irene Aldridge

entry.summary: Provides an exact decomposition for auditing black-box dynamic decision-makers, showing cumulative regret equals the sum of per-period covariances between cost and decision. Extends a single-period identity to full multi-period stochastic dynamic programming.

entry.title: Addressing Market Regime Changes and Heavy-Tailed Returns in Portfolio Optimization via Bayesian VAR and Elliptical Black-Litterman

author.name: Daniil Mikriukov (University of Liverpool, Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University), Ruoyu Sun (Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University), Angelos Stefanidis (Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University), Jionglong Su (Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University), Zhengyong Jiang (Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University)

entry.summary: BAVAR-BLED combines Bayesian-averaging vector autoregression and an elliptical Black-Litterman model within a TD3 deep RL architecture for portfolio optimization. It addresses fat-tailed returns and market regime changes that standard DRL portfolio models ignore.

entry.title: CANS: Accelerating Multiuser Collaborative Edge Inference via Cooperative Autodidactic NeuroSurgeon

author.name: Zheshun Wu, Ziyang Zhang, Changyao Lin, Zenglin Xu, Jie Liu

entry.summary: CANS accelerates multi-user collaborative edge inference by learning optimal DNN partitioning under unknown and time-varying wireless and device conditions via a cooperative autodidactic NeuroSurgeon framework. Targets resource-constrained mobile edge computing scenarios.

entry.title: BSTabDiff: Block-Subunit Diffusion Priors for High-Dimensional Tabular Data Generation

author.name: Al Zadid Sultan Bin Habib, Md Younus Ahamed, Prashnna Gyawali, Gianfranco Doretto, Donald A. Adjeroh

entry.summary: Introduces BSTabDiff, a block-subunit diffusion framework for generating high-dimensional low-sample tabular data such as omics, partitioning features into latent blocks generated via shared low-dimensional subunits. It targets ill-conditioned density learning where features vastly outnumber samples.

entry.title: AI Assurance in UK Defence: Challenges in Operationalising JSP 936

author.name: Callum Cockburn, Sam Farrow

entry.summary: Argues that robot middleware should be recognized as the harness layer for Physical AI, mediating learned policies, planners, and VLA models at control, computing, and network boundaries. It transfers the language-agent harness framing to robotics.

entry.title: MST-Direct at Scale: Multivariate and Conditional Geostatistical Simulation via Sinkhorn Optimal Transport

author.name: Tcharlies Bachmann Schmitz

entry.summary: Extends MST-Direct, a Sinkhorn optimal-transport approach for multivariate geostatistical simulation, to conditional, multivariate, large-grid settings via a sparse candidate-restricted matcher with linear memory complexity. It adds hard-data conditioning by fixing observed tuples and conditioning the Gaussian backbone through kriging.

entry.title: Learning Transfers: Kan Extensions for Neural Invariants

author.name: Luciano Melodia

entry.summary: Develops a category-theoretic formalization of transfer learning using Kan extensions to define the universal transferred invariant and a transfer discrepancy measure. It aims to specify precisely which structural invariant should carry over between source and target tasks.

entry.title: TRUST-SCF: Transformer-based Risk Understanding and Scoring for Transactional Supply Chain Finance

author.name: Mohammadamin Davoodabadi, Amirabbas Shakeri

entry.summary: Proposes TRUST-SCF, a transformer for transaction-level credit risk and dynamic scoring in supply chain finance, with a financially aligned attention bias combining utilization similarity and recency plus continuous repayment-delay prediction. It targets evolving exposure in LendTech platforms.

entry.title: BrainSurgery: Reproducible and Reliable Declarative Weight Manipulations for Model Editing and Upcycling

author.name: Gianluca Barmina, Annemette Broch Pirchert, Andrea Blasi N\'u\~nez, Lukas Galke Poech, Peter Schneider-Kamp

entry.summary: Introduces BrainSurgery, a tool for reproducible declarative weight manipulations on neural network checkpoints via YAML plans, supporting layer restructuring, precision casting, low-rank factorization, and LoRA extraction. Replaces fragile ad-hoc scripts. Useful infrastructure for model editing and upcycling.

entry.title: Zero Touch Predictive Orchestration: Automating Time-Series Models for the Cloud-Edge Continuum

author.name: Abd Elghani Meliani, Arora Sagar, Adlen Ksentini, Raymond Knopp

entry.summary: Proposes a fully automated time-series prediction architecture for the Cloud-Edge Continuum that solves the cold-start problem for newly discovered nodes via a data-mixing methodology and a lightweight Resource Exposer. Enables proactive Zero Touch Management. Applied systems/forecasting contribution.

entry.title: A systematic investigation of molecular encoding methods for drug property predictions across neural network and Transformer encoder-based model

author.name: Sheng-Ya Chen, Shan-Ju Yeh

entry.summary: Systematically investigates how different molecular encoding methods (topological, substructure-based, and string-based fingerprints) affect drug property prediction across an MLP and a Transformer-encoder model on seven datasets. Provides guidance on optimal encodings for molecular property prediction.

entry.title: Integrating gene regulatory priors into Transformer attention with scTransformer for interpretable scRNA-seq analysis

author.name: Mikele Milia, Louis Fabrice Tshimanga, Henning Mueller, Manfredo Atzori, Barbara Di Camillo

entry.summary: Presents scTransformer, which embeds known gene regulatory structure into transformer attention to improve interpretability and robustness in single-cell RNA-seq analysis. Tests whether biological priors aid both performance and insight.

entry.title: ROSUM-MCTS: Monte Carlo Tree Search-Inspired HDL Code Summarization with Structural Rewards

author.name: Prashanth Vijayaraghavan, Charles Mackin, Luyao Shi, Apoorva Nitsure, Ashutosh Jadhav, David Beymer, Tyler Baldwin, Ehsan Degan, Vandana Mukherjee

entry.summary: Proposes ROSUM-MCTS, an MCTS-inspired LLM approach for hardware description language code summarization using structural rewards balancing functional correctness, content adequacy, and fluency. Targets the underexplored HDL summarization domain.

entry.title: ClinicalAligner26AM: A Cross-Lingual Aligner for Dataset Translation; Evidences from the MultiClinCorpus Shared Task

author.name: Fran\c{c}ois Remy

entry.summary: Introduces ClinicalAligner26AM, a large-context multilingual word-alignment model for biomedical and clinical text trained via Sinkhorn optimal-transport sharpening and distillation of fused multi-level alignment signals. Targets specialized-domain cross-lingual annotation projection.

entry.title: How Far Can Prompting Go for Minimal-Edit Ukrainian Grammatical Error Correction?

author.name: Kateryna Karpo, Artem Chernodub

entry.summary: Evaluates 11 commercial and one open-source LLM on Ukrainian minimal-edit grammatical error correction, finding the best configuration closes over 90% of the gap to fine-tuned state of the art. It shows language-specific minimal-edit prompts outperform other strategies.

entry.title: Trustworthy Visual Predicates for Robust Manipulation Understanding under Degradation

author.name: Fatemeh Ziaeetabar

entry.summary: This paper proposes a predicate-level reliability framework for manipulation understanding, measuring how visual relational predicates (contact, grasp, support) degrade under blur, occlusion, and noise. It provides confidence-aware metrics for robustness analysis.

entry.title: Self-supervised Learning Matters: A Simple Ensemble Solution for Micro-Gesture Recognition

author.name: Tingyi Liu, Kun Li, Fei Wang, Junjie Chen, Zhiliang Wu, Jihao Gu, Haixu Liu, Dan Guo

entry.summary: A challenge-winning ensemble for micro-gesture recognition combines a self-supervised masked-video-modeling RGB model with supervised multi-stream models. The self-supervised RGB baseline alone achieves strong accuracy, demonstrating value of in-domain unlabeled pretraining.

entry.title: Frequency-Scale Saliency for Spectral Descriptor Analysis in 3D Shape Retrieval

author.name: Jianru Shen

entry.summary: This work introduces a frequency-scale saliency framework to audit classical spectral descriptors (HKS, WKS) for 3D shape retrieval by quantifying each scale interval's contribution via ablation. It finds short scales dominate retrieval while long scales can harm performance.

entry.title: Systems-Level Planning and Coordination of Truck-Drone Collaborative Delivery Networks

author.name: Didem Cicek, Burak Kantarci

entry.summary: This paper proposes a five-layer planning and coordination framework for truck-drone collaborative last-mile delivery from a systems and control perspective, spanning spatial-demand alignment to scalable orchestration. It treats the problem as a networked cyber-physical delivery paradigm.

entry.title: Integrating Deep Learning Demand Forecasting with Multi-Objective Optimization for Circular Coffee Supply Chains: A Data-Driven Framework for Cost, Emissions, and Freshness Management

author.name: Ger\c{c}ek Budak (Department of Industrial Engineering, Ankara Y{\i}ld{\i}r{\i}m Beyaz{\i}t University, Ke\c{c}i\"oren, Ankara 06010, T\"urkiye), Faraz Gholamzadeh Gharehgheshlaghi (Department of Industrial Engineering, Ankara Y{\i}ld{\i}r{\i}m Beyaz{\i}t University, Ke\c{c}i\"oren, Ankara 06010, T\"urkiye), Melika Barjesteh Vaezi (Department of Kinesiology and Sport Management, Texas Tech University, Lubbock, TX, United States), Ahmad Gholizadeh Lonbar (Department of Civil, Construction, and Environmental Engineering, University of Alabama, Tuscaloosa, AL, USA)

entry.summary: This work integrates a CNN-LSTM demand-forecasting model with tri-objective mixed-integer optimization for circular coffee supply chains, balancing cost, emissions, and freshness. It reports strong forecasting accuracy and connects forecasting, optimization, and traceability often treated separately.

entry.title: A Multi-Agent System for IPMSM Design Optimization via an FEA-AI Hybrid Approach

author.name: Jinseong Han, Sunwoong Yang, Namwoo Kang

entry.summary: This work proposes a multi-agent IPMSM motor design optimization framework integrating retrieval-augmented generation for problem definition with an uncertainty-aware FEA-AI hybrid optimization pipeline. A RAG-connected design agent provides domain knowledge to automate setup.

entry.title: From Coarse to Fine: Managing Temporal Granularity in Spatio-Temporal Data for Fine-Grained Traffic Prediction

author.name: Shuhao Li, Weidong Yang, Yue Cui, Zizhuo Xu, Lipeng Ma, Fan Zhang, Xiaofang Zhou

entry.summary: This work formulates predicting fine-grained future traffic from coarse-grained sampled data to address temporal granularity mismatch in spatio-temporal data systems, reducing storage and computation costs. It proposes a spatial-temporal model for this novel problem.

entry.title: mllm-shap: A Shapley Value Explainability Platform for Text-Audio Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Jakub Muszy\'nski, Pawe{\l} Pozorski, Maria Ganzha

entry.summary: Introduces mllm-shap, an open-source framework extending Shapley value explainability to text-audio multimodal LLMs, with modality-aware masking, multi-turn tracking, and phonetic alignment-based grouping that cuts coalition space 10x-50x. Makes SV estimation feasible for multimodal models.

entry.title: Accelerating Birkhoff Projection for Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections

author.name: Chenrui Wang, Yixuan Qiu

entry.summary: Develops an accelerated, accurate end-to-end Birkhoff projection for 4x4 manifold-constrained hyper-connections, replacing slow Sinkhorn-Knopp iteration unrolling that adds compute and memory overhead. Improves stability guarantees of doubly-stochastic residual mixing.

entry.title: Outage Detection in Self-Healing Smart Grids Using Reinforcement Learning with Spectral Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Lihui Liu, Mucun Sun, Caisheng Wang

entry.summary: Combines reinforcement learning with spectral graph neural networks for outage detection and network reconfiguration in self-healing smart grids, capturing relational structure that spatial GNNs miss. Targets fast, low-cost outage mitigation.

entry.title: Structured Neuron Pruning in Deep Neural Networks Using Multi-Armed Bandits

author.name: Salem Ameen, Sunil Vadera

entry.summary: Develops a structured neuron pruning framework treating each candidate neuron as a multi-armed bandit arm, using policies like UCB1, Thompson Sampling, and Hedge to estimate safe-removal rewards from loss changes. Enables hardware-friendly structured sparsity.

entry.title: DSFNet: Learning Dual-Domain Spectral Operators for Multi-Modality Spatio-Temporal Forecasting in Urban Transportation Systems

author.name: Yongchao Li, Yang Li, Zhuoxuan Li, Jun Chen, Chu Zhang, Jinde Cao, Leszek Rutkowski

entry.summary: DSFNet is a dual-domain spectral filtering network for multi-modality spatio-temporal traffic forecasting that explicitly models cross-variable couplings across modalities and heterogeneous spatial dependencies. It targets urban transportation forecasting under exogenous influences.

entry.title: SHIELD-IDS: Structurally Heterogeneous Ensemble with Integrated Layered Defense for Intrusion Detection Systems

author.name: Maryam Zaman, Muhammad Khuram Shahzad

entry.summary: SHIELD-IDS (IDS-Anta++) extends an adversarially robust intrusion detection ensemble with XGBoost and LightGBM models wrapped in a three-layer black-box defense including isolation-forest anomaly detection. It improves structural diversity for resistance against adversarial network-flow perturbations.

entry.title: AeroSpectra Sentinel: An Auditable LLM Prompt-Chaining Decision-Support Workflow for Acute Asthma Risk Assessment from Respiratory Sounds and Clinical Signals

author.name: Aueaphum Aueawatthanaphisut

entry.summary: AeroSpectra Sentinel is a client-side decision-support prototype for acute asthma risk assessment combining STFT respiratory sound analysis, lightweight ML screening, and a five-stage LLM prompt-chaining workflow. It emphasizes auditable, transparent clinical reasoning and safe escalation logic.

entry.title: Failure-Aware Refinement of Vision-Language Model for Lithography Defect Detection

author.name: Pangyun Jeong, Jiyeong Kong, Yuehua Hu, Dohee Jeong, Kyung-Tae Kang

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage vision-language framework for semiconductor lithography defect detection: LoRA-fine-tuned Qwen3-VL predicts defects, then a refinement module trained on first-stage failures corrects errors. Targets false positives, missed defects, and misclassifications.

entry.title: Decoding Pedestrian Crossing Intention from Egocentric Vision via Vision Language Models

author.name: Danya Li, Xiang Su, Yan Feng, Rico Krueger

entry.summary: Studies decoding pedestrian crossing intentions from egocentric video by framing it as closed-ended VQA and benchmarking VLMs, finding zero-shot models exceed chance but lack higher-level traffic reasoning. Adapts VLMs via parameter-efficient fine-tuning for improvement.

entry.title: PhysScene: A Scene Graph Dataset for Scientific Visual Reasoning in Physics Experiments

author.name: Minghao Zou, Qingtian Zeng, Shangkun Liu, Yanda Meng, Guanghui Yue, Baoquan Zhao, Abdulmotaleb El Saddik, Wei Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces PhysScene, the first scene graph dataset for physics experiment scenes capturing specialized instruments and functional relations. It enables evaluation of relational reasoning in scientific experimental contexts underserved by generic datasets.

entry.title: Shape Formation for the Cooperative Transportation of Arbitrary Objects Using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Mohamed Sayed, Wolfram Burgard, Tanja Katharina Kaiser

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-agent reinforcement learning approach for shape/pattern formation control to cooperatively transport arbitrarily-shaped objects with non-uniform mass distribution. It addresses formations that securely support real-world objects atop multi-robot systems.

entry.title: PTL-Diffusion: Manifold-Aware Diffusion with Periodic Terminal Laws

author.name: Danqi Zhuang, Jisui Huang, Xiaoyue Xi, Andrew Kiggins, Xiaojie Wang, Ke Chen, Yue Wu

entry.summary: Proposes PTL-Diffusion, a proof-of-concept diffusion framework whose forward process converges to a nonconstant periodic family of Gaussian terminal laws rather than a single invariant distribution. It aims to inject manifold structure for data concentrated near low-dimensional manifolds.

entry.title: Vessel Traffic Flow Prediction on Sparse Data via Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks with a Learnable Tweedie Head

author.name: Kyeongjun Lee, Heeyoung Kim

entry.summary: Proposes a model-agnostic learnable Tweedie output head for spatio-temporal GNNs to handle sparse, intermittent maritime traffic data with excess zeros and bursts. It improves over conventional ST-GNNs and zero-inflated models for vessel flow prediction.

entry.title: Conditional Random Ordered Transport Spaces

author.name: Lei Luo, Jian Yang

entry.summary: Introduces conditional random ordered transport spaces (CROTS), L0-valued spaces of random measures with a Wasserstein metric and stochastic order to certify whether mass moves in admissible directions. It targets evidence-constrained, causal, and risk-sensitive learning.

entry.title: Loss-Guided Adaptive Scale Refinement for Molecular Force Prediction

author.name: Limin Yu

entry.summary: Introduces a loss-guided adaptive scale refinement framework for molecular force prediction that treats predefined spatial scales as initial anchors and discovers task-optimal resolutions through interpolation and differentiable scale updates. Tested on a NaCl aqueous system. Niche molecular ML contribution.

entry.title: Quantifying Uncertainty in Space Debris Capture with Active Tether-Net Systems Caused by Noisy Observations

author.name: Feng Liu, Achira Boonrath, Eleonora M. Botta, Souma Chowdhury

entry.summary: Presents a pipeline to propagate and quantify uncertainty from noisy debris-state observations in active tether-net space debris capture systems, where decisions depend on robust net maneuver and closing choices. Applied uncertainty quantification for aerospace robotics. Niche but practically motivated.

entry.title: Non-Archimedean Polydisc Spaces and Applications to Optimisation

author.name: Paul Lezeau, Yiannis Fam, Anthea Monod, Yue Ren

entry.summary: Introduces non-Archimedean polydisc spaces inspired by Berkovich geometry as a new framework for optimization over hierarchical data, showing metric trees embed naturally and establishing geodesic properties. Proposes optimization-compatible functions for these spaces.

entry.title: QnRL: Quantum-Native Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Alexander DeRieux, Walid Saad

entry.summary: Proposes Quantum-Native Reinforcement Learning, a distributional RL framework that directly models environment random variables as quantum state distributions rather than estimating expected outcomes. Aims to exploit the distributional nature of quantum computers for greater expressive power in stochastic environments.

entry.title: Ishigaki-IDS: An Open-Weight Verifier-Aware Model for Information Delivery Specification Drafting in Building Information Modeling

author.name: Ryo Kanazawa, Koyo Hidaka, Teppei Miyamoto, Takayuki Kato, Tomoki Ando, Chenguang Wang, Dayuan Jiang, Naofumi Fujita, Shuhei Saitoh, Atomu Kondo, Koki Arakawa, Daiho Nishioka

entry.summary: Presents Ishigaki-IDS, an open-weight LLM specialized for verifier-aware Information Delivery Specification drafting in Building Information Modeling, combining continued pretraining, SFT, and RL with verifiable rewards. Addresses a practical BIM authoring bottleneck with schema-conformant generation.

entry.title: Detection and Interpretability Analysis of Quotation Errors by Large Language Models

author.name: Bei Huang, Yingyi Zhang, Shenghao Huang, Chengzhi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes an LLM-based task of automated detection of quotation errors, the inconsistency between cited information and original sources, with interpretability analysis. Addresses a prevalent and labor-intensive problem in academic integrity.

entry.title: HydraQE: OSU's Submission for the IWSLT 2026 Speech Translation Metrics Shared Task

author.name: Kevin Krahn, Eric Fosler-Lussier

entry.summary: Presents HydraQE, a reference-free speech-translation quality estimation system for IWSLT 2026 built on a Qwen3-ASR backbone with sparsemax layer mixing and three prediction heads trained on human and pseudo-label supervision. Addresses scarcity of human-annotated QE data.

entry.title: Toward Signing Activity Projection in Sign Language Interaction

author.name: Takao Obi, Wang Yusong, Koji Inoue, Kotaro Funakoshi

entry.summary: Presents an initial transfer study adapting Voice Activity Projection architectures to predictive turn-taking in dyadic sign language interaction, deriving signing activity streams from the Public DGS Corpus. It targets accessibility for signing users with social robots.

entry.title: Automated IEP Generation from Traditional Chinese Parent-Teacher Interviews via Corpus-Grounded Feature Diffusion

author.name: Kuanlin Chen, Cheng-En Ou

entry.summary: Proposes a low-resource fine-tuning pipeline using Corpus-Grounded Feature Diffusion to automatically generate Individualized Education Programs from Traditional Chinese parent-teacher interviews. It addresses domain data scarcity and privacy constraints in an unexplored language setting.

entry.title: DroneDAR: Long-Range Drone Distance Estimation Using Monocular Vision and Bounding-Box Features

author.name: Knut Peterson, Zaid Mayers, David Han

entry.summary: DroneDAR estimates long-range drone distance from monocular image crops combined with bounding-box geometry, using a convolutional backbone with a lightweight gating mechanism to integrate box-derived features. It addresses extreme target scale variation and background clutter.

entry.title: Local Search on Vertex Coloring for Bipartite Graphs

author.name: Johanna Gasse

entry.summary: This thesis analyzes local search landscapes for vertex coloring on differently structured bipartite graphs, identifying structures that guarantee only global optima versus those enabling arbitrarily bad non-global local optima. It characterizes when local search can succeed.

entry.title: DynaOD: Dynamic Origin-Destination Flow Generation with Discrete-to-Continuous Temporal Semantic Modeling

author.name: Jie Zhao, Xianqi Dai, Jie Feng, Huandong Wang, Yong Li

entry.summary: DynaOD generates dynamic origin-destination mobility flows from temporal context alone, modeling discrete directional trends and continuous temporal evolution to produce coherent OD patterns while preserving spatial heterogeneity. It does not rely on historical OD observations.

entry.title: Bidirectional Semantic Complementary Tool Retrieval for Remote Sensing Agents

author.name: Zeyuan Wang, Dongyang Hou, Cheng Yang, Xuezhi Cui, Linrui Xu, Bo Yu, Gaozhi Zhou, Ziyu Li, Liangtian Liu, Kai Ouyang, Wang Guo, Lili Zhu, Chao Tao

entry.summary: Proposes a bidirectional semantic complementary tool retrieval method for remote sensing LLM agents, addressing the semantic asymmetry between high-level queries and fine-grained tool documentation. Improves precise tool selection within context-window limits.

entry.title: An AI Security Agent for University ACMIS: Multi-Vector Threat Detection and Automated Response

author.name: Joseph Walusimbi, Joshua Benjamin Ssentongo

entry.summary: This paper presents an AI security agent for University Academic Management Information Systems combining supervised anomaly detection, behavioral analytics, and an NLP chatbot for secure password recovery. It monitors five operational layers to detect threats indistinguishable from normal operations.

entry.title: Deep Active Re-Labeling: Toward Noise-Resilient Annotation Efficiency

author.name: Md Abdullah Al Forhad, Weishi Shi

entry.summary: Deep Active Re-Labeling addresses the impact of human annotation errors in deep active learning by allocating part of the annotation budget to re-labeling, informed by human learning patterns. Aims for noise-resilient annotation efficiency.

entry.title: OnlyDense: Reduced-Order Modeling for Lagrangian simulation

author.name: Tu Do, Shannon Ryan, Santu Rana

entry.summary: OnlyDense proposes a learning framework for scalable reduced-order modeling of massive particle systems in Lagrangian simulations like SPH and MPM, avoiding the cost of graph-based per-particle methods. Targets expensive multi-scale physics simulations.

entry.title: Self-Paced Curriculum Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Superbike Racing in Simulation

author.name: Luca Ghisi, Jacopo Essenziale, Carlo D'Eramo, Matteo Luperto

entry.summary: Presents a self-paced curriculum reinforcement learning framework using Soft Actor-Critic to train autonomous superbike racing agents in a physics-accurate simulator, automatically generating progressively harder tasks. Tackles the added complexity of balance and lean-angle control in motorbikes.

entry.title: TriHead-GAN: A Generative Adversarial Network with Triple-Head Discriminator for Carbon Emission Time Series Generation

author.name: Zesen Wang, Lijuan Lan, Yonggang Li, Chunhua Yang

entry.summary: Proposes TriHead-GAN, a GAN with a triple-head discriminator for generating scarce city-level carbon emission time series, providing explicit supervision for cross-variable correlations and first-difference statistics. It addresses limitations of existing generators that match marginals but collapse domain structure.

entry.title: Measuring Poverty and Inequality with Reduced Data: A Machine Learning Approach Using Nigerian Household Data

author.name: Vanesa Jord\'a, Miguel Ni\~no-Zaraz\'ua
